## Flinch polish: the enforcer, stairs, AD's humanoids, real weapons (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flinch2`, 2026-10-18)

- **Enforcer shuffle: fixed.**
  - Why: its stand frame leans over its rifle. Its centre of mass sits about 3.7 units ahead of its ankles, and its
    short legs (about 0.59 m) shrank its feet's support to 4.5 units, where a grunt's is 5.8. So the recovery test and
    the capture-step gate kept finding it off its support, and it shuffled 8-9 steps until the 2 s settle.
  - Now:
    - `beginFlinch` reckons the stance frame's own centre of mass from its feet's middle (`Stagger::supportOffset`,
      model space turned as it stands). The support, the lean and the capture-step gate all measure round it.
    - Foot Support scales only up with leg length (`clamp(leg / 0.75, 1, 2)`).
    - A flinch may take 4 more corrective steps once its backpedal's are spent.
  - The enforcer now recovers in 0.32-0.52 s (1-2 steps) from a shotgun, a super shotgun or a blow, as the grunt does.
- **Hand-back:**
  - Pain frames are no longer candidates (an enforcer had been handed back in `painc4`).
  - The arms' wheeling fades out after 0.12-0.32 s, so they are back by the hand-back.
  - Gaps (mean vertex distance; the vertical part in brackets):

    | case | gap |
    |---|---|
    | shotgun, flat floor | 0.3-0.4 units |
    | blow, flat floor | 2.6-3.2 units |
    | slope | 3.3 units (-3.2) for a shot, 5.3-6.3 for a blow |
    | stairs | 15.9-16.1 units (-15.7 to -15.9) |

  - The stairs gap is nearly all vertical. On these 16x16 stairs any monster box rests on the stair above (its 32-unit
    box always spans two), while the body stands with a foot on the stair below. No stand spot at the body's own height
    exists within 24 units; the hand-back now tries both the plain spot and the lifted one and keeps the smaller gap.
    It is the same 16 units every walking monster's model floats at there.
  - So the blend now also scales by the vertical gap, up to 2x (0.44 s): the root rises into the box over the blend
    instead of popping.
- **AD's humanoids:**
  - Shots, nails and blasts never reached the flinch for AD's monsters: they take damage in AD's own `ad_T_Damage`.
    `VR_AD_Hit` (vr_ad_bridge.qc) now calls `VR_Flinch_Hit`, then `VR_AD_KdSave`, so AD's pain gives way to the
    flinch as it does to a knockdown. Blows and throws already came through `VR_HitStagger_*`.
  - Tested in AD's start map (dispenser numbers):

    | choice | monster | flinches and recovers |
    |---|---|---|
    | 200 | death knight | yes |
    | 205 | guard | yes |
    | 211, 223, 227 | AD's soldiers (rocket, grenade, plasma) | yes |
    | 212, 217 | AD's enforcer variants | yes |
    | 216 | fury | yes |
    | 225 | sergeant | yes |
    | 232 | pyro | yes |
    | 235 | fumigator | yes |

  - Every class recovers in 0.32-0.62 s; the point-blank super shotgun knocks them over, as designed. One 212 blow
    settled at 2.0 s.
  - The crossbow knight (202) cannot ragdoll at all (`canRagdoll` 0): it keeps the old reactions.
- **Firm ground on AD maps:** the recovery test's ground check falls back to Quake's own trace (`Context::traceHit`).
  Neither the physics world's ray nor its floor saw AD's start map floor, and a still soldier toppled on "ground".
- **Real weapons through the mock** (impulse 154/155/156, the hand aimed level, `+attack`, at a grunt with 300 health):

  | weapon | distance | pellets hit | impulse | expected | change of speed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | shotgun | 64 | 6 | 42 N s | 6 x 7 | 0.52 m/s |
  | shotgun | 192 | 6 | 40 N s | x0.95 falloff | |
  | shotgun | 512 | 4 | 19 N s | 4 x 7 x 0.68 | under the threshold |
  | super shotgun | 64 | 9 of 14 (the spread) | 108 N s | | 1.35 m/s |
  | super shotgun | 192 | 6 | 69 N s | 6 x 12 x 0.96 | |
  | super shotgun | 512 | 9 | 74 N s | 9 x 12 x 0.68 | |

  - Nailgun: 20 N s a nail (Quake VR's nails deal more than Quake's 9). One nail is under the threshold; two in quick
    succession sum to 31 N s, 0.39 m/s, and it flinches.
  - Melee, his recorded takes replayed where you stand: an overhead punch to the head, 26 damage, 79 N s (= 3 x
    damage; only 0.34 m/s of it level, since it comes down from above); a two-handed stab, 23.6 damage, 71 N s,
    0.74 m/s. The hook punch take missed at 32 and 48 units.
  - Every impulse matches the design's formula and falloff.
- **Still rough:** a blow landing soon after a knockdown and get-up (the monster's pose odd: an attack frame, a wide
  stance) still sometimes shuffles 8-11 steps and topples at 2.0-2.3 s, about 1 run in 2 of the shotgun, super
  shotgun, blow sequence, for the grunt and the enforcer alike. Fresh hits do not.
- `vr_flinch_debug 3` also prints every hit that reaches the flinch and why a class cannot flinch.
  `vr_flinch_test_health` gives the test grunt more health, for the real weapons test.

Arcane Dimensions' melee monsters drop their weapons as Quake VR's knights drop their swords (QC `vr_ad_melee.qc`,
from `VR_AD_Dying`; `vr_admelee_drops`): the death fury its two swords (one per hand: dual-wield), the death knight, the
zombie knight and the death guard their swords, the hunter ogres their hammer and mace. AD's gibs throw no second one
(`ad_gib1mdl`/`ad_gib2mdl` cleared). Each is the knight's sword, `WID_SWORD`, with a kind in its weapon flags (bits 8-10,
`QVR_WPNFLAG_SWORD_KIND`, `vr_ad_guns_defs.qc`): no new weapon id, item bit or ammo; it holsters, throws and parries as
the knight's sword. Those bits are the grapple's hook tag's, so `DecodeLevelParms` now strips the tag from a grapple
only (`VR_Grapple_StripTagOf`): a sword keeps its kind across a level change.

  damage `vr_admelee_heavy_damage` (1.6x the knight's sword) in two hands, `vr_admelee_heavy_1h` (0.5) of it in one.

## Flinch: the odd-pose shuffle (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flinch3`, 2026-10-18)

The shotgun, super shotgun, blow sequence (fl_classes.sh's, `vr_knockdown_time_* 0.5`) in vrtesthall, 12 runs a class.
`vr_flinch_debug 3` now also prints the frame it was struck in and its stance (feet apart, its middle off them).

- **Why:** not the get-up itself. Three things, all about the pose it was struck in:
  - **Its steps kept the struck stance.** `beginStagger` took each foot's place round its middle from the pose as
    struck. Struck in an attack frame, the grunt's middle stood 9 units off its feet the wrong way (its stand frame:
    2.4), so after every step it was as far off its support: 11 steps, toppled at 2.31 s. A flinch's stance now comes
    from its stand frame (`beginFlinch`).
  - **A blow's body was made in its pain frame.** A blow reaches the flinch after its damage, its pain's first frame
    already set. The enforcer's `paind1` bends its chest 35 degrees over, and it stayed so (`painc1`: 20 degrees, 1.0 s).
    T_Damage now keeps the frame it had (`vr_fl_prepain`), and a blow's or a throw's flinch is made in it.
  - **A bent torso stayed bent.** With a still clip a joint's motor holds any bend up to twice its weight's torque; the
    spring alone could not pull an attack frame's aim (23-29 degrees) back, so the enforcer failed the tilt test and
    stood until the 2 s settle. A flinch's torso and head motors now turn towards the stand frame as their tone comes
    back (4/s of the way, at most 3 rad/s).
- **Numbers** (recovered at, steps; the third hit unless said):

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | grunt | 8 of 12 at 0.32 s (0-1 steps); 4 toppled at 2.31 s after 11 steps | 12 of 12 at 0.32-0.38 s, 0-1 steps |
  | enforcer | 4 at 0.32 s; 6 at 0.95-1.40 s (3-6 steps); 2 toppled at 2.0 s | 8 at 0.32-0.45 s; 3 at 0.83-0.87 s (1-2 steps); 1 at 1.25 s (4) |
  | enforcer, 2nd hit (super shotgun) | 3 of 12 at 2.0-2.1 s (2-9 steps) | all 0.45-0.76 s, 0-2 steps |
  | enforcer, a blow alone | painc1 1.0 s (4 steps), paind1 toppled at 2.0 s | 0.32 s (6 of 6) |

- Fresh hits are unchanged (0.32-0.38 s, 0-1 steps). `vr_flinch 0` takes none of these paths (the new QC field is only
  read by the flinch).
- eval.sh --full with `vr_flinch 0`: 168/177 (the same 5 known diffs).

## AD rigs: no ragdoll after the weapon drops (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/hunterrag`, 2026-10-18)

The hammer's and the mace's hunter ogres had no ragdoll (`ragdoll: progs/mon_hogreham.mdl: bone hand_r got 0
vertices: no ragdoll`, with any `vr_admelee_drops`). Cause: "AD melee monsters drop their weapons" made their weapons
loose pieces (vr_monstermods.cpp collapses them in the death frames at load, whatever the cvar), and their seed tables
were measured with the weapon in the hand: `hand_r`'s middle sat in the hammer, so with the hammer left out no motion
cluster was nearest it (the fist's cluster went to the forearm). The same in the sweep of every AD monster model
(`vr_ragdoll_info progs/mon_*.mdl` with `-game ad`): the death guard's and the crossbow knight's `hand_r`, the death
fury's `forearm_l`, the death knight's and AD's hell knight's `forearm_r` (their sword hands), and the ice golem's
`pelvis`.

- vr_ragdoll.cpp `adoptPastPivot`: a bone no cluster went to takes its parent's vertices past its pivot (on the side
  away from the parent's pivot), then refine moves the boundary by the motions; only when both keep 3 or more (else no
  ragdoll, as before). Only bones that failed before change: the working rigs are the same. Hand bones now: hammer and
  mace ogres 33 vertices, death guard 32; the fury's left forearm 34, the death knight's right 32, the hell knight's 12.
- The crossbow knight: its fist is not its forearm's (the left hand's and the chest's clusters hold it), so its
  `hand_r` middle moved from the bow to the fist (3.5 -7.5 -2.5): 22 vertices.
- The ice golem is the golem's mesh x1.5, 12.3 units up (least squares over four frames, within 1.2 units): its own
  seeds, the golem's so scaled (`adIcegolemSeeds`).
- vr_dents.cpp: the crossbow knight's, the two hunter ogres' and the death guard's `hand_r` are flesh now (the fist;
  the weapons are loose, found by themselves).

Still no ragdoll (no seed table, not the 0-vertex failure): AD's own ogre (`mon_ogre.mdl`, the nail ogre), fishing ogre,
knight, death lord, Quoth death guard, boil, deflector, floyd, jim, lost soul, sentinel, wraith.

Tests: the sweep (every AD model above rigs, the rig cache off); `vr_test_spawn 208/213; impulse 241; vr_test_kill 1` in
ad_dm1: both ragdolls (12 parts, lying, `vr_corpse_poses`), the dropped hammer beside them.

## Flinch: balance from the legs, `vr_flinch 2` (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flinch4`, 2026-10-18)

His VR notes on `vr_flinch 1`: a shotgun to the chest froze it with its feet glued while its body wobbled back; a
medium blow wobbled its whole ragdoll on stuck legs; an uppercut floated it, then sprang it back. He wants Euphoria-style
balance from the legs: a bend at the hit, then steps (backpedal, sidestep) driven by the centre of mass against the
feet, and no global spring. Design and causes: FLINCH.md, "Balance from the legs".

- **Causes:** the pelvis pin (an anchor on the stand pose's pelvis, height included, up to 2 weights at 5 Hz, carried a
  fixed short way: 2 units for a shotgun, 5 for a blow), the lift of 0.6-0.95 g on every part, and `turnWhole`. With
  the pin carrying it, the capture point never left the feet: no step, ever (0 steps in every case below).
- **`vr_flinch 2`:** no pin, no lift; weight borne only through feet on the floor (a push, never a pull); centre of
  pressure kept within the feet's soles; capture-point steps with the swing foot carried to its spot; momentum-keeping
  upright. `vr_flinch 1` and `0` are unchanged (every new path is gated on `Stagger::legs`). `vr_flinch` stays 1:
  the stairs are not good enough yet (below). New settings: `vr_flinch_legs_push` 2.5, `vr_flinch_legs_upright` 1.
- **Measured** (headless, vrtesthall, a grunt hit along +y, 8 runs a case, spot and stand phase jittered;
  `scratch/fl4_suite.py`, not committed). Recovered/8, mean steps, their mean cosine along the hit, the most rise of
  the centre of mass (units), recovery time (s):

  | case | `vr_flinch 1` | `vr_flinch 2` |
  |---|---|---|
  | flat, shotgun 64 / 192 units | 8, 0 steps, rise 0.7, 0.32 s | 8, 1 step (1.00 along, 15 units), rise 0.4, 0.37 s |
  | flat, 30-damage blow | 8, 0 steps, 0.32 s | 8, 1 step (1.00, 21 units), 0.50 s |
  | flat, uppercut (35, to the chin) | 8, 0 steps, rise 0.9, 0.32 s | 8, 1 step (1.00), rise 4.8 (falls back), 0.39 s |
  | slope, shotgun | 8, 0 steps, 0.32 s | 8, 0 steps, 0.32 s |
  | slope, blow / uppercut | 8, 0 steps | 8, 1 step (1.00), 0.43 / 0.49 s |
  | stairs, shotgun | 8, 0 steps, 0.32 s | **0**: 4 steps against the hit (-0.1), falls |
  | stairs, blow / uppercut | 8 / 8 | **2 / 0** (2 steps, 0.8 along), falls |

- **Rough:** the stairs (its steps there wander and it falls from a shotgun); one step where he wants "a few" (a
  longer backpedal needs a shorter stride, which then fell behind its capture point and toppled after 5-9 steps);
  only the grunt was measured (the other classes, AD's, the enforcer's odd poses: not yet).
- **Frame strips** (side view, a shot every 7 frames): `scratch/fl4_strip_<case>_<terrain>[_old].png`.

## Flamethrowers light the room (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/flamelight`, 2026-10-18)

Before: no light at all from a flamethrower's stream (the player's AD pyro gun, the pyro monsters): AD's flame sprites
(`progs/s_burst_flame.spr`) and our fire particles, nothing lit. Now (vr_emissive.cpp, `VR_FlameLights`, called after
`VR_TorchLights` in CL_ReadFromServer): each frame `VR_ProjectileLight` gathers the flame sprites drawn (a young flame
weighs more), they are clustered (a flame joins the nearest cluster within 72 units; clusters within 288 merged, nearest
first, down to the cap; more still: the heaviest and nearest kept), and each cluster is one light at its weighted
centre (put back in the open along a trace from its first flame), as bright as its flames' weight (four fresh flames a
full light), as wide as they are spread (160 + 1.2 x spread, at most 320). The lights are slots kept from frame to frame:
a cluster takes the nearest light within 160 units, which follows it smoothly; a light swells in within a tenth of a
second and dies down in about a third when its stream stops; a fast torch-like flicker. Unshadowed (no shadow tiles),
coloured, through `setGlow` (both falloffs, so Quake's lighting look too); models are lit as by any dynamic light. The
fumigator's poison and the smoke under water make no light.

Settings: `vr_flame_lights` (3; how many lights for all the streams together, 0 off; the lighting presets: Low 1,
Medium and up 3), `vr_flame_light_scale` (1, their reach); Light Sources rows "Flamethrower Lights" and "Flamethrower
Light Size"; Debug: "Flame Lights Info" (`vr_flame_lights_info`: flames, clusters, each light's place, level, reach).

Cost (`--exclusive -RealTime`, `vr_profile_report`, a pyro monster streaming at a wall, 7 flames in the air): CPU no
change measurable (the client's other time 0.027-0.029 ms either way); GPU world 0.404 -> 0.421 ms with the stream's 2
lights. The naive way (a light a flame; a test build with no clustering): 8 lights, GPU world 0.365 -> 0.389 ms, and 8
of the 64 dynamic light slots per stream (three pyros: 24) against 2-3 for all the streams here. Scripts (scratch):
`flamelight.sh` (the player's gun, on/off screenshots), `flamemon.sh` (a pyro monster), `flameprof.sh`,
`flamemonprof.sh`; screenshots `fl1.png`, `fm2.png`.

### For VR

The player's pyro gun in a dark corridor and a pyro monster's stream: the light's brightness and colour (too strong?
`vr_flame_light_scale`), whether it pops or lags when sweeping the stream, and the light on your own hands and gun.

## Flinch: `vr_flinch 2` on stairs, more steps (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flinch5`, 2026-10-18): not landed

The goal was making `vr_flinch 2` good enough to be the default. It is not: `vr_flinch` stays 1 and `vr_flinch 2` is
unchanged from `agent/flinch4`. The attempt is kept in the branch's history (commit "Flinch WIP ...", reverted in the
next one) for whoever picks it up.

- **Why the stairs fail** (measured with `vr_flinch_debug 4` and a floor probe; vrtesthall's stairs are 16 units high
  and 16 deep, 45 degrees; a grunt's legs are 17.7 and 21.7 units, 31.5 units a metre):
  - A grunt put on them stands with its box on the step above and its feet hanging: one 4.5 units over its step, the
    other 20 units over the step below (its stance, 15 units, is wider than a step). `vr_flinch 1`'s pin hides this;
    with no pin it starts unsupported, falls onto one foot and off the step's edge.
  - `floorAt` traced from 0.3 m above a foot: it missed a floor 20 units down (the far foot read as standing on air,
    its fallback) and starts inside the step above for a foot next to a riser (no hit). A trace from the pelvis's
    height down is right (`floorUnder` in the WIP).
  - A step's way (a straight line with an arc of 0.12 leg) goes through a riser when it steps up; the foot's carry
    then pushes the body sideways at up to 7 m/s through the contact.
- **What the WIP tried:** a common rest gap and hanging feet put down where they can reach (a settle step); feet held
  on their spot by a friction-like grip; landing spots traced from the pelvis, moved off stair edges and kept within
  0.45 leg up / 0.6 leg down of the other foot (so both share a step); a swing that lifts clear of the step first;
  the floor's level push scaled by the legs' push and capped at 0.8 g (grip); capture steps cut to max(0.45 leg,
  0.72 x the full step) so a stronger hit takes 2-4 steps, re-planned over the first 60% of a step; closing steps
  for split stances; the leading foot first for side hits.
- **Result:** worse everywhere. Flat recovery fell from 8/8 to 0-2/8 with ~11 steps (stepping in place, the centre of
  mass rising up to 15 units); stairs 0-2/8 (was 0-2/8). Switching each new part off in turn (a temporary bitmask)
  did not bring flat back, so the regression is in the unswitchable parts (the bearing rules, the rest gap, the
  landing height, the settle step or the swing path); not found within the round's budget.
- **Kept:** `vr_flinch_test_class` (0 grunt, 1 enforcer, 2 knight, 3 death knight, 4 ogre, 5 zombie) for
  `vr_flinch_test 20` and `21`, with a Debug > Tests > Flinch row "Test Monster". Checked: an enforcer from it
  flinches and recovers (`vr_flinch 1`, a shotgun, 0.38 s).
- **Next:** start from `agent/flinch4`'s code and take one change at a time with the 8-run suite after each
  (`scratch/fl5_suite.py`, `FL5_CLASS`, `FL5_ONLY`): first `floorUnder` alone, then the swing path, then the settle step
  for hanging feet; the stairs test may also want a gentler flight (a 45-degree, 16-deep stair asks a grunt to stand
  across two steps 80% of its leg apart).

## Flinch: `vr_flinch 2`, one change at a time (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flinch6`, 2026-10-18)

The method flinch5 asked for: a fast suite first (`scratch/fl6_suite.py <label> <mode>`, `FL6_CLASS`, `FL6_ONLY`; 6 cases
x 8 runs, spot and stand phase jittered, ~40 s; `scratch/fl6_table.txt` has every summary), then one change at a time,
kept only if flat stays 8/8 and nothing regresses. `vr_flinch` stays 1: mode 2 is below mode 1 on the stairs (and for
the enforcer everywhere).

Grunt, recovered/8 (flat shotgun 64, flat blow, flat uppercut, slope blow, stairs shotgun, stairs blow):

| step | flat sg64 | flat blow | flat upper | slope blow | stairs sg64 | stairs blow | kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vr_flinch 1` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | |
| `vr_flinch 2` baseline | 8 (1 step) | 8 (1) | 8 (1) | 8 (1) | 0 (3.9, along -0.10) | 2 | |
| 1 `floorUnder` for the bearing feet | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 0 (2.5, +0.19) | 2 | no (knight stairs 6/8 -> 4/8) |
| 2 swing kept 0.08 leg over the floor | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 0 (4.0) | 2 | yes |
| 3 hanging foot put down first (6 variants) | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 0-1 | 0 | no |
| 4 first steps cut short, re-planned (4 variants) | 8 | 0-2 | 0-8 | 2-8 | 0 | 1-6 | no |

- **Step 1:** right for the grunt, but the knight on stairs fell more: the old trace (from 0.3 m over the foot) missed
  the floor under a hanging foot and fell back to "standing", so the hanging foot bore and held it up. Undone for the
  bearing feet; `floorUnder` stays for step 2.
- **Step 3, why the stairs fail** (`vr_flinch_debug 4` and `swing:` lines, now gone): on vrtesthall's stairs the hit
  (+y) runs across them; the grunt's feet are side by side along the rise (x), one on its step, the other 20 units
  over the step below. Its legs (about 20 units, its pelvis 20 over its feet) cannot reach 15.5 units lower, so a
  straight-down settle never bears. Moved onto the same step (8 units in) it bears, and with the settling foot held as
  an edge meanwhile the capture point stays within 2 units; but the next capture step then aims a stair or two down
  (33 units) out of reach, and the swing's carry, unable to follow, shoves the body up through the leg (the pelvis 3-5
  units over its stand height with the legs' push at 0) and it falls off its foot. Sinking the pelvis for a step down
  (at once: it free-falls; over the step: no better) and reachable landing spots did not bring a stairs run back.
  Kept in history: "Flinch WIP (not kept): hanging feet ..." and its revert.
- **Step 4:** a step cut short lands short of the capture point; once a second step is needed it runs away (7-8 steps,
  200 units, falls) on flat, even with only the first step cut and the rest full and re-planned. Bimodal: a run takes
  1 step and recovers or runs away. On the stairs it helped (blow 2 -> 6 with every step cut to 0.6). Easing the carry
  off a stuck foot (off its way by 0.2 leg) broke flat blows (0/8): a fast step's foot lags that much. Kept in history
  as "Flinch WIP (not kept): first capture steps ..." and its revert.
- **Step 5** (sidesteps): not started (budget).
- **Other classes** (final code, recovered/8 in the six cases, `vr_flinch 2` / `vr_flinch 1`):
  - enforcer: 0 0 8 0 0 0 / 8 8 8 8 8 6. Mode 2 was already so before this round (0/8 flat shotgun, its steps against
    the hit, along -0.54): its lean over its rifle (`supportOffset`) wants a look first.
  - knight: 8 8 8 8 6 6 / 8 8 8 8 8 8 (with step 1: stairs 4 4).
  - ogre: a shotgun 64 and an uppercut do not flinch it (both modes); blows 8 8, stairs blow 0 (+2 none) / 6.
- **Melee:** `eval.sh --full` with `vr_flinch 0`: 168/177 (unchanged).
- **Next:** the second step's runaway on flat (why a step landing short of a running capture point never catches it)
  before more steps; the enforcer's mode 2; on stairs, a test hit along the rise as well as across it.

### VR Calibration: height step dropped when standing (calibstep)

The intro ("Stand up straight and look ahead, hold still") and Body Calibration step 1 (Stand Tall) both measured the eye height standing. Standing now goes intro -> Body Calibration straight (no separate HEIGHT step); Stand Tall says "Hold still." too and judges its pose at the height held. Seated keeps the HEIGHT step (Body Calibration has no Stand Tall then). The data is unchanged: Stand Tall's capture and vr_height_calibration on Apply are the same code; a body result that is not applied no longer leaves the intro's height behind.

Axe size onto slot 0, so the plain axe grew too).

  (`QVR_WEAPON_UNINHERITED` lines in vr_weapons.inc, generated from `vr_wofs_dump` of the effective values: 48 per AD
  gun, 36 / 35 / 52 for the upgrades). The QVR_WEAPON_OWN marks of 34-35 went with it. Slot 0 (axe) back to its values

## Wet from liquids: fixed, and an even wet coat (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/wetcoat`, 2026-10-18)

- **Regression:** since the glove shells (cf2ee0477, "Glove depth"), `progs/hand_rig.mdl` and `progs/vrbody_bare.mdl`
  load with extra surfaces (the shells after the first), and the wound masks' `regionOf` refused any model with a second
  surface: your hands and body got no mask, so no wetness, no drips, and no painted blood or burns on you either (the
  liquid events still came: `vr_wounds_debug 1`). `regionOf` now takes a model whose extra surfaces are glove shells
  (`handrig::gloveShellSurfaces`; they share the skin's layout at u + 2 and read the first surface's mask).
- **New look:** no dither for wetness. Where a mask is wet at all (b > ~0.01), an even coat: the look 30% darker (lit
  texels, not fullbrights), the bumps filled 35%, a glossy film in the model's own light (tight highlight, a broad one,
  a little Fresnel; no dynamic light). Its strength is per model (`vr_wounds_wet_coat`, 1, Gore > Wounds on Models >
  Wet Sheen, 0..2) times smoothstep(0, 0.75, the drying left): full for the first ~7 s, gone at 28 s. Monsters get it
  too. A weapon (or a carried prop) in a hand whose wrist went under the surface takes it all over; the hands drip only
  when they went under. Instance data: `GloveShell.zw` (`VR_AliasWetCoat`). `vr_wounds_info` prints a `wet:` line.
- **Checks:** `scratch/wet_test.sh` (vrfiringrange: spawn, the pool at 612 474 -180, back): before the fix 0 masks,
  after it 3 (hands, body), coat 1.0 just out, 0.51 at ~17 s, weapon (crowbar, main hand) the same. Off hand's back,
  mean RGB 254 214 157 dry, 242 177 134 just out, 254 204 153 half dry (overexposed spot). GPU (`--exclusive`,
  4 s each, wet, hands + crowbar + body in view): models 0.178 / 0.174 / 0.174 ms coat on / off / on: no measurable cost.
- **For VR:** swim, climb out: hands, forearms, gloves and the weapon darker and glossy, evenly, drips from the hands,
  fading over ~25 s; wade knee-deep: only the legs/body below the line, hands dry and not dripping. Wet Sheen slider.

## Swing sounds by speed (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/swoosh`, 2026-10-18)

- **Before:** a fist's, slap's or melee weapon's whoosh played only as a blow landed (`VR_Melee_Whoosh`), always at 1.
- **Now** (`vr_melee_swish` 1; QC `vr_melee.qc` "Swing sounds by speed"): every motion of a fist, open hand or melee
  weapon is measured as a share of the speed its blow would land at (`VR_Melee_LandNeed`, the hand's and blow's own;
  a weapon's far end counted at 1/3 of its speed, so a wrist-whipped blade counts). Under `vr_melee_swish_min` (0.5):
  silent. Up to 1: a soft swish (the same samples), at most `vr_melee_swish_sub` (0.45), smoothstep from the least
  share, up to 6% lower the softer, played at the motion's fastest (its four-pose mean slowed to 90% of its peak). A
  blow: as before, as it lands, at 1 up to `vr_melee_swish_gain` (1.6) at `vr_melee_swish_full` (2.2) times its landing
  speed (this pose's or the last's share), up to 6% higher. Per hand: once a motion (re-armed once the part slows under
  0.35 of its landing speed), soft ones 0.2 s apart at least; none under water or while pushing (bash, shove). Guns keep
  the blow's whoosh only, at 1. Menu: Combat > Melee > Swing Sounds (5 rows).
- **Louder than full:** QC `sound()`'s volume may now go to 4: `SV_WriteSound` sends a volume over 255 as a short
  (`SND_LOUD`, protocol.h; clamped to 255 in NetQuake's protocol), the client's channel keeps `master_vol` over 255,
  and the 8-bit and band-limited mixers (and the spatial audio's shadow mix) skip their 255 cap for such a channel only
  (static sounds combined over 255 are still capped as before).
- **Checks:** 29 takes replayed (`developer 1` prints `melee swish:` lines): punches land at 1.37-1.48 of their
  landing speed (volume 1.13-1.21), the slap 1.79 (1.44), a backswing cut 2.13 (1.59), overhead cuts 1.88-2.35
  (1.49-1.6), a weak one 1.03 (1.0); the "no hit" waves and wiggles play soft swishes 0.07-0.45. Synthetic closed-fist punches (0.8 m,
  `vr_mock_play`): 1 and 2 m/s silent, 2.7 m/s a soft 0.06, 3.3-7.3 m/s blows at 1.06-1.6 (10 m/s 1.48: its first
  pose read low); `snd_show 2` L+R 29 (0.06), ~225 (0.45), ~503 (1.0), 532 (1.06), 610 (1.21), 707 (1.41), 800 (1.6):
  the engine plays them over full. `eval.sh --full` 168/177 (its 4 differences from
  the baseline are older: the bash damage default 10 -> 5, a stab replayed at 15.9 with `vr_melee_swish 0` too).
- **Mock caveat:** where the 90 Hz poses beat against the server's ticks, a steady motion reads double one pose in four
  (a soft swish was fired just before the blow by such a dip): soft swishes use the four-pose mean. The melee model
  itself lands mock punches on those spikes (a steady 0.77 of the landing speed landed a blow): not changed here.
- **For VR:** slow arm moves silent; a brisk wave or a wind-up a soft whoosh; a punch or cut a clear step louder; a
  very fast punch or full cut louder than before and a touch higher. Waving a sword or axe about now whooshes softly
  each stroke (0.2 s apart at most): if too busy, raise Heard From or lower Short of a Blow.

## Linux: the EGL binding, foreign-architecture manifests (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/lineegl`, 2026-10-19)

- **Report:** a CachyOS player (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, WiVRn 26.9, Quest 2; build 7258): "xrCreateSession not called: no
  GLX context current", then `openxr_wivrn.i686.json` tried and failed (-51). SDL had made an EGL context: Arch's
  `sdl2` is sdl2-compat on SDL3, which prefers Wayland on a Wayland desktop (EGL there); the game bound GLX only.
- **Now** (`vr_xr_linuxgl.cpp`, was `vr_xr_glx.cpp`): the session binds SDL's current context, GLX
  (`XrGraphicsBindingOpenGLXlibKHR`) or EGL (`XrGraphicsBindingEGLMNDX`, `XR_MNDX_egl_enable`, enabled when offered:
  Monado, WiVRn). libEGL is found in the process with `dlopen(RTLD_NOLOAD)`: no EGL headers or link. The step line
  names the binding, the SDL video driver and (EGL) the EGL version and vendor; a failed `xrCreateSession` names the
  binding; an EGL context with a runtime lacking the extension stops with a warning naming `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11
  SDL_VIDEO_X11_FORCE_EGL=0`. `contextReady` checks and restores either kind.
- **SteamVR** (no EGL binding): before SDL's video init (`VR_BeforeVideoInit`, `xrruntime::beforeVideoInit`; the
  config's `vr_xr_runtime*` and the `vr_xr_test*` command-line values read first), when the plan has SteamVR, `DISPLAY`
  is set and no SDL video/EGL variable is, SDL is asked for X11/GLX (SDL2's and SDL3's variable names).
- **Architectures:** a manifest named `<name>.<arch>.json` for another arch, or whose library's ELF class/machine isn't
  the game's, is left out of Auto ("for i686 (the game is x86_64): left out"); `active_runtime.<arch>.json` is read
  before `active_runtime.json`, as the loader does.
- **Checks (WSL Arch, llvmpipe, Monado simulated HMD):** GLX on Xvfb, EGL on Xvfb (`SDL_VIDEO_X11_FORCE_EGL=1`) and EGL
  on WSLg Wayland (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=wayland`) each reach FOCUSED and render (17-23 `xr` frame lines in 150 waits);
  `vr_xr_test` plans: SteamVR active -> SDL asked for X11, WiVRn active -> kept, `openxr_wivrn.i686.json` left out.
  Windows build and mock smoke unchanged. Not tested: NVIDIA's EGL, WiVRn itself, a runtime without the EGL extension.

**The flinch removed.** The author tried vr_flinch 2 ("On, Leg Balance") in VR and judged it worse (enemies seem to
freeze, no real steps, some melee hits sent ragdolls flying and gliding across the floor), then decided to remove the
physical flinch altogether, modes 1 and 2. What it was, what was tried and why it did not work:
`FLINCH_RETROSPECTIVE.md` (its test suites in `Misc/quakevr/flinch_archive/`).

  prop's `vr_fl_thrown`, the pre-pain frame), the `ragdollflinch` builtin, `box3d::ragdollFlinch`, `flinchStatus_f`
  (`vr_flinch_status`), the overlay; in `vr_ragactive.cpp/.hpp` and `vr_box3d_knockdown.cpp` everything the flinch
  added (those three files are back to their state before it, `d060895c5^`, with the two sweep commits made since
  re-applied: `34e4f0777`, `aa3fb263f`); `activeTraceHit` (its Context trace); the Combat > Flinch page and the Debug >
  Tests flinch rows; `FLINCH.md`.
- Kept: what other features use: `VR_HitReact_Where` (the small hit reaction's), the knockdown's dead-only room
  (`vr_kd_room_dead_only`, now the ragdoll triggers'), the AD rigs' active classes, vrtesthall's slope.

  unbalance by Hits Unbalance as before.

  next write leaves them out. No config version change (nothing to migrate: the settings are gone).

  grunt struck: 6.5 (old vr_flinch 1) and 7.6 units (vr_flinch 2) of drift over 180 frames, now about 10, then still:
  no glide in any. A standing grunt with Hits Unbalance forced (`vr_hit_stagger_chance 100`): it staggers back 127
  units over ~2.5 s upright (the shove's stagger at a two-hand shove's push, impact 1; code unchanged, and only this
  far at the forced chance). The flinch's own glide came from its pinned body under real hand blows, which the mock
  cannot reproduce; with it gone nothing further was changed.

**Ragdoll triggers** (QC `vr_kdtrig.qc`; Combat > Ragdoll Triggers; the author, 2026-10-19: situations in normal combat
that make a living humanoid an active ragdoll, besides the leg pull, the leg sweep, the lift and the shove).

- A table (`VR_KdTrig_Init`): each trigger a name, its switch, chance, least damage and push cvars and how it falls
  (pushed whole over an edge, `ragdollshovetopple`'s ledge mode, or toppled where it stands, carried `throw` units per
  push). `VR_KdTrig_Match` says whether it holds for the hit and its weight. To add one: a `VR_KdTrig_Def` line, a case
  in `VR_KdTrig_Match`, its cvars, a page in `vr_menu_gameplay.inc` and its row in `vr_menu.cpp`'s pages.
- Hooked in T_DamageDeal (after the damage, before the pain) and AD's VR_AD_Hit. In table order each trigger that
  holds rolls (its chance x its weight / the monster's resistance, at most 1); the first that wins knocks it down
  through the shove's knockdown (`VR_Knockdown_Start`), so it lies, can be held and gets up as any knockdown; its
  pain's frames then do not play (as for any knockdown).
- The triggers (defaults; least damage times the resistance; stronger hits up to 1.5 times the chance at twice it):
  1. Ledges (`vr_kdtrig_ledge` 0.7, least 12): a drop of `vr_kdtrig_ledge_drop` (48) or more behind it along the hit
     within `vr_kdtrig_look` (40) units past its hull, room for its hull to drop: pushed off.
  2. Stairs (0.5, least 15): two or more steps down (6+ units each) behind it, the first within 16 units past its
     hull, 24+ units down in all: pushed whole down them.
  3. Slopes (0.4, least 15): ground under it steeper than `vr_kdtrig_slope_angle` (18 deg), the hit within 60 deg of
     downslope: toppled down it.
  4. Shotgun range (0.35): your shotgun or super shotgun within `_range` (160), at least half of `_pellets` (8)
     landing; weight pellets / 8, times 1 - 0.5 x distance / range.
  5. Wounded (0.25, least 5): under `_health` (0.3) of its full health; weight 0.5 at it to 1 at none.
  6. Strong blows (0.25, least 30): your melee blow or flung prop; weight damage / least up to 2; a blade's edge
     (axes, swords, the chainsaw) times `_blade` (0.4); fists, a gun's butt, AD's hammer and mace, a pommel, the
     crowbar and props blunt.
  7. Explosions (0.6, least 15, push 1.25): radius damage that leaves it alive (ours, `QVR_HITKIND_SPLASH`, and AD's
     own, `VR_AD_Splash` round AD's VR_AD_Hit: an `ad_import.py` patch), within `_range` (200) of the blast's centre;
     weight damage / least up to 2, times 1 - 0.5 x distance / range; thrown away from the centre (48 units a push).
- Never: Ragdoll Triggers or Knockdowns off, a kind without an active stagger (`ragdollcanstagger`), one down,
  staggering, parried, flying or swimming, a boss (1000+ health), an anchored dummy; for `vr_kdtrig_cooldown` (4 s)
  after it gets up. Its ragdoll's room: a dead body may go, never a living knockdown.
- Monster resistance (Ragdoll Triggers > Monster Resistance): its kind's own (`vr_kdtrig_resist_army` 1, `_enforcer`
  1.15, `_knight` 1.15, `_hknight` 1.6, `_ogre` 2.5, `_zombie` 1; 0: by size), else its hull's volume over a grunt's
  to `vr_kdtrig_resist_size` (0.5). Every trigger's chance is divided by it and its least damage multiplied. The
  shove's, the leg sweep's, the leg pull's and the lift's own chances are unchanged (the shove's are per kind already:
  Knockdowns); the Ragdoll Triggers page links their pages.
- Menu: Combat > Ragdoll Triggers (on, cooldown), a page per trigger (on, chance, least damage, push, its own rows),
  Monster Resistance, links to Knockdowns (shove, ledge, leg sweep, Hits Unbalance) and Holding Enemies (lift, leg
  pull). Debug > Tests > Ragdoll Triggers: `vr_kdtrig_debug` (1: a `kdtrig:` line per knockdown, which and why; 2: also
  lost rolls), test hits on the nearest monster.
- Tests (`vr_kdtrig_test`: 1 shotgun, 2 super shotgun, 5 blunt blow, 6 blade blow, 7 blast, 20 a test monster at
  `_x _y _z`, 30 + k: `vr_kdtrig_test_n` trials of test k on a fresh one there; `_class`, `_health`, `_damage`,
  `_yaw`, `_dist`). Headless, vrtesthall, 20 trials each (fired of 20; the expected chance):

  | case | spot | fired | expected |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | stairs, blow 30 down the stairs | 9th step | 16-17 | 0.75 |
  | ledge, blow 30 off the platform | platform's south edge | 20 | 1.0 |
  | slope, blow 30 down the ramp | 22-deg ramp | 13-15 (+2 blow) | 0.6 |
  | shotgun 6 pellets at 64 units | flat | 1-5 | 0.21 |
  | super shotgun 14 pellets at 64 units | flat | 6-7 | 0.49 |
  | wounded (a fifth of its health), blow 20 | flat | 3-4 | 0.19 |
  | blunt blow 45 / blade blow 45 | flat | 11 / 2 | 0.38 / 0.15 |
  | blast 20 at 48 units | flat | 17 | ~0.75 |
  | blast 30: grunt / death knight / ogre | flat | 20 / 8 / 0 | 1 / 0.41 / 0 (least 37.5) |
  | negatives: blow 20 flat full health; super shotgun at 600; stairs hit up them; triggers off | | 0 each | 0 |

## Projectiles: one path; grenades on knocked-down bodies; the fury's curve; sword fix; no holster for the hammer and mace (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/projconsist`, 2026-10-19)

**Projectiles: one path.** Every projectile's touch now calls `VR_Proj_Begin(kind, damage)` before its hit and
`VR_Proj_End()` after it (QC weapons.qc, "Projectile hits"): the prop, gib or ragdoll it met (or flew through) pushed
(`VR_ShotPush`, a nail's push; explosives push by their blast), where it struck found along its flight
(`VR_TouchTrace`, `PositionalDamage`: the headshot crack, a corpse's head or limb worn, `VR_Limb_CorpseWear`), the hit
tagged a shot there, and a kill at the head or a limb armed to pop (`VR_Decap_ProjArm`, vr_limbs.qc: lasers and plasma
bolts `vr_decap_pop_laser`, any other bolt, nail or lump the new `vr_decap_pop_projectile` 0.85; explosives none of their
own, their blasts pop, `vr_limbs_blast`). Wall torches come off through the damage (T_Damage's `VR_WallTorch_Shot`; AD's
T_Damage hands ours to ours).

The real bug: AD's crossbow bolt (and AD's lasers, plasma and its player-sized small projectiles, MG3's alt laser and
seeker eye) are `MOVETYPE_FLY`: their move is `MOVE_NORMAL` without `MOVE_HITGIBS`, so it passed through corpses,
knocked-down bodies and gibs (`SOLID_NOT_BUT_TOUCHABLE`) and missed the wall torch's shot box (`VR_ShotTargetClip` only
meets shots and missiles). A projectile marked `.vr_projectile` (`VR_Proj_Mark`: AD's `ad_launch_projectile`,
`ad_launch_plasma`, `ad_Launch_Missile`, `ad_Launch_Grenade`, MG3's FLY ones, every grenade made by `VR_Grenade_Make`)
now moves as AD's pellets did (vr_hitmodel.cpp `VR_HitModelMoveFlags`: `MOVE_HITGIBS` + precise hits). Grenades: a
marked prop meeting a ragdoll (Box3D `Kind::Corpse`) now touches it (vr_box3d_step.cpp `touches`): a living, knocked-down
monster (DAMAGE_AIM) is struck as standing, so a grenade goes off on it instead of bouncing; a corpse is bounced off.

## Hands stir flames; the chainsaw cord's hint (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/flamewobble`, 2026-10-19)

### Flames stirred by a fast hand (`vr_flamewobble.cpp`)

- **Now** (`vr_flame_wobble` 1, `vr_flame_wobble_strength` 1, `vr_flame_wobble_speed` 1 m/s; Graphics > Fire Model
  Particles > Flames in the Air): a hand faster than the speed (horizontal, in the room: the play space's own motion
  left out; smoothed over 30 ms) pushes the flames whose axis it passes within 5 units + a quarter of their height,
  linearly more the nearer, 16 lean/s^2 a m/s over the speed. The lean (sideways units a unit up, at most 0.8) is a
  damped spring (1.4 Hz, damping 0.45): it swings the hand's way, comes back about a fifth the other way and settles
  in about a second. Only the flames within 64 units of a fast hand are looked at; only the swinging ones are kept.
- **Covered:** map flame models (`progs/flame2.mdl`: braziers, large and small flames, burning bodies' flames, crates')
  sheared over their foot in `VR_AliasPreTransform`; the wall torches' fires (`vr_walltorch.cpp`, hung or taken: their
  flame tilted, not by the hand holding it); the pyro's pilot light (its particles carried, 40 u/s a unit of lean, not
  by the gun's own hand); fire and smoke particles within 14 units of a fast hand drawn towards half its velocity
  (`particles::gust`). Not leaned: id's whole torch model (`progs/flame.mdl`, only with `vr_walltorch 0`: stick and
  flame are one model) and candles/lanterns (their body would shear too). No flame sprites exist in id's game.
- **Debug:** Debug > Info > Flame Wobble (`vr_flame_wobble_info`: hands' speeds, swinging flames and their most lean,
  the nearest flame model and torch fire), Debug > Logs > Flame Wobble (`vr_debug_flame_wobble` 1 pushes, 2 every
  frame's lean).
- **Checked (headless):** start, `setpos 958 496 30 0 90 0`, the mock main hand swept (`vr_mock_play`) through the large
  flame at (958 526): 3 m/s: peak 0.32 (18 deg) at +0.34 s, back -0.065, settled under 0.02 at +0.93 s; 6.2 m/s: 0.49
  (26 deg), back -0.10, settled at +1.06 s; back through it at 0.6 m/s: no push. Strip (3 m/s, every 0.08 s):
  0 .01 .08 .21 .31 .29 .17 .05 -.03 -.06 -.06 -.03 -.01 .01 0.

### The chainsaw cord's hint (`vr_chainsaw.cpp`)

- **Now** (`vr_chainsaw_cord_hint`: 0 off, 1 until the first pull (default), 2 always; Combat > Enemy Weapons >
  Chainsaw Engine > Cord Hint): a chainsaw in a hand (the main hand's first) is drawn without its seated handle (frame
  9) and the handle alone (frame 10) dangles about its seat, with the cord from its hole: a spring (2.2 Hz, damping

  dangle (now, the most since the last); `vr_chainsaw_cord_pulled 0|1` sets it.

middle, 7.8 cm off it, loaded too, and the 4 cm contact above the tops was tight.

### Heavy weapons: struggle, droop, recoil, two-handed swings (heavyweapons)

- A weight class per weapon, Weapon Weights' **Heft** (`vr_wofs_w_heft_NN`, 0 light .. 1 the laser cannon; -1 from its
  mass, `vr_heavy_auto_from` 10 .. `_full` 20 kg), with its own `w_droop` and `w_hrecoil` multipliers (1; 0 off). Defaults
  (vr_weapons.inc): laser cannon 1; hammer 0.9, mace 0.85; rocket launcher, Widowmaker, chainsaw 0.6; hell knight's and
  death knight's swords 0.35, death guard's 0.3; AD crossbow 0.2; every other weapon 0 (exactly as before: axe, crowbar, knight's,
  zombie knight's and fury's swords, the other guns). Everything below is times Heft times the share held in one hand
  (`l.twoHanded`): two hands, none of it. `vr_heavy 0` turns it all off. New cvars only: no migration (vr_wofs_version
  and vr_cfg_version untouched).
- One-handed struggle (vr_weight.cpp `heavyWrist`): the wrist's stiffness on it times `vr_heavy_struggle_stiffness`
  (0.25) and its damping times `_damping` (0.5) at Heft 1: an abrupt snap lags and swings back springily. The wrenched-out
  drop (vr_weight_drop*) is unchanged and still drops the extreme snaps (in game: the hammer at 1813 deg/s, limit 1583).
- No more abrupt put-backs (weapons with a Heft; others unchanged): far behind the hand (from 60 degrees) the wrist pulls harder (up to 31x near
  165), and the spring keeps it on a 150-degree leash (dragged along, not put back in the hand at once). In game, the
  hammer one-handed, `heavy_wrist_snap.mock`: its 425 deg/s yaw-and-back lagged to 165 and was put back (a 165-degree jump
  in a frame); now 103 at most, no put-back in any step (the extreme ones held at the leash, 150).
- Droop (`vr_heavy_droop` 1, `_deg` 9 at Heft 1): the spring's target turned barrel down about the grip, the drawn hand,
  the aim and the melee with it. In game the hammer sits 11.4 degrees below the controller in one hand (8.1 droop + the
  spring's sag), 0.3 in two.
- One-handed kick (`vr_heavy_recoil` 1, `_kick` 100 deg/s at Heft 1, `_recovery` 0.5x the wrist's stiffness fading over
  `_time` 0.4 s): `weight::heavyKick` from `weaponfx::playerFired`, a spin of the spring (the aim with it), any weapon (the
  laser cannon and rocket launcher have no programmatic recoil). w_hrecoil: laser 0.5 (rapid fire), RL and Widowmaker 1.5.
  In game the laser cannon: one shot 4.4 degrees up, five 0.1 s apart 20, none two-handed.
- Two-handed heavy blows (QC vr_melee.qc): the speeds a blow needs times 1 - (1 - `vr_heavy_melee_2h` 0.45) x Heft (in
  `mh_lenient`); a blow slower than a light weapon's needs a deliberate arc instead: `meleearc` (builtin) walks the far
  end's history back while it goes at least half the speed needed and turns under 45 degrees a pose (under 150 overall):
  at least `vr_heavy_swing_arc` 0.3 m over `_swing_time` 0.12 s (the history holds 24 poses, about 0.33 s: a longer arc
  needs a faster swing). Such a blow skips VR_Melee_CameFar and the wiggle test; its strength is
  `vr_heavy_swing_strength` 1.3 at Heft 1 (up to 1.3x for twice the arc), the weight's damage on top (weightdamage);
  a fast blow keeps its own if stronger. Non-deliberate heavy blows keep a light weapon's CameFar.
- Menu: Weapon Weights > Heavy Handling (a readout, Heft, Droop, One-Handed Kick per weapon; the globals). Debug >
  Heavy Handling Test (`vr_heavy_test [slot]`, offline, every weapon: droop, abrupt-snap lag with and without the
  struggle, the extreme snap against the drop limit, kick peak and recovery, a 170-degree yaw and back).
- Tests: `vr_ad_test 128`/`129` put the hammer/mace in the main hand. `Misc/quakevr/heavy_swings_gen.py <out.mock>
  [onehand]` writes sweeps through a shambler at 0.9, 1.6, 2.2, 3.5 m/s, each back at 0.3 m/s, a 0.27 m jerk and a

## Box3D updated to upstream efca0c18 (worktree `dequant`, branch `agent/box3dup`, 2026-10-19)

Vendored `Quake/vr/external/box3d` from 5d83df83 to upstream main efca0c18 (still the 4 commits audited 2026-10-18:
a2e4816b "Fixes for #175", 8128d740 a template, 0cfc475b "Solver stuff (#189)", efca0c18 "Gyro tolerance (#191)").
21 files copied per the README; our patched files (`src/mesh_contact.c`, `src/core.h`, `src/core.c`) are untouched
upstream in that range, so kept as they were; no files added or removed. API: only additions
(`b3WorldDef.isotropicInertiaTolerance`, `b3World_Set/GetIsotropicInertiaTolerance`, a zero time step runs collision
only); nothing in our code needed changing.

- `isotropicInertiaTolerance = 0` on the game's world (`vr_box3d.cpp`) and on `vr_physics_mtbench`'s: upstream's 0.2
  drops the gyroscopic torque for nearly isotropic bodies; 0 keeps it on every body but an exactly isotropic one, which
  is the old behaviour (before #191 it ran for every body; for an isotropic one the term is zero anyway). Not judged in
  VR whether 0.2 would matter (it would only touch near-cubes and near-spheres, which spinAlign barely turns anyway).

## Melee on ragdolls, batting on purpose, parried enemies stagger as ragdolls (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/meleefeel`, 2026-10-19)

The author: melee blows send ragdolls (corpses, knocked-down or staggering monsters) flying much more than expected;
a random wrist move or a gun brought round bats a projectile back; the parried enemies' stagger looks unnatural.

- **Melee on ragdolls** (`vr_box3d_contacts.cpp` limitRagdollPush; QC `vr_melee.qc` VR_Melee_RagdollPush). Two
  paths flung them. (1) The hands' and weapons' kinematic bodies (vr_box3d_weapon_push) met a ragdoll's part as if it
  weighed nothing: the part took the weapon's speed there and the joints dragged the body along (the "Pushes by mass"
  limit, limitPushes, only ever scaled a ragdoll's pelvis). Now, after each step, a ragdoll a hand's body pushed has
  every part's gain scaled alike: the momentum it got is at most what the pusher brought (its mass, pusherMass: the
  weapon's Mass and vr_box3d_weapon_arm_mass, at its speed into it, times 1 + `vr_melee_ragdoll_bounce`, default 0.2),
  the struck part's share by two masses meeting (the ragdoll's effective mass there: the momentum gained over the part's
  gain, between the part's own and the whole body's), pushed on in later steps the arm's force (vr_box3d_push_force),
  and the part's gain at most `vr_melee_ragdoll_most` (default 5 m/s). The squeeze of a weapon pressed into a body on
  the floor (big sideways ejections with no gain along the push) is caught by the momentum bound. (2) A blow's
  vr_melee_push knockback was a whole-body velocity added to every part (min(600, damage x 10) x 0.5 x vr_push / size).
  A blow on a ragdoll now pushes the part struck (physicspush, new optional `bounce` and `most` arguments) with the
  held thing's mass and the arm's at the blow's speed (mh_dmgspeed) along its way; on a body not yet a ragdoll (killed
  by the blow, a corpse without one) the velocity of the two masses meeting against its whole mass
  (VR_Grapple_MonsterMass). The living standing keep the old knockback. `vr_debug_shots 1`: `melee push: ...`;
  `vr_debug_ragdoll 1` / `vr_debug_box3d 1`: `box3d: ragdoll <n> ... part <b> hit|shoved by <kg>: ..., x<keep>`.
- **Measured** (`vr_ragdoll_speeds`, new; Debug > Tests "Ragdolls' Fastest Since Last": each ragdoll's fastest middle
  (momentum over mass) and part since the last ask): vrfiringrange, synthetic `chop_down_gib` takes at a grunt's corpse
  and at a knocked-down grunt (scratch/launch.sh); middle / part u/s after the chop, before -> after (which contact
  happens varies run to run): sword corpse 282/665 -> 24/128, knocked down 194/465 -> 49/98; AD hammer corpse 233/959
  -> 71/142; AD mace corpse 145/391 -> 54/298; crowbar knocked down (the blow landed) 15/104 -> 51/204; axe 0-75 before
  (misses), 28-36 after. Worst middle 282 -> 71 u/s.
- **Batting on purpose** (`vr_juice.qc` VR_Deflect_SwingWhy). With `vr_deflect_swing` (default 1) a weapon line bats
  only if the pose is a swing as a blow is one: the far end at vr_deflect_speed (as before), the hand itself at
  `vr_deflect_wrist` m/s or faster (default 2, meleewristspeed: a flick turns the weapon, not the hand; a gun brought
  round goes slower), from `vr_deflect_run` m or further (default 0.2, meleerun), not wiggled, taken down to reload or
  drawn back. The timing is the old window (vr_deflect_window 0.2 s; bashes vr_bash_deflect_window 0.3 s of the push,
  unchanged). developer 1: `deflect: accepted <what> of <who>, ... (the hand m/s, from m)` and `deflect: rejected <what>
  of <who>, passing hand <h>'s weapon: <why>[; its last batting swing <s> ago (the window ..)]`, once a projectile.
  Menu: Combat > Batting Projectiles: Batting Needs a Swing, Batting Hand Speed, Batting Swing Length.
- **Checked**: scratch/defl_gen.py mock plays with the shotgun against `impulse 247` (a spike at the face): before, a
  wrist flick, a repositioning (min-jerk, 0.45 m in 0.45 s), a timed swing, a timed one-hand bash and a swing 0.35 s
  early all batted it; after: flick rejected (its far end 0.8 of 1.9 m/s as it passed), repositioning rejected, early
  rejected, swing accepted (hand 2.6 m/s, from 0.31 m), bash accepted.
- **Parried enemies stagger as ragdolls** (`vr_parry_ragdoll`, default 1; QC `vr_kdtrig.qc` VR_Parry_Ragdoll, the
  engine's ragdollStagger `recoverAt` and `sure`). A parried monster on the ground whose monster group takes the
  ragdoll triggers (Combat > Monster Groups: grunts, enforcers, knights, death knights, ogres, zombies, mummies), not
  a boss nor the dummy, staggers back with the shove's active-ragdoll stagger instead of the pain pose. The ground
  behind it (away from you) is looked at as the ragdoll triggers do (ledge, stairs, slope down). Level: push 0.35,
  carried 12 units, sure-footed (no fall by itself), up again at vr_parry_stagger (the old recovery). Over a drop or a
  slope: pushed that way (push 0.7, 28 units), its balance 0.2..0.7 at random (under 0.5 it gives way), its own
  recovery: it may go down (a knockdown, up as any). Its recovery ends the parry (`parry interrupt: <m> recovered (a
  ragdoll's stagger, s)`; down: `... went down from a ragdoll's stagger`). 0: the pose's stagger as before. Menu:
  Combat > Parry and Bash: Parry Stagger as Ragdoll.
- **Checked** (scratch/parry.sh, the shotgun guard, a knight's blow via `impulse 242`, vr_parry_stagger 0.8):
  vrtesthall: stays up, recovered 0.85 s (the pose's: 0.80); vrragtriggers' wide stairs behind it: three runs,
  balance 0.65 and 0.64 recovered on the steps (1.10 s), 0.42 went down at 0.90 s; `vr_parry_ragdoll 0`: the pose's
  stagger, recovered.
- **For VR:** chop and stab bodies on the floor with the sword, axe, AD hammer and mace: they should jolt and
  slide a little, not fly; a strong two-handed hammer blow moves a body most. Bring a gun round in front of a spike or
  flick the wrist: no bat; a real swing and a bash bat. Parry knights and grunts on flat floor (they reel back a step as
  a ragdoll and come at you again after the same pause) and at the top of stairs (sometimes they go down them).

## Stagger and knockdown fixes (agent/staggerfix)

From the author's VR notes on active-ragdoll staggers.

- **Parry ragdoll in the real game** (QC `vr_kdtrig.qc` VR_Parry_Ragdoll). The parry pushes the attacker
  (VR_Push, `vr_parry_push_enemy`, his 0.55, the default) before VR_Parry_Interrupt asks for the ragdoll, and VR_Push
  clears FL_ONGROUND, so the `FL_ONGROUND` gate always failed and the pain pose played. The headless check had
  `vr_parry_push_enemy 0`. Now the gate looks for ground under its feet (a box trace 6 units down), and the parry's
  push and lift are undone before the knockdown starts (the stagger carries it). Checked with the defaults: a knight's
  blow (3/3) and a grunt's shove (3/3) parried on flat floor make it stagger back as a ragdoll and recover at 0.80 s.
- **No freeze at the end of a stagger** (engine `vr_ragactive.cpp` staggerFrame). It used to wait until 0.2 s after its
  pin's carry ended and its pelvis was under 0.4 m/s (up to 1.2 s). The carry eases out, so the last part looked like
  gliding. Now it recovers once 90% of the carry is done, it isn't mid-step, it is steady and slower than
  `vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_settle` (1 m/s), or at the latest `vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_settle_time` (0.35 s) after
  the carry. Flat two-hand shove, carry 1.60 s: recovered at 1.81 s before; 1.27 to 1.30 s now (1.96 s with the cap
  when still leaning). The handback gap is unchanged or smaller (8 to 18 units at most, before 14 to 18).
- **Surprise shoves knock down** (`vr_knockdown_surprise` 1, `vr_knockdown_surprise_angle` 70; QC `vr_melee.qc`
  VR_Knockdown_Surprised, VR_Knockdown_Try). Surprise is taken as the blow lands, before its damage wakes the monster:
  either it isn't fighting the shover (`enemy` not him) or the shove's direction is within the angle of where it faces.
  Then it always goes down: a stagger with balance 0 that gives way after its steps, if its group's shove chance is
  above 0. Grunts on flat floor: 10/10 from behind and 10/10 unaware went down; facing you and aware, 7/10 by chance.
- **No backpedalling on air** (`vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_drop` 20 units). If the floor under its pelvis is more than
  that much lower than where it stood, for 0.06 s, the stagger falls (a topple), sure-footed or not. Tested with
  `vr_knockdown_ledge 0` and the ledge/stairs triggers off, a steady grunt (chance 0.01). Shoved off vrragtriggers' 32
  drop: 10/10 fell "no floor under it" (with `_drop 0`, 4/4 walked off and recovered on the floor below). Shoved off
  the top of the wide stairs: 10/10 fell.
- **Getting up on slopes** (engine `vr_box3d_knockdown.cpp` standSpot; `vr_knockdown_getup_slope` 30,
  `vr_knockdown_getup_force` 4.5 s; QC VR_Knockdown_Think, VR_Knockdown_Upright). On a slope, the standing box over the
  floor point cut into the slope uphill, so no place was ever free ("no room to get up", forever). Now the box is
  lifted clear by about how far its corner rises on the slope, up to the slope limit (plus 1 degree). A steeper slope
  doesn't count as somewhere to stand. Still down `_force` s after it went down with no room: it gets up where it lies
  (ragdollgetup anywhere). A monster stood up over the floor drops onto it (Upright clears FL_ONGROUND when there is
  nothing under it). Enforcers knocked uphill on the 12, 20 and 30 degree ramps got up on the ramp; before the 1
  degree margin, the 30 ramp (30.03 degrees) took the forced path at 4.6 and 4.9 s; on 40 degrees they slid to the
  floor and got up there.
- **Tests**: `vr_kdtrig_test` 8 (two-hand shove), 9 (its blow on you), 10 (knocked down), 11 (its shove on you);
  `vr_kdtrig_test_class` 6 knight, 7 enforcer; `vr_kdtrig_test_wait`, `_face`, `_aware`.
- **Menus**: Combat > Knockdowns: Surprise Shoves Knock Down, From Behind Within, Steepest Slope to Stand, Forced
  Get-Up; beside Stagger Recovery Blend (physics menu): Stagger Settles Below, Stagger Settle at Most, Stagger Drop Falls.
- **For VR:** parry a knight's swing and a grunt's shove: it steps back as a ragdoll and comes on again. Shove a grunt
  until it recovers: it should take up the fight right as its backpedal ends, with no pause or glide. Sneak up and
  shove one from behind, or one that hasn't seen you: it goes down. Slap a grunt standing at a ledge or at the top of
  stairs: it falls instead of walking on air. Knock enforcers down on a ramp: they get up on it; on a steep one they
  slide, then stand up within about 5 s.

## Swept blades: the whole blade and a heavy head's volume strike (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/meleesweep`, 2026-10-19)

His note: long weapons feel like they miss; the blow seemed to land only where the blade first touched (a sword swung
at the ground slashed at its tip; a big swing passed an enemy its blade went through).

- **Before:** VR_Melee_Sweep swept each of the layout's points (a sword's 6 striking points, 0.27..1 of the hand to the
  tip; an axe's, the AD hammer's and mace's 2, at 0.75 and 1) as a 3-unit line from the last pose to this one; the
  blow landed at the outermost point in the thing, a wall at the first point touching it. Between two points nothing
  struck (the hammer's points 7.9 units apart: a thin thing between them was passed), a hammer's or mace's head struck
  only on its handle's line (its head is 23.6 and 19.8 units across, 9.4 and 14.1 deep), and a flat chop at the floor
  landed at the pommel (the first of the points, all as early).
- **Now (`vr_melee_swept 1`, the default; Debug > Tests > Melee Sweep > Swept Blades; 0 is the old way exactly):**
  VR_Melee_Ribs makes the sweep's lines: the layout's points, and between two neighbouring striking points as many lines
  more as keep them at most 1.5 thicknesses apart (at most 3 more a pair: the swept quad covered by the lines' 3-unit
  thickness, a curved blade's chords between its points on the curve); a hammer's or mace's head adds a grid of lines
  over its middle (at most 4 x 4), as thick as half its depth and reaching its faces: its volume as a set of capsules.
  The head's box comes from AD's model as made (vr_admelee.cpp: the head's vertices in the frame admeleebend uses, as
  shares of the line; builtin `admeleehead(kind, which)`); without AD's data there is none (the line's points as before).
  Each thing the lines meet (its box, or its model with vr_hit_precise) is scored by how squarely a line crossed it:
  the line's nearest to its middle, the blade proper's lines (from VR_MELEE_BLADE_FROM out, a fist's knuckles) before
  those nearer the hand, a line already in it last. The blow lands on the thing crossed most squarely, at that line's
  contact; its kind and strength stay the outermost striking point's in it (VR_Melee_Decide unchanged: a stab is still
  a stab, the same damage). A wall: where the blade went deepest past its surface (held off it by the hand's slide: the

## Heavy weapons settle; Ghost Hands (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/heavyfix`, 2026-10-19)

The author: the rocket launcher, chainsaw and AD hammer in one hand spazzed out at a fast wrist wiggle and bounced at a
flick; the hammer two-handed bounced and turned too much at the end of a blow.

- **The cause** (vr_weight.cpp `step`, weapons with a Heft only): far behind the hand the catch-up raised the wrist's
  pull up to 31x without its damping (a damping ratio down to a fifth), and the wrist's torque limit clipped the pull
  and the damping together: at the limit the weapon lost its damping, the leash dragged it along at the hand's speed and
  the limit could not stop it again. A +-60 degree yaw wiggle at 2 Hz swung the hammer, chainsaw and rocket launcher
  +-180 (gain 3), 113-135 degrees still off 0.3 s after the hand stopped. On top, the struggle's damping (0.5) times a
  weapon's own Spring Damping (the laser cannon 0.6, the chainsaw 0.65) left the laser cannon at a ratio of 0.3: a blow
  stopped dead swung on 54 degrees and rang.
- **Fixed:** the catch-up's damping grows with the square root of its pull (the same ratio); the torque limit clips the
  pull alone, the damping acts beyond it; a weapon with a Heft is damped at least `vr_heavy_damping_min` (0.8, Weapon
  Weights > Heavy Handling "Settle (Least Damping)"; no lower than Aiming: Spring's own damping). Light weapons
  unchanged (the old path).
- **Test:** `vr_heavy_wiggle [slot] [motion hands]` (Debug > Heavy Wobble Test): offline at 90 fps, per heavy weapon one-
  and two-handed, yaw wiggles +-30/30/60/45 at 3/5/2/4 Hz, roll and pitch +-45 at 3 Hz, flicks (30, 90, roll 45 in 60 ms
  and back), a blow stopped dead; gain, fastest turn over the wrist's, ringing, degrees still off 0.3 s after. One-handed
  w60@2 gain before/after: rocket launcher 2.84/1.22, laser 0.61/0.66 (late 11.7/2.2), chainsaw 2.99/0.98 (late
  112.7/4.3), hammer 2.97/0.97 (late 134.6/4.3); the laser's 1H blow late 66.7/12.2 (ring 4/1); two-handed unchanged
  (gain 1.05-1.2). In game (`Misc/quakevr/heavy_wiggle_gen.py`, vr_debug_weight 1 trace): the w60@2 lag 150 (the leash)
  -> 50 for the hammer and the chainsaw. The extreme snaps still drop (vr_weight_drop untouched).
- **Not reproduced:** the chainsaw's fast bounce at a small flick and the two-handed hammer's bounce at the end of a
  blow (offline: 6 degrees past, settled in 0.1 s; in game `Misc/quakevr/heavy_chop_gen.py`, chops into the floor at
  2-5 m/s: at most 7.5 degrees, no ringing). No Hit has four new labels for takes: "Heavy: Wrist Wiggle, Rocket
  Launcher", "Heavy: Chainsaw Flick", "Heavy: Hammer 1H Wiggle", "Heavy: Hammer 2H Blow on the Ground" (replay with
  vr_debug_weight 1: weight_trace.txt rows now end with the target's angles, tpitch/tyaw/troll).
- **Ghost Hands** (Player Appearance > Ghost Hands; default off): `vr_ghost_hands` 0 off, 1 hands, 2 hands and forearms
  (a translucent forearm from the drawn elbow); `_which` 0 both, 1 the off hand only; `_alpha` 0.35; `_lightness` 1.6;
  `_tint` 0.6 (0 own colours, 1 cold blue); `_fade_from` 2 cm, `_fade_range` 4 cm (the farther of the grip and a point
  15 cm ahead, so a turn counts). The jointed hand's mesh as posed (the same bones), placed where setupHand would draw
  it at `hands::State::unresolvedPos/Rot` (new: before the walls, the two-handed grip and the spring), translucent and
  light-multiplied. Debug has a toggle too. Checked: the hammer drooped 80 degrees, the ghost drawn below the drawn hand.
- **For VR:** wiggle and flick the rocket launcher, chainsaw and hammer in one hand: they should lag and settle, never
  whip round; snap hard: still dropped. Hammer two-handed blows on the ground: if it still bounces, record the new No Hit
  labels. Ghost Hands on with each heavy weapon and a two-handed grip.

### Leg-sweep test made deterministic (2026-10-19)

`Misc/quakevr/foegrab/legsweep_test.py` ran on the wall clock (`-RealTime`). `vr_mock_play` paces on `realtime`, so the
0.25 s sweep (8 cm a tick at 72 Hz) met the shins on different ticks, or not at all, depending on the machine's load.
That is why 9-10 cases failed, and different ones each run. It now runs with `vr_fixed_frames 1` (fast mode): the play's
clock advances by the same 1/72 s frames as the server, and `sv_random_seed 7` fixes the grunt's AI. Five runs in a row
gave byte-identical legsweep lines and verdicts (`LS_REALTIME=1` gives the old runs). Harness fixes for cases that never
met the legs:
- The laser cannon is held 40 degrees higher. Its 42-unit line rested its muzzle on the floor, where it stuck, then
  jumped past the legs in one frame, which was ignored as a teleport.
- The brick and the crate sweep 0.3 m lower and further forward. Held flat, they passed over and in front of the shins.
- The crate is now the small one (107), put in the hand at the start pose. A crate that jumped there with the hand was
  let go ("carry: stopped at the body").

A missing or stale game log now fails the case. Stable result: 17/20. Three falls fail every time, and the cause is the
physics, not the timing:
- nailgun_lr and sword_hilt fall backward: the head lands 30 units back by its facing and only 13-17 against the sweep.
- shotgun_toward falls back-right, its feet sliding 7.6 units against the sweep.

Every lr fall leans backward by 15-30 units; these two lean far enough to fail the check.

### Cut flesh after Quake's gibs; the cut piece's fountain streams after it

The cut's flesh was a fan of 1D blood stripes (the limb cap: each corner its own column of an 8-row red strip; the body stump: the wound paint's star of three reds over the cone the cut bone collapses into). Now both use one recipe after Quake's own gibs' and heads' necks (sampled for its colours only: mostly the palette's dark blood ramp 64..72, brown meat 96..100, pale sinew 117..119, dark pits, wet glints; chunky cells; the bone and marrow in the middle): the limb model's cap (vr_limbmodel.cpp fleshColour) is laid flat on a 32-row flesh strip under its skin at 2.5 texels a unit; the body (vr_glsl.h StumpFlesh) draws it within 1.25 limb thicknesses of each cut joint (InstanceData's new Stump: the cut bones, the reach; ragdoll::stumpLook), the cone and round it, a ragged edge, wet but not glazed. The cut piece's own fountain (vr_limbs_end_fountain) throws 2-5 drops a tick (was 1-3) with a share of the piece's speed, so they stream after it. Test aids: vr_limb_test 39 (float 14 units from the nearest corpse's stump, facing it) and 40 (the last limb hung 10 units before your eyes, its cap turned to you), Debug > Gore Tests > Limb Gore.

- **Weight classes**: the monster's weight is `vr_kdtrig_weight` (80 kg) times its group's resistance (grunt 80, knight
  and enforcer 92, death knight 128, ogre 200); the thrower's is the thrown body's mass (its ragdoll's) or yours
  (`vr_kdtrig_tackle_weight` 80). Up to `vr_kdtrig_weight_topple` (1.5) times the thrower's it can be toppled (the
  knockdown's topple, the way it was struck); up to `vr_kdtrig_weight_stagger` (3) times it only staggers (a parry's

  strike's way); heavier stands. Shamblers, fiends, dogs and the bosses never (their groups take no triggers).

  `ragdollfling`) or held while a holding hand swings (not only dragged), its middle at a quarter of `_speed` or more,
  its parts' boxes meeting a living monster's box (ragdolls pass through living monsters in the physics: no contact
  existed), and calls `VR_KdTrig_BodyHit(m, body, mass, vel)`. Strike = mass x speed / (monster's weight x `_speed`
  200): 1 or more topples a toppleable class (chance `vr_kdtrig_thrown`, 1), `_least` (0.4) .. 1 only staggers, less

## Melee frame-rate independence (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/meleefps`, 2026-10-19)

The server ticks at 72 Hz whatever the headset's rate, and each tick reads the latest frame's pose. At 90 Hz a tick's
pose is one or two frames newer than the last tick's (11 or 22 ms for the tick's 13.9), at 120 Hz (the author's
headset, the recorded takes) 8 or 17 ms, at 144 Hz 7, 14 or 21 ms; a dropped frame likewise. Every speed was the pose's
move over the tick's time, so a steady swing read at 0.8 and 1.6 times its speed by turns (90 Hz), and every gate read
from one sample (blow speed, land, whoosh, pullback, deflect, bash, wiggle, meleearc's floor) beat with it.

- **Pose clock.** The client sends its poses' time with each move (`VrMove::poseClock`: `hands::State::poseTime`, the
  tracking's time after slow motion's filter, modulo `VR_POSE_CLOCK_WRAP` 1024 s) -> `.vr_posetime`. `VR_Melee_Track`
  and the leg sweep (`vr_legsweep.cpp`: its speed gate, the 25 m/s teleport guard, its 0.08 s stroke) measure over the
  poses' times (the ticks' when unknown or implausible: 0-0.25 s); a tick with the same frame's pose again is no news.
- **Turning chords** (`VR_Melee_TurnVel`): a far or near point's velocity about the grip is its chord over the span
  turned on to, and scaled as, a 1/72 s chord (a chord's way is the arc's at its middle: over two frames a blade's tip
  points further back into the turn, PULLBACK). At 72 Hz frames nothing changes.
- **Swept arcs** (`VR_Melee_ArcRib`): a point's line bends through the arc's middle (about the grip) when the chord
  cuts its inside by more than half the line's thickness (`VR_MELEE_ARC_SAG` 0.5; ribs 40 -> 48).
- `meleearc`'s 45 degrees a pose is 45 degrees a 72 Hz tick, per second over the two poses' times.
- Weapon wrench (`vr_weight.cpp`): its clock is the poses' time; its ring 64 -> 128 samples (0.5 s at 240 Hz); the
  tracking-jump guard 90 degrees a 72 Hz frame, per second.
- Replays: takes play their poses at their recorded `xr_time` (the runtime's, steady; a frame's dt jitters a
  millisecond). Tooling: `vr_motion_eval_rate/_jitter/_stutter` (defaults for vr_motion_eval: eval.sh `EVAL_PRE`), the
  eval's `stutter N` (every N-th frame dropped), `vr_fixed_frames_stutter`, legsweep_test `LS_RATE`/`LS_STUTTER`.

Measured (177 takes; flips: verdicts against the same build's takes at their own 120 Hz frames; strength: the first
hit's, mean |difference|):

| rate | before: fails, flips, strength diff | after: fails, flips, strength diff |
|---|---|---|
| native (120 Hz, recorded ticks) | 9, -, - | 8, - (1 vs before: slash_backswing_up_left 12-35-23 now passes), - |
| 72 | 8, 1, 0.21 | 8, 2, 0.07 |
| 90 | 13, 4, 0.32 | 8, 0, 0.07 |
| 120 (engine ticks) | 10, 3, 0.17 | 8, 0, 0.05 |
| 144 | 8, 3, 0.22 | 8, 2, 0.07 |
| 90, every 5th frame dropped | 19, 12, 0.30 | 18, 10, 0.20 |
| 144, every 5th dropped | 20, 13, 0.26 | 19, 11, 0.15 |

At the reference the verdicts hold, but the first hits' strengths are 0.11 lower on average (damage about 19% lower):
the beat's 1.2-times peaks at 120 Hz are gone (a swing's speed is its own). Open: dropped frames still miss ~10 slashes
(the blade's far end jumps early, far 30 m/s with the grip at 0.9, touching the dummy before the swing, which then
can't strike it again until it re-enters; not the speed estimate, not the weight's put-back: to be found). The leg
sweep suite's verdicts at 72/90/120/144: 3/4/4/2 fails (before 3/3/4/3), mostly the fall's direction (physics) and the
borderline `toward` case; with dropped frames 11 both before and after (four weapons "no contact").

Follow-up (same branch): the strength keeps the old feel. His takes are 120 Hz (Virtual Desktop; `vr_melee_speed` at its
default 3.2). The beat had read the first hits 1.15-1.2 times too fast, and his strengths were tuned on that:
`VR_MELEE_STRENGTH_SPEED` 1.13 scales the speed only for the strength and damage (the land/slow/wiggle gates read the
true speed; a QC constant, no cvar to migrate). Takes at their own frames: first-hit strength 1.171 (old 1.168), damage
per take 26.07 (old 25.95); at 120 Hz with the engine's ticks 1.181 / 26.56. Verdicts as before but
slash_backswing_up_left 12-35-23, now a pass. The dropped-frame misses are not the speed: with every 5th frame dropped
the replayed hands sit further from the recorded ones (`hand_error_u` median 2.6 units against 1.7 at 90 Hz, 0.9 at
the takes' own frames; the missed slash 11.7 against 2.7; at most 87): the blade reaches the dummy earlier in the
swing (slower, drawn back: refused) and is through it before the blow. To be found: what places the body or hands
differently with an irregular frame (the lean, the body's gait, the replay's placement). The rule that a struck thing is
struck again only entering it is not involved (it applies only to what a blow landed on).
## Parry balance (worktree `dequant`, branch `agent/parrybalance`, 2026-10-19)

Vittorio's approved plan: a parry's effect depends on how strong it is against how sturdy the monster is, so bare hands
no longer stagger an ogre and weapons/explosives stay the answer to heavy monsters.

- **Strength** = tool x grip x timing (QC `combat.qc` VR_Parry_Strength): bare hands `vr_parry_tool_hand` 0.4, any
  weapon `vr_parry_tool_weapon` 1, a heavy one up to `vr_parry_tool_heavy` 1.3 at Heft 1 (by its weight class,
  `weaponheft`); two hands (and the crossed arms) `vr_parry_grip_2h` x1.5; well timed `vr_parry_timed` x1.25.
