## Zombies fall as ragdolls; the toolgun's Widowmaker loaded (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/zombierag`, 2026-10-19)

Zombies (BACKLOG "Zombies stuck knocked down"): the stock fall (paine1..12: not solid, health reset each frame, up only
where `walkmove(0, 0)` fits, else retried for ever) could leave a zombie lying for good, out of reach of every shot but
a blast. Now zombie_pain's fall (a hit of 25 or more, or a second hit within 3 s) is `VR_Knockdown_ZombieFall`
(vr_knockdown.qc): a knockdown's active ragdoll (room made from the dead only), toppled away from the attacker (push
0.6, 16 units), down for the knockdown's time; hit there (its own rules: health back to 60 each hit, only 60 in one hit
gibs it), grabbed, beheaded, its limbs cut, gibbed; up through the zombie's get-up (paine13 on, or the engine's rise),
its AI back (inpain 0 at zombie_run1). A downed or rising zombie never begins another fall. No ragdoll (ragdolls off,
no rig, no room): the stock fall, but lying solid with a lying body's box (`zombie_lie`; also paine12's retries, the
mummy's, a lying-spawned one's wake), so shots reach it.

The other fake-death zombies: Rogue's mummy never falls in pain (only its lying spawn's wake: its retries now solid);
Hipnotic's lying zombie rises at once (zombie_lay12); Dawn of the Machine's shub zombies and infected are monster_zombie
with zombie_pain (their rising lie stays upstream's); AD's zombie, mummy and zombie knight: `VR_AD_ZombiePain`
(vr_ad_monsters.qc) wraps AD's pain (no AD file patched) and turns the fall it begins (paine1, painb1, the knight's
paind1) into the ragdoll; down there each hit puts its health back (`VR_AD_PainDown`). With no ragdoll AD's own fall
stays (its wakeup gibs a zombie blocked too long). No Quoth zombie in the progs. Honey's axe gibbing "zombies on the
ground" (.wad) only sees the stock fall.

Checks (vrtesthall, `vr_knockdown_test 23/24`): a 30 hit: "falls as a ragdoll", up after 4.2-4.8 s, knocked down again
(inpain reset), up again; a grenade 150 units short: down, up after 4.3 s; down, a 5 hit: health 60; a 260 hit: gibbed;
down, `vr_decap_test 7`: beheaded, dies for good; down, the SSG test shot (aimed at the standing head) killed it whole
by a limb (the zombie rule); AD's mummy (238) and zombie knight (201): ragdoll, up after 5.1 / 5.4 s.

The toolgun's Widowmaker (`toolgun_upgrade_ssg`, a func_weapon_grabbable): its record was made with the super shotgun's
clip (2) before its upgrade was set; `VR_WeaponGrabbable_Make` now gives it `VR_ClipSizeOf` (the tube, 16).
`vr_ad_test 148`: "comes loaded: PASS (16 of 16)"; the map pickup's (`vr_ad_test 149`'s last check) passes too (its
other checks fail in the plain headless run: no manual reloading there).

### Body shields

A corpse (or a knocked-down monster) held in one hand or two already stops monsters' hitscan and projectiles: their
traces (MOVE_HITGIBS | MOVE_HITMODEL) and missiles meet its drawn ragdoll, which takes the damage, the blood, the wounds
and limb pops (a held shin shot off drops the body). Held up against you, though, the body lies inside your own hit box,
whose face a shot meets first: `VR_BodyShield_Take` (weapons.qc; FireBulletsImpl for monsters' pellets, VR_Proj_Begin
for their projectiles) looks for the held body's shape along the shot up to your middle and gives it the hit. Checks
(`scratch/shield.sh` of worktree fastship: a grunt corpse taken with `vr_mock_hand_to ... ragdoll near`, held up with
`vr_mock_hand`; `vr_knockdown_test 26` holds the nearest grunt or enforcer still, `27` fires its own shot at you, `28`
one aimed through the held body, `25` prints your health and what you hold): e1m1, one hand, a grunt's 20 rounds: 8 on
the body, 5 on you (over it at the head, beside it), 7 wide; vrtesthall, two hands, 15 rounds through the body: 15 on
it; enforcer lasers through it: on it (two limb pops, then it fell). The shield code's own case (the body wholly inside
your box) did not come up in these poses (`vr_debug_shots 2` prints its looks). Open: after the off hand takes a
ragdoll first, its QC `offhand_held` reads empty while the engine says the hand holds it.
## Enemy weapons' relief (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/weaponreliefs`, 2026-10-20)

His note: many new equippable enemy weapons look flat. **Inventory** (relief inside the skin's islands: mean tilt,
share over 5 degrees, alpha mean / 10th percentile; our player weapons' baked maps: 3-6 degrees, 25-35 %, 224-243 / 210-239):

| Weapon (model) | Relief before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knight's sword `v_ksword`, death knight's `v_hksword` | baked (7.5 / 9.1 deg) | unchanged |
| Grunt gun `v_gruntgun`, enforcer rifle `v_enfrifle` | baked (7.7 / 8.8) | unchanged |
| Ogre chainsaw `v_chainsaw`, laser cannon `v_laserg`, Mjolnir `v_hammer` | baked (3.9 / 4.1 / 4.1) | unchanged |
| Freddie's super nailgun (`v_nail2`, ours) | baked | unchanged |
| AD Shadow Axe / Widowmaker / Plasma Gun (`#vr`) and the Plasma Gun's cell, well | made from colours, shallow (vr_parallax_models 0.25) | relief made at load: 3.3 / 2.1 / 5.8 deg, alpha 237 / 244 / 244 |
| AD soldiers' guns `v_gruntgun.mdl#adv0..7` | made | the rifle's baked map on its rows + relief on the add-ons: 5.6-6.7 deg, alpha 235 / 218 |
| AD crossbow `w_dcrossbow.mdl#gun0` (and old `#gun<n>`) | made | 5.7 deg, alpha 225 / 213 |
| AD melee `#melee`: fury, death knight, zombie knight, death guard swords, hammer, mace | made | 1.3-7.1 deg, alpha 225-244 / 208-240 |

**How** (`Quake/vr/vr_skinrelief.cpp`, new): a model whose name has `#vr`, `#adv`, `#gun` or `#melee` (`VR_SkinReliefWanted`)
gets, instead of the map made from its skin's colours, one made from its skin in our bake's style, ported from
normaltiles.paint_heights / normaldetail.weapon_heights: painted seams (narrow elongated valleys, 6-16 texels long) as
0.8-texel grooves, painted rivets (round bright peaks up to 3.5 texels) as 0.9-texel domes, wood and leather grained along
their streaks (no checkering); twice the skin's size (four times under 256 wide); heights as finish_heights (broad forms
out, 95th percentile the surface, 0.4 units at alpha 0, HEIGHT_CAP), from the model's own units per texel (the
area-weighted median over its first frame), capped at 0.3 units a texel: AD's monsters' weapons are about a unit a
texel, where every texel would reach the cap. Drawn as an authored map (NORMALMAP_AUTHORED | FILE, new
NORMALMAP_RELIEF: vr_normalmap_authored, vr_parallax_authored; TexMgr_AuthoredHeights raises the islands' rims, so the
rays stop at seams). Made in TexMgr_LoadImage32 from the skin as it uploads, so a reload remakes it; never a file, so
nothing from AD's assets is written to the repository. The burst rifle's variants copy `v_gruntgun.mdl_0_norm.png` over
their skin's first 260 rows (vr_adgunart.cpp keeps the rifle's coordinates). Kept in the disk cache with the made skin
maps (vr_normalmap_cache; build `5e1ef00000000001`, bump with any change).
New cvar **`vr_weapon_relief`** (1; 0: the colour-made map as before; read as the model loads, so a restart).

**Cost**: made once per skin (2-35 ms on the pool: a #adv variant 25-35 ms, a melee weapon 3 ms; about 0.35 s for
all 24 on AD's first load), then read from the disk cache. Drawing: the authored path, as our own weapons. Video
memory: the maps are twice the skin (a #adv variant's 512 x 840).

**Checks**: `scratch/wr_all.sh <name>` (worktree gorefx) holds each in the main hand on AD's start (`vr_ad_test 97..99`,
`73..80`, `116..119`, `128`, `impulse 165`), lit at the spawn and in shade at (616 0 244); `PRE="vr_weapon_relief 0"`
for the old maps. `developer 1` prints a `skinrelief:` line per map with the statistics above. Before/after sheets:
`scratch/weaponreliefs_light.png`, `_shade.png`, `_crossbow.png` (crossbow: `vr_test_spawn 202; impulse 241; vr_ad_test 93`).
Screen pixels changed on the held weapon: 4-30 % lit, 0.1-5 % in shade (dark there). Our own models' maps are untouched.
Thin parts: the heights stay within HEIGHT_CAP (0.12 units, x1.5 at vr_parallax_authored) and the rims rise at every
island edge, so blades and handles can't pull texels across a seam; not seen moving in VR yet.

- **For VR**: hold the Shadow Axe, the Widowmaker, an AD soldier's gun and a death knight's sword close up under a
  torch and turn them: seams and rivets should catch the light as on our shotgun; look along a sword's blade and the
  axe's handle at a grazing angle for paint that swims. `vr_weapon_relief 0` + restart for the old look.

## Shoulder charge (the tackle redone) and thrown bodies that topple (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/shouldercharge`, 2026-10-20)

His two items: the tackle fired far too often by accident (he turned it off); thrown bodies toppled live enemies too
rarely and pushed them too little.

**Shoulder charge: design (phase 1, a prototype behind the old tackle switch, off).** The guard, palm-forward and
shove poses are gone (`VR_KdTrig_TacklePose`, `vr_kdtrig_tackle_gap`, `_slow` removed). New `VR_KdTrig_ChargePose`
(QC `vr_kdtrig.qc`), in the level frame along the run, from the head:

- side-on: the hands' middle lies `vr_kdtrig_tackle_turn` (50) degrees or more round from the run. With `vr_movement_mode 1`
  he runs where the head looks, so the head can't show the torso's turn; the hands in front of a side-on torso sit
  beside the run (the hands to the right: the left shoulder leads; the event's sub `left`/`right`);
- both hands `_low` (12) units or more below the head, each within `_reach` (20) of the head's line, none reaching
  ahead past 0.6 of it (the leading arm tucked, not a shove); no shove or bash going, no gun aimed two-handed;
- held `_hold` (0.15) s (the pose may be taken standing, before the run-up), running at `_speed` (0.85) of
  sv_maxspeed the way he looks (60 degrees: a sidestep doesn't count), his box about to meet a living monster's.
- The hit: a `shouldercharge` event (motion takes); he bounces back `_bump` (100 u/s) always; by weight
  (`VR_KdTrig_Bump`, his `_weight` 80 kg): a toppleable class is launched and carried `_knock` (96) units times his
  weight over its (up to 1.5) times `_push`, then toppled (a grunt: carried 96, the ragdoll "shoved down: 77 units
  on"); a heavier class staggers back 12 + 0.6 of that on its feet (an ogre: moved 43 units); heavier stands.
- The training dummy judges it with the Shoulder Charges off too (the event and his bounce; it stands), so takes
  record and replay whatever the switch.
- `vr_kdtrig_tackle_on` 0 (config 169 migrates 1 -> 0); menu Combat > Ragdoll Triggers > **Shoulder Charges** (the page
  renamed from Tackles: menu path check 0 missing); `vr_kdtrig_debug 2` says, each half second while running fast, why
  the pose isn't a charge (`kdtrig: charge pose: no (a hand high (11 units below the head); turn 0 deg, ...)`). Each take
  sample has `charge` (turn, drop, reach) and `charge_ok` (the side or 0, the ground speed, held s) in its `qc` column.

**Motion recorder**: categories **Shoulder Charge** (`shoulder_charge`: left, right, hands_clasped, arms_tucked,
with_gun, with_melee) and **Shoulder Charge Not Expected** (`no_shoulder_charge`: running_guard, running_shove,
running_gun, walking, sidestep, running_idle, running_melee); expect.cfg `shouldercharge` / `!shouldercharge`; the
replay's events column carries it; the header's settings list `vr_kdtrig_tackle*`, `vr_movement_mode`, `sv_maxspeed`.
eval.sh (kit; staged as `fastship/scratch/eval_charge.sh`, the current kit eval.sh plus this): the takes are out of the
melee sets and replayed with the lift/judo ones, `shoulder charge: expected caught a/b, missed c, false d/e`, each take
by name. Synthetic takes (`motion_synth.py charge`: the moving stick now written): left and right caught 2/2, 0 false
of 5 (running guard, running idle, running shove, walking 155 u/s: too slow, sidestep).

**Takes to record** (melee recording room, the training dummy, empty hands unless said; start each 4-5 m from it, start
the take, take the pose, push the stick fully forward, run into it, end the take): positives 16: 4 `left` and 4
`right` (arms tucked), 4 `hands_clasped` (2 each shoulder), 2 `with_gun`, 2 `with_melee`; negatives 20: 4
`running_guard`, 4 `running_shove`, 4 `running_gun` (aimed one- and two-handed), 3 `walking` (the charge's pose,
walking in), 3 `sidestep` (strafing into it side-on), 2 `running_idle`. Then the detector gets tuned on them.

**Thrown bodies.** What limited the topples: (1) the strike was a hard gate, toppling only at 1 or more (a grunt
corpse on a grunt slower than `_speed` at contact never toppled; hand throws' middles are often 100-200 u/s); (2) the
strike's speed was the body's middle at contact, after its limbs dragged or caught on the way; (3) no push back at all:
`ragdollshovetopple` carries a body its reach only with a launch along the way, and `VR_KdTrig_Down` gave none, so it
fell over where it stood (about 25-30 units whatever the strike; the stagger's step back the parry's 12 units). Fixed:
the topple's chance grows from none at `_least` to its full at a strike of 1 (else a stagger back); the engine
(`callBodyHits`) counts a thrown body's strike at 0.85 of its fastest since the throw at least (`thrownPeak`); the
topple launches it at 150 + 100 x strike x push u/s (at most 450) and carries it 8 + 32 x push units (thrown's carry
24 -> 32; push 0.6 x strike, 0.6..1.5, times `_push`); a stagger is pushed back 12 + 20 x strike x push units (0.6 of
it for a heavier class, at most 96). His values are the defaults (config 169): `vr_kdtrig_thrown_speed` 200 -> 160,
`_least` 0.4 -> 0.05, `_push` 1 -> 2.

Headless (`vr_kdtrig_test 44`, new: Debug > Tests > Ragdoll Triggers > Throw Trials; a fresh grunt corpse 128 units
before a fresh grunt, flung at it; the push the target's level move, its pelvis when down, after 1.2 s; 10 trials
each; his values both times):

| fling u/s | before: down / staggered / stood, push | after |
|---|---|---|
| 120 | (strike 0.9: never toppled; not run) | 8 / 2 / 0, 38 units |
| 160 | - | 10 / 0 / 0, 37 |
| 200 | 10 / 0 / 0, 23 | 10 / 0 / 0, 46 |
| 300 | 9 / 0 / 1, 24 | 10 / 0 / 0, 62 |
| 450 | 10 / 0 / 0, 30 | 10 / 0 / 0, 85 |

At an ogre (300 u/s, strike 0.8): staggered 5 of 5, pushed 31 units. In the headless room his values already toppled
nearly always at 200 u/s and more; in his games the bodies' slower middles (and the hard gate) were what kept them up.

**For VR**: throw corpses and knocked-down grunts at grunts gently and hard (more topple, and they fly back farther

## Gib impacts: one rule for thrown, held and struck gibs (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/gibhits`, 2026-10-20)

The author: a head gib (or gib, small gib, brain chunk) smashed while held into a wall, the floor or a monster should
burst as a throw does (it never burst held), and a light tap must not burst it: tossed up and tapped with the other
hand it burst every time (any hand hit at `vr_melee_speed`, 3.2 m/s, dealt 20+ damage against 12/18 health); it should
bounce off like a volleyball. Now one impact rule, `VR_Gib_Impact` (vr_carry.qc): intensity = the impact's speed over
the kind's burst speed (`VR_Gib_BurstSpeed`); from 1 it bursts, from 0.5 it is worn by `(2i - 1)` of its full health
(two hits at 0.75 burst it), below 0.5 nothing. The paths:

- **Hand and weapon hits** on a loose one (`VR_Gib_Struck` the touch, `VR_Gib_Blow` a melee blow, `VR_Gib_HeldFrameHand`
  one held in the other hand): the hand's (blow's) speed against it (at most its own, as before; a blow times its
  stamina). Short of bursting it bounces off the striker along the hit (`VR_Gib_HandImpact`: `v += n (1 + e) u`, u the
  approach speed, e `vr_gib_bounce`, at most 15 m/s); a small gib in its blow grace stays put. One tap is one hit
  (`.vr_gib_hittime`, 0.15 s: the touch and the sweep's blow land together). The touch still starts at `vr_melee_speed`
  (slower: the nudge's push, as before). `vr_sgib_graceblow` is gone (`VR_Gib_Hit` takes the speed now).
- **Held smash** (`VR_Gib_HeldSmash`, from `VR_Carry_Follow`, one or two hands): the hand's line meets the level (its
  trace), or a monster or solid thing (a second trace with monsters); the speed into it is the smaller of the gib's last
  frame's motion and the hand's own velocity along the normal (walking into a wall with it held out is not a smash). It
  bursts out of the hand (`VR_Gib_KnockOut`); no damage to the monster (the hand's own blow does that).
- **Thrown** (`VR_Gib_Think2`, `VR_Gib_Touch`): as before, its own thresholds as the intensity (turn / Gib Splat Speed,
  hand speed / Hard Throw Bursts, speed into a monster / Gib Splat Speed): only the outcome goes through the rule.
- Shots and blasts: `T_Damage` / `VR_Gib_Damage` as before.

New cvars (Gibs and Corpses page, after Hard Throw Bursts): **`vr_gib_burst_speed`** 5 m/s, **`vr_gib_burst_head`** 1.3x
(6.5 m/s), **`vr_gib_burst_small`** 0.7x (3.5 m/s: small gibs, brain chunks), **`vr_gib_bounce`** 0.4.

**Checks**: `vr_smallgibs_test 25` (Debug > Gore Tests, "Gib Impacts: Smash, Tap, Hit"; after test 15): a head held in
the off hand smashed into the wall at 13 m/s bursts, at 2.17 doesn't; a head falling at 120 u/s struck from below by the
touch and by a blow at 3.9 m/s (0.6x) bounces up (-120 to +220 u/s, worn 18 to 14.4), at 9.75 bursts. Test 12 (thrown at
a wall) as before: 220 u/s sticks, 400 bursts. `Misc/quakevr/gib_2h_throw_test.sh`: every burst is a thrown one's wall
hit (no held smash or hand hit fired during the two-handed throws).

- **For VR**: toss a head up and tap it with the other hand: it should bounce up; slap it hard: it bursts. Hold a head
  and slam it into a wall or the floor fast: it bursts; press it on slowly: it stays. Punch heads lying on the floor
  (they bounce away unless the punch is fast). Tune with Gib Burst Speed / Head Burst Speed / Gib Bounce.
## Mantle height, one-hand drag by part, shallower dents (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/mantledrag`, 2026-10-20)

- **Mantle Height** (`vr_climb_mantle_height` 18 units; Movement > Climbing, before Mantle onto Slopes). A mantle
  needs a hand pulled down 8 units (mantlePull) and the head this far over the ledge's top (was the fixed 8). At a
  chest-high lip the 8-unit pull already put the head 15 over the top, so the pull was what fired it: leaning up over
  the ledge mantled. 18 is a little later. `Misc/quakevr/climb/mantle_height_test.py` (vrslopes' level top, hands at
  1.49 m pulled down 0.2-0.8 m and held): at 8 the shallowest pull that mantles is 0.30 m (the head 15.3 over the top),
  at 18 it is 0.40 m (head 18.0); 20: 0.45 m, 24: only the full 0.8 m. slopes_test.sh: all 8 tops as before. The
  mantle's debug line (`vr_climb_debug 1`) now prints the head's height over the top.
- **One hand drags by its torso and shoulders only** (`vr_foegrab_drag_onehand` 1; Combat > Holding Enemies > Effect,
  One Hand Drags By: 1 Torso, Shoulders, 2 + Head, 0 Anywhere as before). With one hand alone on a standing enemy, the
  follow and the pull (serverFrame) count that hand only at its torso, shoulders or upper arms (foegrab::oneHandDrags):
  on its legs (legPartAt) it is the one-hand leg pull's, at its head or neck (the neck snap's head zone) the head
  hold's, on a forearm or a hand neither. Two hands on it drag as before. Not dragged, a hand pulled away past the
  break lets go as any hold. `vr_foegrab_debug 1` prints each hand's part and whether it drags; `vr_foegrab_status`
  shows it and the enemy's origin. `Misc/quakevr/foegrab/onehand_drag_test.py` (one hand pulled 0.4 m in 1 s):
  shin, not dragged (the hold broke at 1.32 s); chest, dragged 12.7 units; head, not dragged; shin with 0, dragged
  11.1. leggrab_test.py: pull_solo pulled (1.8 m/s, needs 1.56), pull_solo_weak not (now the hold breaks instead of
  the grunt being dragged), pull_one, pull_both, slow, thigh_half_slow as before.
- **Dents** (migration 168, his config of 2026-10-20): `vr_gore_dents_depth` 3 -> 2.5. His other dent settings
  (`vr_gore_dents` 1, `_size` 1.25, `_max` 12, `vr_ragimpact_dent` 2, `vr_dummy_dents` 0, `vr_decal_melee_blunt_depth`
  1) were the defaults already.
- **For VR**: hang from or stand at a chest-high ledge and lean up and down over it: no mantle until you really pull
  up (try Mantle Height 22-26 if it still fires). Grab a grunt's shin with one hand: walking back no longer drags it;

The cause: AD's zombies (zombie, mummy, zombie knight) have only one death, a gibbing, so AD's wake-up

kill one whole, for good (`VR_AD_ZombieDie`), never gibbed. A map's dormant zombie (lying with AD's ONFLOOR flag until a
trigger fires) keeps `use = wakeup`: beheaded where it lay, the trigger later stood the headless body up (its ragdoll
dropped: solid again) and ran it, in place, through its get-up and run frames. Reproduced headless (`floor` case: 144
warnings from the watch over 15 s, solid 3, frames 133 on), gone after the fix.

  `ad_mon_zombie.qc` / `ad_mon_zombiek.qc`); `VR_AD_ZombieDie` clears its `use`. A living zombie's rising (its fall's,
  a dormant one's) is unchanged.

  dead one; `VR_AD_PainDown` only acts on a living knocked-down one; stealth's animations check `VR_Stealth_Applies`
  (health); id1's and AD's `monster_use` check health. One more of the class fixed: MG's paused path walker
  (`MG_MonsterBeginWalking`, its `use`) walked a monster killed while it stood paused; it returns on a dead one now.
  Statues (Rogue's, `knight_pause`), Honey's trigger spawns and the lavaman take no damage before their use: not
  reachable.
- The watch: `vr_debug_deadanim 1` (Debug > Logging, "Dead Monsters Animating"; developer 1) prints "deadanim: dead ..."
  for a dead monster whose think is its AI's stand/walk/run/attack (or AD's wake-up) again, or whose frame changes twice
  within 0.5 s once 3 s past its death (once: the engine putting a stuck corpse at its death's last frame).
- The test: `Misc/quakevr/deadanim_test.sh <agent> [choices]` (cases stand down getup stagger parry fall floor; KILL=1
  kills instead of beheading): `vr_deadanim_test` 1 report, 2 stagger, 3 parry's stagger, 4 a zombie's own fall,

## Weapons held off their handle collide with the level (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/gripcollide`, 2026-10-20)

The author: a weapon held anywhere but its main handle (by a secondary hotspot, or anywhere on it) passed through walls
and floors. Cause: the walls' test (vr_handpose.cpp resolvePositions, round 21's slide) ran only for a hand with a
muzzle, and a weapon carried off its handle (the hand-off, taken off the floor by a hotspot or anywhere: twohand::carrying)
has none ("no aim"); its shape (modelcollide::weaponShape) was not recorded for it either. Now its shape is its drawn
model in the frame of the carrying hand (as a held weapon's is in its hand's), its tip the carried tip as drawn
(view::carriedWeaponPose), and it slides out of the level as a held one does. Carried with the other hand on it too
(drawn between the hands: carriedInBoth), the other hand is moved by the same push, so the weapon moves as a whole and
both grips stay on it. Held by its handle, with or without the other hand (a hotspot, anywhere: either hand primary),
nothing changed: the holding hand already carried the test. The models' push (vr_model_collide) still skips carried
weapons, as before.

**Measure**: `vr_gun_wall_depth` (the Debug page, "Weapons Into the Walls", by Log Hand Offsets): each hand's drawn weapon, how many of its
sample points are in the level and how deep (lines from the eyes), and how far the walls held the hand out.
`bash Misc/quakevr/gun_wall_test.sh <agent>`: each grip walked into vrtesthall's north wall. Deepest point, before ->
after: by the handle 5.0 -> 5.0 cm (main), 4.9 -> 4.9 (off); handle + other hand anywhere 5.1 -> 5.1 (either hand
primary); hand-off, carried anywhere 13.5 -> 0; taken off the floor anywhere 29.4 -> 0; by the crowbar's blade hotspot
18.5 -> 0; carried with both hands 28.8 -> 0. Pushing against the wall for 60 frames: no hand moves (0.000 units, every
grip). eval.sh --full: 169/177, verdicts as the baseline (one event's offset 39.1 -> 39.0 units, PASS both).

Seen while testing (not changed): an empty hand pushed into a wall is drawn up to 3 cm into it (walls 0 in
vr_debug_hand_offset: the torso-to-hand stop doesn't catch it there).

- **For VR**: take a weapon off the floor by its barrel or a crowbar by its blade, and hand a shotgun off to the other
  hand's grip on its barrel; push each into a wall and the floor (and with both hands on it): it should stop at the
  surface and slide along it, as a weapon held by its handle does, the hands staying where they hold it.

## Prop impacts: the gibs' rule for every prop that breaks (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/propimpact`, 2026-10-20)

The author: extend the gib impact rule to all destructible props (light hits push, medium damage, hard destroy; held
smashes, throws, hand, weapon and melee hits alike). `VR_Prop_Impact` (vr_carry.qc) now takes every kind: a gib goes
to `VR_Gib_Impact` (numbers unchanged), any other prop by `VR_Prop_Kind` / `VR_Prop_BreakSpeed`: intensity = impact
speed / break speed; from 1 it is killed (a crate breaks, an explosive box blows up, in the hand too), from 0.5 it takes
`(2i - 1)` of its full health (`VR_Prop_Full`: max_health, else its health at its first impact), below nothing. Break
speed = `vr_prop_break_speed` (9 m/s, a small crate's 75 health) x `sqrt(full / 75)` (0.5..2.5) x the material's
multiplier; a crate's piece its own `vr_prop_break_piece` (4 m/s).

| Kind | Entities | Before | Now (defaults) |
|---|---|---|---|
| wood | `vr_crate`, `vr_barrel` (auto-placed and mapped), AD wooden/flesh/custom `func_breakable` | blows did weapon damage (fist 10+, 75 health: ~7 punches); Box3D hit from 70% of `vr_crate_impact` 16 m/s: `health * i^2` | blow 9 m/s small (11.4 large), heft-scaled; held smash; Box3D hit from 70%: `(2i-1)` |
| piece | a crate's pieces | burst by any hand touch or blow at `vr_melee_speed`, any damage; thrown: never | 4 m/s touch/blow/held smash; thrown at `vr_crate_piece_impact` 8 m/s (only when thrown); shots and blasts still burst it (1 health) |
| explosive | `misc_explobox`, `misc_explobox2`, MG1 `func_explode` | blows did weapon damage (20 health); Box3D hit at `vr_explobox_impact` 14 m/s blew it up | blow / held smash 8.4 m/s (x1.8) blows it up, half that damages; Box3D as before (>= 1 only) |
| glass | AD glass and ceramic (`func_breakable_vase`, windows) | weapon damage (health often 1) | x0.5: a health-1 vase 2.25 m/s |
| stone | AD rock/brick (style 0, 1, 5), SoA `func_breakablewallwithrubble` | weapon damage | x1.5 (a health-10 wall 6.75 m/s) |
| metal | AD metal `func_breakable` | weapon damage | x1.5 (health 200: 22 m/s, practically shots only) |
| not props | shootable buttons/doors/triggers, SoA `trigger_damagethreshold` (rocket walls), MG3 `func_breakable` (Dimension of the Machine's sinking pillar), `func_vr_target`, dummies | - | unchanged |

Paths: **melee blows** (`T_Damage_VRMelee`: only a hand's blow from `PlayerVRMeleeImpl`, `vr_melee_blowhand`; the
chainsaw's running chain and other melee-kind damage stay as they were): `VR_Prop_BlowDamage`, the blow's `mh_speed`
times stamina times the weapon's heft (`sqrt(damage / a punch's)`: axe 1.41, chainsaw 1.6, slap 0.7) replaces the
blow's damage (no positional or cap); a light blow deals none but still pushes (`vr_melee_push`, by the blow's own
damage); one hit per 0.15 s per prop (`.vr_gib_hittime`). **Held smash**: `VR_Gib_HeldSmash` became
`VR_Prop_HeldSmash` (any kind; a prop's line is extended by its least half-size, its face meets the wall first).
**Thrown/dropped**: `VR_Crate_Impact`, `VR_Explobox_Impact`, new `VR_CratePiece_Impact` route through `VR_Prop_Impact`.
**Piece touch**: `VR_CratePiece_Struck` by the rule (it bursts only from 4 m/s; a slower touch wears it and the nudge
pushes it). `VR_CratePiece_Damage` wears health (shots still burst).

New cvars (Crates page, Breaking, after Breaks On Impact): `vr_prop_break_speed` 9, `vr_prop_break_wood` 1, `_glass`
0.5, `_stone` 1.5, `_metal` 1.5, `_explosive` 1.8, `vr_prop_break_piece` 4, `vr_crate_piece_impact` 8.

**Checks**: `vr_prop_impact_test 1` (Debug > Gore Tests, "Prop Impacts: Tap, Hit, Smash, Throw"), e1m1, god mode: a
small crate, an explosive box, a piece and a rubble-wall stand-in each: blow 0.4x unhurt, 0.75x damaged (crate 75 to
37, box 20 to 10, piece 1 to 0.5, wall 10 to 5), 1.2x broken, 0.75x with the axe's heft broken; piece touch 0.5x
unhurt, 0.9x worn, 1.2x burst; held smash at 2x into the wall breaks crate, box (blows up), piece; crate at 0.75x
damaged; thrown crate 0.6x unhurt, 0.85x 75 to 22, 1.1x broken; box 0.9x unhurt, 1.1x blows up; piece thrown 0.4x
unhurt, 0.75x worn, 1.1x burst, dropped at 1.5x unhurt. AD stand-ins (fields only, no models): vase 2.25 m/s, window
(20) 2.32, wooden (75) 9, metal (200) 22. `vr_smallgibs_test 25` unchanged (13 m/s bursts, 2.17 doesn't, -120 to +220
u/s, 18 to 14.4).

- **For VR**: tap a crate or an explosive box lightly: it only moves; punch a crate hard (or swing the axe): it breaks
  in one or two; a medium punch makes it creak. Punch an explosive box hard or slam one held into a wall: it blows up
  (Break Speed: Explosive). Slam a held crate into a wall fast: it breaks out of your hands. Tap crate pieces: they
  are only pushed; punch them: dust. Throw a piece at a wall hard: dust. In AD maps, vases and windows break from almost any
  blow, stone and metal need hard hits or weapons. Tune with Crates > Breaking > Break Speed and its materials.
## The ragdoll tool (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/ragtool`, 2026-10-20)

His request: a flat-screen tool, in the codebase and on the game's code paths, to see the active ragdoll animations on
a rig of his choice and tweak them interactively. Built as a mode of the game: `-ragtool` (implies -flatscreenmode) or
`vr_ragtool`; usage in RAGTOOL.md. Engine: `vr_ragtool.cpp` (the mode, 24 behaviours as steps of the game's own calls,
the parameter registry of 94 settings in 9 groups, presets, orbit camera, keys), `vr_box3d_ragtool.cpp` (overlays:
part frames, joint limit cones and hinge arcs, ragactive::debugDraw's targets, contacts, centre of mass over the
support's outline; the run's measures), `vr_menu_ragtool.inc` (Debug > Ragdoll Tool and a page per group). Hooks, all
inert with the tool off: V_CalcRefdef (camera), V_RenderView (the debug lines over a flat view), Host_ServerFrame (pause
and step), Key_Event (its keys), VR_MenuRunsGame (the game runs behind its page), the struggle's holds (the physgun's
hold counts as the first player's hand while the tool runs), toolgun::spawnEntryAt (the spawner by entry).

New settings, 1 by default (the game unchanged): `vr_ragdoll_active_{hertz,damping,torque}_{legs,torso,arms,head}`
(the drive per joint group, `ragactive::Channel`) and `vr_ragdoll_limits_{legs,torso,arms,head}` (the joint limits per
group, as the ragdoll is made). `ragactive::tracking` measures the driven joints' mean miss of their targets.

Checks (headless, flat): every behaviour played on a grunt and on AD's death knight, no errors (a fresh subject now
stands 0.5 s before its steps: a just-made AD knight refused `vr_knockdown_test 0` at once). On the death knight the
game itself does not begin vr_ragdoll_act's stagger, throw, flinch and knee buckle, nor its shoves' staggers (`ragact:
... NOT begun (no ragdoll)`), seen not changed; the grunt does them all. The legs' motors off raised the
stagger's mean tracking error from 29.7-31.6 deg (three default runs) to 37.9-39.3; a preset saved, reset and loaded
back (94 settings, the 2 changed restored).

- **Flat (desktop)**: `ironwail.exe -ragtool`; orbit with the mouse, Tab for the page; play each behaviour on a few
  models; Struggle with each Hold, moving the hand; edit a Joint Groups slider and replay; Save and Load a preset.

## AD humanoids: hit reactions (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/addkstagger`, 2026-10-20)

The ragdoll tool saw AD's death knight refuse vr_ragdoll_act's stagger, throw, flinch and knee buckle and the shoves'
staggers. On `next` now (the tool's fresh subject stands 0.5 s first) the stagger, throw and every shove's stagger begin
on all AD humanoids, by their group's chance (death knights 0.12); only the flinch and knee buckle did not: AD's monsters
take damage through AD's T_Damage (AD_Damage), whose hit hook VR_AD_Hit never sent the hit reaction (T_DamageDeal's
VR_HitReact_Hit). Fixed: VR_AD_Hit calls it (before the situational knockdowns, as ours do), and AD's ad_ai_walk and
ad_ai_run take VR_HitReact_Dist (the slow-down, a leg hit's hitch). vr_ragdoll_act's missed flinch now says "no hit
reaction drawn" (a flinch is no ragdoll's). Checked in the tool on the grunt, the knight and AD's death knight, death
guard, fury, sergeant, crossbow knight, rocket, plasma and grenade soldiers, defender and eliminator: flinch and knee on
2 of 12 before (and the fury's flinch), 12 of 12 after, each knee hit's limp logged; in ad_sepulcher a zombie knight
flinches and limps, no QC errors.

- **AD maps**: shoot AD knights and soldiers in the body and the legs: they flinch, a leg hit buckles the knee and they
  limp a step, as id1's grunts do; shove them: they stagger (death knights rarely go down).

## Rotating autosaves, safe autosaving, the death menu

Player feedback: an autosave made in an ambush trapped them (respawn, die again, progress lost without a manual save).

- **Rotation** (vr_continue.cpp `VR_AutosaveRotate`): `vr_autosave_slots` (3) autosaves kept per map. The newest keeps
  the old name (`autosave/<name>.sav`: Continue, the skill menu's Resume, older saves unchanged), the older ones are
  `<name>@2.sav`, `@3`... (their file times kept by the rename). The autosaves queue `save <name> 0 rotate`;
  Host_Savegame_f waits for a save still being written, then shifts the slots (each `.addon` with its save). Every save
  now has a `// qvr_player <health> <armor> <seconds into the level>` context line for the menu.
- **Only when safe** (host.c `Host_AutosaveUnsafe`/`Host_AutosaveWait`; both the level-start and Ironwail's timed
  autosave): not while a living monster is after you (`vr_autosave_safe_alerted`), a living monster in sight is within
  `vr_autosave_safe_radius` (600), or your health is below `vr_autosave_safe_health` (40%) of its maximum. A due autosave
  waits and is made as soon as it is safe; after `vr_autosave_safe_maxdelay` (60 s) of waiting for monsters (one stuck
  hunting you) it is made anyway, never at low health. `vr_autosave_safe 0`: none of the checks. `developer 1` logs
  `Autosave: waiting: ...`, `safe now, after x s`, `made anyway after x s`.
- **Load Autosave** (menu.c `m_autosaves`, `menu_autosaves`): the main/pause menu's row under Continue (shown when
  autosave/ has one) and VR Settings > Saves and Autosaves list the loadable autosaves newest first, two lines each
  (`e1m3: The Necropolis` / `Health 65 Armor 50, 3:12 in, 5 min ago`; an older save without the player line: the time
  only). Inspections are cached by path and file time.
- **Death menu** (`vr_death_menu` 1, `vr_death_menu_delay` 2 s; single player, campaign maps): Respawn (as fire:
  `restart`, the last save with `sv_autoload` 2), Restart the Level (`restart fresh`), then the autosaves. Back: you
  stay dead and fire respawns as ever; it doesn't open again for that death.
- Settings: VR Settings > Saves and Autosaves (also sv_autosave, sv_autosave_interval, vr_autosave_level_start,
  sv_autoload). Debug > Tests > Saves: List the Autosaves (`vr_autosave_list`, `vr_autosave_load <n>`), Open the Death
  Menu (`menu_autosaves death`).
- Tests: 4 level starts with 3 slots leave e1m1, @2, @3 (the oldest dropped); an alerted grunt delays the level-start
  autosave until `vr_test_kill`, health 30 until `give h 100`, a grunt left alive with maxdelay 5: made after 5 s; the
  main menu's Load Autosave > 2nd row loads `@2`, the death menu's 5th row loads `@3`; an old-format `e1m1.sav` lists
  without health, loads, and rotates to `@2`. (Scripts' `kill` respawns at once in Quake: tests die to a grunt with
  `give h 1`. A scripted Respawn prints "Autoload failed!": Host_AutoLoad's load waits behind the script's `wait`s, as
  it always did; not so in play.)

## Body and Equipment (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/bodycustom`, 2026-10-20)

Players: the chest gear too far back (the flashlight hard to grab), the ammo belt too low and sinking over a session,
changing the height breaking the legs until a full Body Calibration. Measured with a new probe, Debug > Views > Log Body
Heights (`vr_debug_body_heights`: twice a second, metres over the body's floor: eyes as calibrated and as learnt
standing, pelvis, knees, ankles, each leg's straightness, the ammo pouch and hip holsters and their offset from the
pelvis, the grenade pouch, the chest holsters from the chest). Mock eyes at 1.70 m.

- **The legs.** No leg calibration exists: the whole body is scaled to `vr_height_calibration` and hangs from the head,
  the legs IK'd to the floor. A Height off from the eyes' real height broke them: Height 1.547 (the test baseline's),
  ankles 0.23 m in the air, legs locked straight; 1.40: 0.37 m; 2.00: knees bent (straightness 0.71) and the body in its
  crouched pose. Body Calibration fixed it only because it measures the height again. Now `vr_body_leg_fit 1`
  (avatar `legFit`): hip-to-ankle lengthened or shortened (0.75-1.3x) so that at the height the headset sees you stand at
  (`hands::State::standingHeight`, Leaning Detection's learnt standing height: rises fast, settles slowly while centred
  and not crouched) the feet reach the floor with straight knees, and the crouch depth is measured from there. After:
  Height 1.547 ankles 0.081, 2.00 straightness 0.94 (clamp), 1.40 ankles 0.16 (clamp; 30 cm off). A Height equal to the
  eyes: unchanged (fit 1). Seated: off.
- **The belt too low.** The holsters and pouches are placed in Quake units from the player's origin (2 units up, Z
  offsets times the Height), the body in metres times the Height and the world scale on `vr_floor_offset`'s floor: the
  taller (or the bigger the world scale, or the higher the floor) the lower the gear on the body. Hip holsters from the
  pelvis: -0.04 m at Height 1.40, -0.13 at 1.547, -0.21 at 1.70, -0.39 at 2.00; ammo pouch -0.00/-0.08/-0.16/-0.23.
  `vr_body_gear_fit 1` (vr_body.cpp `fitToBody`): the old placement taken as on the reference body it was tuned on
  (eyes 1.55 m, the author's; world scale 1.2; floor -22) and scaled to this body about the floor under the box's middle.
  After: ammo pouch -0.075..-0.084 at every Height, hip holsters -0.12..-0.17 (proportional), chest holsters
  -0.02..-0.03 from the chest (before +0.06..-0.27). The author's setup (1.5546 m, 1.2, -22): unchanged (k 1.003).
- **The drift.** A 100 s session (stand, stick walk, walk turning, crouch to 1.15 m and up 5 times, look down 60 degrees,
  a 4 cm slouch for 20 s, straight again): nothing accumulates; every standing phase returns the pouch to the same
  height (0.891 m, -0.086 from the pelvis; 0.895 before the first walk: the feet's stance). The gear is carried by the
  pelvis, which hangs from the head: any lowering of the head (a slouch, the headset slipping down the face, the
  runtime's floor moving) lowers the belt 1:1, and as the calibrated height stayed the reference the knees stayed bent
  (straightness 0.96) for as long as it lasted. With the leg fit the learnt standing height settles to it within ~20 s
  and the legs straighten (1.000); the belt still follows the head, as the body does. Looking down 60 degrees with the
  mock lifts the body 11 cm: the mock pitches the head about the eyes (a real head pitches about the neck, dropping the
  eyes as much), not a bug.
- **The page.** VR Settings > Body and Equipment (replaces Holster Calibration and Ammo Pouch on VR Settings; their
  rows are on it; the body clone is shown while it is open): Height, Legs Fit Your Height, Gear Fits Your Body, Body
  Calibration; Shoulders Back/Out/Up (`vr_body_tweak_shoulders_*`), Torso Back; Belt Height (`vr_body_belt_up`, metres:
  hip holsters, both pouches, the belt torch), Flashlight Forward/Out/Up; the ammo pouch's rows; the holsters' rows
  (chest holsters forward for the chest gear); Reset Body and Equipment. The board in the calibration room was not given
  a line (compiling it needs the id texture WAD, not in the worktree).

- **VR**: set Height a little off (VR Settings > Body and Equipment) and look down: the feet should stay on the floor,
  the knees straight; crouch: they bend. Check the belt (ammo pouch, hip holsters) sits on the belt; try Belt Height and
  Flashlight Forward with the body shown in front of you.

## Earned bullet time (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/earnedbt`, 2026-10-20)

The backlog's "Bullet time as an earned resource", the 1.1 default: bullet time's meter no longer fills by itself; the
damage you deal fills it. `vr_bullettime_meter_mode` 1 (earned, default) or 0 (over time, 1.0's: `vr_bullettime_recharge`
after the cooldown, unchanged). `vr_bullettime_earn_damage` 180: the damage that fills it from empty, six grunts' health
(QC `orig_mon_soldier.qc`: 30 each). `vr_bullettime_earn_active` 0.25: damage dealt while it runs fills at a quarter, so
a fight can extend it a little but not forever. The cooldown (`vr_bullettime_cooldown` 2 s) still blocks a restart; in
the earned mode the meter fills during it too. No config migration: the mode is a new cvar, so every config (1.0's had
only the self-filling meter) takes the default, earned.

Decisions:
- **What counts** (QC `VR_BulletTime_Earn`, combat.qc; called from `T_DamageDeal` and AD's `VR_AD_Hit`): the health
  taken from a living monster (FL_MONSTER, health above 0, not a corpse or a dying one), at most the health it had (no
  overkill), dealt by the player or by something he owns (his missiles, thrown things: `.owner`). Never a corpse's, a
  prop's or breakable's, the training dummy's (it returns earlier), a monster's to another, nor damage whose attacker
  is neither the player nor owned by him (a falling body's); single player only (not deathmatch or coop). A zombie
  knocked down and getting up again counts each time it is hurt (it gets its health back: it is a fight).
- **Kept**: the meter is kept on the player (`.vr_bullettime_spent`, 1 - the level, so 0 is full: a new game's and a
  save from before this), saved with the game, carried to the next level by `parm74` (new; `lastExtSpawnParm` 74). A new
  game, a coop respawn (SetNewParms) and an AD exit's inventory reset start full; a restart after death starts with the
  level's starting meter. The engine writes the field every frame and takes a value it didn't write (a load, a level's
  start) as the meter. Both modes keep it this way.
- **The gadget**: the TIME bar (unchanged look) also shows while cooling down in the earned mode (it fills then), and its
  frame lights for 0.4 s as a hit fills it.

Menus: VR Settings > Bullet Time > Meter Refill (Earned by Damage / Over Time); Advanced > Combat > Bullet Time: Meter
Refill, Damage to Fill, Refill While Slowed (Recharge Time and Cooldown's help say which mode they are for). Debug:
`vr_bullettime_meter [level]` prints the meter or sets it (Debug rows "Bullet Time Meter", "Empty the Bullet Time Meter");
`vr_debug_bullettime 1` prints each hit's refill; test aid `vr_test_hurt <damage>` (the nearest live monster takes it from
a shot of yours; Debug row "Hurt the Nearest Monster").

Test `Misc/quakevr/bullettime_earn_test.sh <agent> [case]`, both pass: **earned**: a new game's meter 1.000; emptied, 300
idle frames leave it at 0.000; `vr_test_hurt 15` on a grunt takes 19 (the shot's body multiplier) and fills 0.106
(19/180), the killing 100 only the 11 left (0.167); five more grunts 0.167 -> 1.000; set 0.4, saved, set 0.9, loaded:
0.400; `changelevel e1m2`: 0.400; running at 0.49, a grunt's 30: +0.041 (a quarter). **classic**: emptied, 300 frames
fill 0.208, a grunt killed adds nothing beyond the time. (Grunts spawned onto a fresh corpse were hurt by the falling
body, uncredited: the test lets each settle.) Not run headless: AD's path (`VR_AD_Hit`).

- **In VR**: fight a few grunts in e1m1 with bullet time empty (Debug > Empty the Bullet Time Meter): the TIME bar on
  the gadget grows with each hit (its frame flashes), six grunts fill it; it never grows standing still. Start it and
  kill: it drains, a kill gives a little back. Save, load, take an exit: the meter stays. VR Settings > Bullet Time >
  Meter Refill > Over Time: the old self-filling meter.
## 1.1 pacing: shell pairs, big monsters' health (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/pacing`, 2026-10-20)

Player feedback for 1.1: with manual reloading, ogres feel too tanky.

- **Shell pairs by default** (`vr_reload_shell_pairs` 1; config row 170 moves a config still at the old 0): the pouch
  gives a taped pair unless only one shell is left or the gun in the other hand (a manual shotgun) has one place left
  in its tube (or none): then a single shell (QC `VR_Reload_Take`). A pair taken elsewhere and pushed into a gun with one
  place still loads one and leaves one in the hand. The super shotgun and the Widowmaker keep their own rules.
- **Monster Health** (Combat > Monster Health; `vr_monster_health*`, vr_mgroups.cpp): each monster's health and full
  health (`.max_health`) times a multiplier, once, as it first appears (`VR_MonsterHealth_Frame`, after SV_Physics'
  edicts: every game's monsters alike, those spawned later too). The QC field `.vr_hpscale` keeps the multiplier, so a
  loaded game's monsters are not cut again (an older save's are, by their full health). The cut is a piecewise-linear
  curve on the full health: 0 up to `_from` 150, then (`_hp1` 200, `_cut1` 10%), (`_hp2` 600, `_cut2` 15%), (`_hp3`
  1000, `_cut3` 20%), flat beyond, capped by `_max` 20%; then times the group's `vr_mgrp_<group>_health` (Monster
  Groups > Health, 1). `vr_monster_health_debug 1` prints `mhealth <num> <class> <group>: before -> after`.
- **Bosses**: the curve applies to the bosses fought by damage (Armagon, the dragon, Hephaestus, the morph, the spear
  knight, the bog lord/gug, the demon prince). Left alone: those killed by a trick or fought in scripted waves/phases
  whose health their code sets as they go (Chthon and Shub in every form, Dawn of the Machine's Chthon and Shub, AD's
  eidolon, ice golem, judicator, mammoth, Nour/vermis, fire top), the training dummy, and anything at 20000 health or
  more (scripted invulnerability).

Verified headless: the reload self-test (`vr_reload_test 9; impulse 125`) 77 passed, 0 failed, with the new cases
(single shell for one place, a pair for two, a pair into one place, the last shell single); every spawnable monster
(`vr_toolgun_spawn_test`) logged: grunts, knights, enforcers, zombies, dogs, scrags unchanged; ogre 200 -> 180,
death knight 250 -> 223, fiend 300 -> 266, vore 400 -> 350, AD minotaur/drole/golem 500 -> 431, shambler 600 -> 510,
Hephaestus 1500 -> 1200, Armagon 2500 -> 2000, super shambler 2000 -> 1600; the exempt bosses unchanged. A saved
ogre (180) loads at 180.

- **In VR**: reload the shotgun from empty (pairs), with one place left (a single shell), with one shell in the
  reserve; fight ogres and a shambler: they should go down noticeably sooner. Combat > Monster Health's examples follow
  the sliders.

## Monster hull sizes first met in play: compiled on the pool (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/hullhitch`, 2026-10-20)

Sweep finding: the first move of a monster whose box size the load did not compile (AD's delayed and triggered spawns,
the test spawner) compiled the world's tree in the frame (`treeFor`'s runtime build, without the disk cache). Now
`moveBox` asks `worldTreeReady`: a missing size is read from the disk cache or compiled (and written) on the pool with
the brush models live edicts can meet, one size at a time (a second waits its turn: the build gate would otherwise queue
its work behind the first's job and report it done), and the monster moves with Quake's own hull until it is ready
(wider, as tall from the same feet: the switch is seamless). Whatever changes `built`'s layout or the slots, a setting's
`prepare`, map changes, shutdown and the hull diagnostics wait for the job first (`joinBackground`). `vr_hull_async` (1;
0: the old in-frame compile), Debug > Tests > New Monster Sizes in Play; `vr_hull_stats` counts them. Precompiling every
class's size at load was not done: it would add load time on every map for sizes most never use.

Headless (spawner 0..11, `vr_profile_hitch`; the machine shared with other agents, so times are noisy):

| Map | Size | Before: frame stall | After: frames over 55 ms from it | Ready after (pool) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ad_tears | 40x88, 28x56 | 1.5-4.7 s, 1.4-1.9 s | none (none over 33 ms) | 2.2-2.6 s compiled; 0.11-0.13 s from the disk |
| ad_sepulcher | 40x88, 28x56 | 0.61 s, 0.58 s | none | 0.79 s |
| ad_swampy | 28x56 | 0.27 s | none | 0.37 s |
| MG3 map5 | 28x56 | 0.25 s | none | 0.36 s |

Load times unchanged (no load-time work added; the runs' differences are noise). `vr_mhull_walktest 8` right after an
ogre and an enforcer spawn on ad_tears (the fallback in use for the first 2.5 s): 0 stuck, 0 in solid, 0 embedded for
both. eval.sh: verdicts unchanged (169/177; four takes' damage moves by 0.1).

- Unrelated, seen on the way: ad_swampy's spawns give 0.1-1.0 s "server other" hitches with either setting.
- **In VR**: on an AD map spawn an ogre and an enforcer with the spawner (or reach a delayed spawn): no stall;
  developer 1 prints `hull: 40x88 ready in play ...`.

## AD's monster spawns: their limbs made as the map loads, the normal-map cache kept (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/swampyhitch`, 2026-10-20)

The 0.1-1.0 s "server other" hitches on ad_swampy were `limbmodel::spawnFrame` (VR_ServerFrameEnd): the late limb
models of every AD kind, one a server frame at 5-27 ms each (skins 2.5, normal maps 4-23, draw lists 2), several server
frames in a slow host frame. Two causes:

- **The load's prebuild missed AD's monsters.** It took the edicts with FL_MONSTER and a model; AD's monsters have none
  (or the placeholder `misc_broken.mdl` that sizes them) until `ad_monster_spawn` sets `self.mdl`, 0.1-0.5 s in or at
  their trigger, so every AD kind went the late way (ad_swampy: 15 kinds, 127 limbs). `kindModel` now takes a
  `monster_*`'s `mdl` (a new engine field, `QVR_FIELD(mdl)`) when it is a precached alias model other than its current
  one, posed with it for the lookups (modelindex set back after).
- **The normal-map disk cache emptied itself every session.** vr_skinrelief's relief maps were stored in
  `cache/normalmaps/` under a second build folder, and `prepare` removes a product's other builds: each removed the
  other's files every session, so nearly every skin normal map (the limbs' too) was made again (786 misses, 40 hits a
  run). The relief maps now have their own product, `cache/reliefmaps/` (`VR_ReliefCacheLoad/Store`); the old
  `normalmaps/5e1ef...` folder is pruned on its own. Warm: 810 read, 0 missed.

Headless, no spawner (`wait300` after the load, each map's own spawns; `scratch/sw_maps.sh`, the machine shared):

| Map | Load before / after | Kinds made late before / after | "server other" frames >= 30 ms before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| ad_swampy | 3.28 / 2.57 s | 15 (127 limbs) / 0 | 14 (max 192 ms) / 0 |
| ad_tears | 4.39 / 3.49 s | 3 / 0 | 4 (max 202) / 0 |
| ad_sepulcher | 3.48 / 2.79 s | 4 / 0 | 4 (max 152) / 0 |
| ad_e1m1 | 1.85 / 1.62 s | 3 / 0 | 3 (max 378) / 0 |
| MG1 mge1m1, MG3 map5 | 1.2 / 1.5, 1.0 / 0.8 s | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (2 of 38 ms, a busy machine) |

The prebuild on ad_swampy makes 214 limbs for 28 kinds (was 87 for 12): 0.5 s with a warm cache, 1.5 s cold (the first
session after this build). With the debug spawner (0..11, not probed without `vr_probe_test_spawn`) only its own kinds
are late, now read from the cache. e1m1 unchanged (17 limbs, 2 kinds).

- **In VR**: on ad_swampy, walk into the first fights: no stutter as the monsters appear; developer 1 prints `limb
  models: N made for K kinds of monster (M of them not yet appeared)` at the load and no `first spawned after the load`
  for the map's own kinds.

## play_gore_fight's cost (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/gorecost`, 2026-10-20)

The perf sweep: play_gore_fight's CPU mean 1.98 -> 2.23 ms against 1.1.0-beta2 (p99 +41%, server +24%), Tracy showing
Box3D's jobs, more awake bodies and contacts, VR_Melee_Sweep and hand collide.

**Attribution.** Mostly not slower code: the scenario took another course.
- *The scenario is chaotic.* Seed 7 (the bench's) on next: 19.1 monsters alive on average, 110.7 awake bodies, 128
  contacts; on beta2 18.6, 93.5, 101.6. The same next build with an empty `--settings` file (one `exec` line more before
  the map) plays beta2's fight exactly (every count equal to beta2's to the decimal) at 1.83-1.87 ms against beta2's
  1.87-1.91: for the same fight next's code is no slower. Seeds 1-6 (`vr_bench_seed`/`vr_particle_seed`, realtime,
  exclusive): beta2 1.94-2.40 ms (mean 2.15), next 2.08-2.62 (mean 2.33, two runs disturbed by the machine); the fights
  where next costs more are those where the ragdoll triggers (the flinch's replacement) knock living grunts into active
  ragdolls: seed 7 has 0.8 living ragdolls on average (9.7 awake parts), seed 6 133 awake bodies against 92.
- *Box3D on the pool from 150 awake (+0.08 ms, the p99 spikes).* That course goes over 150 awake bodies (max 173), where
  the step moved to the pool: the main thread then waited on the workers (Tracy, main thread: `Job blocking wait`
  0.06-0.19 ms a frame) longer than it took to step alone. Interleaved A/B, seed 7, same fight (`vr_box3d_threads 0`
  set in the script, which doesn't change the course): CPU 2.22 -> 2.14 ms, p99 4.44 -> 3.64, server 0.87 -> 0.81 (the
  undisturbed 3 of 4 pairs). The physics scenarios at 150 / 300 / never (2 reps each, the disturbed ones dropped):
  props_500_active 3.40 / 3.17 / 3.23 ms, ragdolls_32_active 2.89 / 2.64 / 2.68, gore_blast_crowd_32 2.65 / 2.82 / 2.77.
- *QC functions looked up by name each step (0.033 ms a frame with ragdolls).* `box3d after callbacks` 0.0011 (beta2)
  -> 0.0339 ms: the new `callBodyHits` (Thrown Bodies) looked `VR_KdTrig_BodyHit` up with `qvr::progs::findFunction`,
  a strcmp scan of every QC function, each step while any ragdoll exists (`callRagImpacts` and `monsterFell` the same,
  less often). Same fight after the fix: 0.0010 ms.
- *The rest, from the Tracy pair (each zone a frame):* `VR_Melee_Sweep` 0.052 -> 0.088 ms (the swept blades' ribs, every
  frame a hand holds something, a blow or not); `hand collide` 0.009 -> 0.028; SolveJoints 0.022 -> 0.042, `box3d
  before step` 0.047 -> 0.072, `box3d publish bodies` 0.024 -> 0.040, particle lighting 0.062 -> 0.094 (the fight's
  content: living ragdolls, more gibs and blood).

**Changes.**
- `findFunction` (vr_progs.cpp) uses the VM's hash table (pr_edict.c `ED_FindFunction`), the scan only before it exists:
  every caller by name gets it, the same indices.
- `vr_box3d_threads_bodies` 150 -> 300 (config 172 moves a config at 150; Debug > Physics Threads From has the row).
- The bench's counts add the awake bodies by kind (`ragdolls_living`, `ragdolls_dead`, `awake_rag_living`,
  `awake_rag_dead`, `awake_gibs`, `awake_props`; box3d::profileAwakeKinds), which is how the course was told apart.

**Result** (bench.sh, play_gore_fight, 3 runs, same machine, same fight as next's): CPU mean beta2 2.028 / next 2.198
/ now 2.048 ms (+1% on beta2), p99 3.33 / 3.75 / 3.46, server 0.701 / 0.840 / 0.783, worst frame 4.6 / 6.2 / 6.9 (one
9.3 ms frame in one run; the others 6.5 and 4.7). eval.sh --full: 169/177 pass, the differences PASS -> PASS at the
0.1 level (they change from run to run).

**Not done.** VR_Melee_Sweep could skip a hand too slow for any blow, but its sweep also keeps the struck thing's
"still in it" time and the pommel's pending blow (VR_Melee_Rearm's), so a gate changes when blows re-arm: the melee
feel, not done without his takes. The bench's seed-7 fight is one sample of a chaotic scenario: a regression in it
should be read against a few seeds (scratch `gc_seeds.sh` did it by editing the script's two seed lines).

## Stagger balance walk: stepping legs, bent knees, flailing arms (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/staggeranim`, 2026-10-21)

His notes: the shove stagger's balance walk glided on tiptoe (feet up and down, legs straight; worst the enforcer, then
the zombie and the death knight), the upper body static, and the grunt always fell, even from one-hand shoves.

**The grunt always falling** was the ragtool, not the balance: its onlooker is notarget, so the subject's `enemy` was
never you and every test shove (`vr_knockdown_test 21/22`, the ragtool's shove1/shove2, ragtest's stagger) was a
surprise (`vr_knockdown_surprise`: unaware, down for sure, balance 0). Test shoves 21/22 now make it aware of you (one
from behind, Push From 180, still is a surprise). In a fight (its enemy you, shoved from the front) the roll decides as
before: one-hand grunt shoves recover 13-16 in 20 (chance 0.45 x 0.6 = 0.27), two-hand 4-6 in 20.

**The walk** (`vr_ragactive.cpp` staggerFrame, `vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_walk` 1; 0 is the old glide, for A/B):
- its pin let down `vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_crouch` (0.08) of its pelvis height (eased in, out with its carry; a
  parry's risen before its handback), and its planted legs reach (0.6) for where their feet were put down: the knees
  bend (the clip's stand pose held them straight);
- a planted foot is held where it was put down (its shin's level motion worked off) while its leg reaches it; it
  steps when its capture-point distance says so (as before) or when its hip is 0.45 of a leg from it; feet step in turn
  (the last step's foot passed over when the other is nearly as far off); the swinging foot rises early to
  `vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_lift` (0.3) of a leg;
- the arms are thrown out to the sides and wheel at their own paces (1.7 and 2.2 Hz), flapping a little
  (`vr_ragdoll_active_stagger_arms` 1).
All four are ragtool sliders (Stagger and Balance). `vr_knockdown_debug` prints a `gait:` line as a stagger ends:
steps, stride, foot lift, knee bend from its stand (least, most, mean), the planted feet's slide (glide), the hands'
rms motion about the shoulders.

**Measured** (ragtool shove1/shove2, 20 each per class; old glide -> walk; one-hand/two-hand where they differ; recovered
staggers): foot lift (u) grunt 2.0 -> 2.6, enforcer 2.0 -> 3.6, zombie 2.0 -> 2.8, death knight 2.4 -> 5.2, ogre 2.3 ->
4.8, knight 1.0 -> 2.7; mean knee bend (deg) 8 -> 14, 9 -> 38, 0 -> 41, 18 -> 32, 8 -> 19, 17 -> 25; glide per step
(u, both feet) grunt 14.5/18.6 -> 11.1/11.9, enforcer 13.9/16.2 -> 11.3/14.0, zombie 21.8/24.1 -> 12.1/13.3, death
knight 15.4/24.0 -> 7.7/10.7, ogre 8.9/15.6 -> 5.6/9.5, knight 18.8/23.2 -> 12.3/13.9; steps 6-8 -> 7-9; arms rms (u)
grunt 6.5 -> 8.5, zombie 6.2 -> 8.2, death knight 1.8 -> 3.7, knight 6.9 -> 8.7, ogre 3.9 -> 4.9, enforcer 1.8 -> 1.9.
Recovery rates the same within the rolls (old/new, one-hand: grunt 16/13, enforcer 16/17, zombie 14/16, death knight
20/18, ogre 19/20, knight 18/16 of 20). Frame strips: `scratch/strip_stagger_before.png`, `strip_stagger_after.png`
(enforcer, grunt, death knight; the camera is the tool's default, small).

**Open:**
- The enforcer's and the zombie's rigs have no real knee: their shin hinge sits at the boot (enforcer z -18.6, zombie
  -19.1, sole about -22), the knee ring of the mesh is on the thigh bone, so their visible leg can only bend at the hip
  and the ankle; their "knee" numbers above are ankle bends. Their animations do bend the knee ring (enforcer
  hip-ring-boot 9-59 deg over its frames). A real knee needs the rig's shin pivot moved up to the knee ring (about
  z -11 on the enforcer) and the rig cache rebuilt: every ragdoll of theirs changes, so not done here.

## Running shoves, two-hand shoves x1.25, the held weapon in the hand (worktree `release`, branch `agent/shovevel`, 2026-10-21)

The author's notes: a shove while running at full speed should carry his speed into it; two-hand shoves 1.25 times as
far; the enforcer's rifle hung at his side through every active-ragdoll state instead of following his hand.

- **Running shoves** (QC `VR_Bash_Hit`; `vr_shove_run_carry`, new, 1; "Running Shove Carry" under "Two-Hand Push"): your
  velocity along the shove (40 u/s and more; less is standing, unchanged) is added to the push's speed after Knockback
  (`vr_push`) and the monster's weight, times its group's Shove Push over its weight (`VR_Push_Mass`), at most all of it.
  Its slide (`VR_Shove_Reach`, the stagger's travel) grows with it. The stagger's travel limit (4 m, `ragdollStagger`)
  is now times `far` (`ragdollstagger`'s new optional 8th argument, at most 2.5): the hands' push over 1 squared (two
  hands 1.12: 1.25) times the run's speed-up (linear, so 160 u/s still falls short of 320's).
- **Two hands x1.25**: `vr_shove_push_twohand` 1 -> **1.12** (distance goes by the push's square: the hop and the slide
  are both by the speed, 1.12^2 = 1.25); `vr_cfg_version` 176 moves a config still at 1 (174 the shoulder charge's, 175 struggle3's). A two-hand stagger was at the
  4 m limit already (its uncapped travel 7.4 m), so the limit grows with the hands' push too (above).
- **Measured** (vrtesthall's grunt, `vr_knockdown_test 22`/`21`, `vr_test_shove_run` for the run, `vr_knockdown_debug 1`
  "carried N units"): two hands 342 u/s, 126 units (the limit) -> 383 u/s, **158** (1.25x); running at 160 u/s: 539 u/s,
  226; at 320: 697 u/s, 295; one hand 239 u/s, 107 (unchanged) -> 555 u/s, 300 running at 320. On vrfiringrange
  (`vr_knockdown_surprise 0`, chance 0.01) a standing two-hand stagger recovers after 156 units; a running one at 320
  gives way at 0.23 s (1 step) and lies 182 units off at 1 s (standing, one that gives way: 101).
- **The weapon in the hand** (`vr_box3d_ragdoll.cpp` `createRagdoll`, `looseHolder`, `weldLoose`; `vr_knockdown_weld`
  1): a living ragdoll's loose piece (the grunt's shotgun, the enforcer's rifle, the knight's and death knight's sword,
  the ogre's chainsaw; any rig's, AD's too) is made where the hand that holds it in the rest pose holds it (the part with
  a vertex nearest it there: the enforcer's and the grunt's left forearm, the others' right hand), not where the frame
  had it, welded to that hand, and weighs no more than it. Before: welded where the frame had it to the nearest part
  (a pain frame: the rifle down at his side, welded to his right forearm). `vr_knockdown_weld 2` (Combat, "Weapon Stays
  in Hand": Where It Was (Old)) keeps the old way for an A/B.
- **Measured** (`vr_debug_ragdoll_gun 1`, new; Debug > Ragdolls' Weapons in Hand: every 0.25 s the drawn weapon's
  middle from its holding part's, beside the rest pose's): the enforcer knocked down, old 14-56 units from his left
  forearm (rest 7.2), now 6.1-7.9; struggling (`vr_struggle_force`) old 20-37, now 7.1-8.6; staggering 6.2-7.3. Grunt
  4.7-8.3 (rest 4.7), death knight 5.5-9.0 (5.5). Knight and ogre: on landing the weld gives a moment (18 and 24 units at
  about 1 s, then back to 3.5-4.4 and 14-16).
- Debug > Tests > Enemy Shoves: "Shove the Nearest, Running, Two Hands" (`vr_test_shove_run 320`).

## Shoulder charge tuning on the author's takes (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/chargetune`, 2026-10-21)

His 18 takes of 2026-10-21 (10 Shoulder Charge: left, right, hands clasped, a gun two-handed, the axe; 8 Not Expected:
runs with the hands out, forward, under the chin, hanging low behind, an axe carried, a slow punch). The old detector
caught 3/10, false 0/8: his tucked hands are only 7-12 units below the head (12 asked), his head-down runs top out at
271-301 u/s (0.85 asked 272), "a gun aimed with both hands" rejected his two-handed gun charge, and "side-on" (the
hands' middle 2+ units to the side) failed with the hands right under the head. What sets his charges apart (the 0.35 s
before contact): the **head tipped down** 10-19 deg (his plain runs 0-6) and both hands at or behind the head's line
(the farther-ahead one at most 0.6 units ahead; his runs 4.8-16). A run with the hands hanging low behind
(`no_shoulder_charge_..._00-31-22`) has all a charge has but the head (0.6 deg): the head's tip is the one sign there.

Now: `vr_kdtrig_tackle_head` 7.5 deg (new), `_low` 12 -> 5, `_speed` 0.85 -> 0.75 (reached within the last 0.25 s: a
replay's or a step's dip at contact no longer loses it), the ahead share of `_reach` 0.6 -> 0.3 (6 units), "side-on"
also when the hands' middle is within 2 units of the head's line, the two-handed gun check gone (an aimed gun is high
and ahead), `_face` 60 deg (the sidestep cone, was fixed), and **`vr_kdtrig_tackle_leniency`** (Charge Leniency, 0.5):
strictness k = 1.5 - L multiplies the least thresholds (turn, low, head, hold) and divides the most ones (reach, face,
the speed's shortfall from sv_maxspeed). Config version 174 moves configs at the old speed and low. Shoulder Charges
stay off by default. New take column `charge_hd` (head tip, the farther-ahead hand, k).

Result: 10/10 caught, 0/8 false at L 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 (L 0: 6/10, its head and drop thresholds 1.5 times).
`eval.sh --full` melee verdicts unchanged (3 rows differ by 0.1 in an offset only). In VR: charge with the head down
and see it fire; run head-up into monsters and see it not; a charge with the head up needs Head Down lower or the
leniency up.

## The enforcer's and the zombie's ragdolls get a knee (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/ragknee`, 2026-10-21)

The staggeranim worker's open point: their shin hinge sat at the boot's top (enforcer z -18.6/-17.6, zombie
-19.1/-18.5), so their ragdoll legs bent at the hip and the ankle. The meshes: the thigh bone is the knee ring (the
trousers' lower part, z -6 to -12.5 on the enforcer), the shin bone the boot (-19 to -24), long triangles between them
(textured as the boot). Every ring vertex follows the thigh in the frames (rms 0.3-1.0 units against 3.7-6.2 for the
shin's motion), so the vertex weights stay as they were; only the joint moved. rig.py's motion fit put the joint at
the boot because the animation stretches the shin (8.3-12.6 units on the enforcer, 4.9-9.3 on the zombie): no rigid
hinge fits anywhere (gap rms 2.9 at the boot, 3.9 at the ring), so the knee is now placed by the mesh.

- `rig.py` flag `'knee'` (enforcer_bones.json, zombie_bones.json, the shins): the pivot is the parent's side of the
  boundary, the ring's lower edge the shin's triangles hang from (enforcer z -11.6/-11.5, zombie -13.4/-14.1); the end
  runs down from there through the boot's top to the capsule's floor (the ankle, not the foot's middle).
- `vr_ragdoll.cpp` seeds: thigh ends and shin pivots at those knees, shins to the ankle, `keepHinge` (the derived axis
  would lean 35-44 degrees off the across-axis on the enforcer's left and the zombie's right, their shins leaning out):
  hinge across him, bending backward only; the rest bends 9-17 degrees backward, so a knee straightens to 3 degrees
  short of straight and folds to 150 (the grunt's and knight's limits). `rigVersion` 2 (the rig cache re-derives).

**Measured** (ragtool, `vr_knockdown_debug` gait lines, shove1/shove2 looped 6 runs each; "knee" is the bend at the
shin hinge from the stand's, least/most/mean deg): enforcer before (the ankle) shove1 -21/102/32, shove2 -23/87/22;
after (the knee) -25/62/10, -29/60/5. Zombie before -34/88/31, -34/92/33; after -4/88/28, -5/77/20. Glide per step
enforcer 12.8/22.1 -> 11.1/16.8 u, zombie 14.2/17.9 -> 10.6/16.9. The animations' own knee (hip-ring-boot, the ring's
edge) bends up to 43 degrees (enforcer) and 42-49 (zombie). Suites, before and after alike: active_test.sh (MONS=8:
deaths, head, off), stagger_test.sh (MONS="8 2", rates, getup: 0 FAIL), decap_test.sh zombie, grab_test.sh (MONS=8
death PASS, shove INFO as before), selfcollide_test.sh overlap (0 deep with self-collision on); no crash or NaN.
Ragtool runs of death, shove1/2, stagger, stagger_fall, struggle, drag (held by the leg), knockdown on both: nothing
under the floor, no explosion. Frame strips (`scratch/rs_before_*.png`, `rs_after_*.png`: shove2, leg drag, struggle):
the legs fold at the trousers' and boot's seam, not at the foot; no tear there.

**Open:** the zombie's foot shows as a long noisy block when his leg is held up (drag, struggle), before and after
alike (not looked into). AD's enforcer (mon_enforcer: shin pivot -16, its ring -10.7), AD's zombie and Rogue's mummy

## Gore sounds (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/goresnd`, 2026-10-21)

`vr_goresound.cpp`: the gore's own sounds, all **placeholders** (`quakevr/sound/vr/gore/ph_*.wav`, synthesised by
`Misc/quakevr/make_gore_placeholders.py`; SOUNDS_OURS.md, Gore, lists each with what the recording should be). Hooks:

- Stump spray: `VR_Decap_FountainThink` (neck and limb stumps) sends a spurt at each peak of its beat (2.2 Hz), as loud
  as the fountain is strong (it fades with it); not on the first pulse (the cut's tear is there).
- Blood streams on the floor (the waterfalls): `vr_bloodstream.cpp` hands each stream landing on the floor (not a thing,
  not a liquid) to `goresound::pour` with its flow; the 3 nearest play 0.6 s splatter grains back to back (fades
  crossed), each grain as loud as its stream flows then.
- Choke: `VR_Decap_Effects` (killed by the cut, or dying: 1.5 s) and a heavy blow to the face (`VR_GoreSnd_FaceBlow`,
  vr_teeth.qc: anything but a slap, hardness at least max(0.5, vr_teeth_hardness), or a killing one), for grunts,
  enforcers, knights, hell knights and ogres (by their head gib). The server mutes that monster's CHAN_VOICE for 0.3 s
  (`SV_StartSoundPitch` asks `VR_GoreSoundMutes`), so its pain or death cry is dropped, and the client plays the choke on
  that same channel (a cry already playing is cut). One choke per monster per 3 s and any choke at most every 0.2 s: a
  refused one mutes nothing, so its cry plays (never both, never neither).
- Tear: `VR_Decap_Effects` and `VR_Limb_Cut` on a cut (not a pop: its burst and squish are there).
- Squelch: a hand's carry stat turning to a gib (client), and `box3d::ragdollGrab` taking a dead body (server).
- Wet steps: pools laid on the floor (`decals::place`, Mark::Pool) are remembered 90 s; a step (30 units walked on the
  ground) on one makes the next 4 s of steps wet, fading.
- Slap: `gore::gibImpact` on a wall or a ceiling, from 80 u/s (faint) to 500 (full).

Each kind has a cap of voices at once (spurt 3, pour 3 streams, tear 3, squelch 2, step 1, slap 3), a gap (spurt 0.08 s,
tear 0.05, squelch 0.2, step 0.15, slap 0.1: within it only one at half the distance or less plays) and a distance it
is heard from; a frame's asks play nearest first, and a full cap's farthest voice gives way to a nearer one. Bullet
time lowers the pitch by half its slowing (0.3x: 0.65). `vr_gore 0` or `vr_gore_sound 0`: nothing (the server sends
nothing, so no cry is muted either). QVR_SVC_GORESOUND 35 carries the QC's events (`goresound` builtin). Cvars:
`vr_gore_sound` 1 (Gore > Gore Sounds, 0..1, extends to 2), `vr_gore_sound_debug` 0 (Debug > Logging); commands
`vr_gore_sound_stats [reset]`, `vr_gore_sound_test <kind> [n] [interval] [spread]` (Debug > Tools, Test Effects). No
config migration (new cvars only).

Tests (headless mock, no sound device: counted as played): 8 grunts beheaded at once (`vr_gore_test_crowd 1000;
vr_decap_test 1`): 1 choke (the 7 others cry), 1 tear (7 rate-limited), 12 spurts of 104 asked (one per pulse), 2
streams pouring 25 grains. `vr_gore_sound_test tear 12 0.06`: 7 played (3 replacing a farther one), 5 capped. 10 slaps
at once: 1. A gibbed grunt by a wall: 4 slaps, 7 rate-limited. Bullet time: pitch 0.60-0.64. `vr_gore 0`: a head cut
sends nothing, its cry plays; the test's 3 tears all "off". Not tested headless: the gib squelch and the ragdoll grab's
(the mock's hand did not take the floor gib). `ad_import.py --check`: 0 of 142.

## The mummy's, AD's enforcers' and AD's zombie's ragdolls get a knee (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/ragknee2`, 2026-10-21)

The ragknee section's open point: Rogue's mummy (progs/mummy.mdl), AD's enforcer (progs/mon_enforcer.mdl, id's mesh:
the defender and the eliminator) and AD's zombie (progs/mon_zombie.mdl, id's zombie: the mummy's mesh x0.833, its seeds
scaled; AD's mummy too) bent at the boot. Their meshes are id's: none shares Quake VR's own enforcer's or zombie's
mesh or rig. AD's deflector (id's enforcer's body) and pyro/fumigator (its build, a tank on the back) share the AD
enforcer's legs (the ring 0.2 units off), so they got the same knee. Measured as ragknee did (`rig.py` fits, per ring
vertex the rms following the thigh vs the shin): every ring vertex follows the thigh (enforcer 0.2-0.75 units against
the shin's 3.9-5.5; mummy 0.2-0.8 against 5.5-6.9).

- `rig.py`'s `'knee'` on the shins of `mummy_bones.json`, `mon_enforcer_bones.json`, `mon_deflector_bones.json`,
  `mon_pyro_bones.json`: knees at the ring's lower edge (AD enforcer z -11.7/-11.5, was -16 set by hand; pyro
  -11.6/-11.5; mummy -9.7/-11.1, was -20/-20.2: the boot), shins to the ankle, `keepHinge`. The AD enforcers' and
  the pyro's hand-set hips are kept. AD's zombie: the mummy's new seeds x0.833, 3.9 down (z -12.0/-13.1).
- The mummy's hips (the motions' fit) sit low and in front of his ring, so his thigh's line leans back past his
  shin's: at rest the knee "bends" 12-20 degrees forward by the bone lines, while the leg he shows (his pelvis's
  corners -> ring -> boot) bends 12-20 back. derive's limits (lower = rest - 3, only if positive; upper = flex - rest)
  then let the knee straighten no further than his stand (already straight as seen) and fold 162-170 from it: his
  (and AD's zombie's) shins have flex 118, folding to about 150 as seen. The enforcers keep flex 150 (rest +10..+24:
  straighten to 3 short of straight, fold to 150, as Quake VR's enforcer). `rigVersion` 3.

**Measured** (ragtool, `vr_knockdown_debug` gait lines, shove1/shove2 looped 6 runs each, the knee bend at the shin
hinge from the stand's, least/most/mean deg; scratch `rk2_tool.sh`): AD defender before (the ankle) shove1 -20/66/14,
shove2 -20/55/4; after (the knee) -28/52/4, -26/48/0. AD's mummy -30/78/20, -55/77/17 -> -15/61/12, -12/62/13. DoE
mummy -25/81/33, -39/72/12 -> -21/63/11, -22/52/4. Glide per step down on all (defender 10.5/20.4 -> 10.2/17.4, AD
mummy 11.6/23.4 -> 8.7/15.3, DoE mummy 10.3/18.8 -> 8.1/13.1). Death, stagger, stagger_fall, knockdown/getup, struggle
and drag (held by the leg) on each: nothing under the floor (lowest part 2.9-11.5 u over it, as before), no explosion,
error or NaN. Suites before and after alike: stagger_test.sh (MONS=14: rates and getup, 0 FAIL, the mummy recovers
4/4 both ways), decap_test.sh monsters (MONS=14: beheaded, ragdoll), ad_active_test.py 212 217 232 255 238 (shove,
getup, neck: 15 PASS, FAILS 0). Self-collision on (selfcollide_test's overlap measure, 4 beheaded DoE mummies and 8 AD
enforcers of the four kinds killed by body/head/arm/leg shots): 0 deep but once (seed 7: one still-awake pyro at
12.7 s, 1 deep; seed 11: 0). Strips (`scratch/rk2_pair_<defender|admummy|doemummy>.png`, before over after: shove2,
leg drag, struggle): the mummies' legs fold at the knee ring now (they stayed straight, bending at the hip), no tear.

**Open:** the mummies' AD runs: `vr_decap_test` beheads the nearest, so AD's mummy was not in the overlap count (the
