## Gore sounds: recordings (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/goresnd2`, 2026-10-21)

The gore's placeholder sounds are replaced by cuts from CC0 recordings: `Misc/quakevr/make_gore_sounds.py` (its `CUTS`
table records every cut; sources, authors and IDs in its header, CREDITS.md "Gore sounds" and SOUNDS_OURS.md "Gore").
Freesound HQ previews (17 used of the 30 listed; every page checked: CC0 1.0) and OpenGameArt's *8 wet squish, slurp
impacts* (Independent.nu, CC0; FLAC, decoded with the engine's libFLAC through ctypes). The `ph_` prefix is gone
(`vr/gore/spurt1.wav`...; `vr_goresound.cpp`'s `kinds`); squelch gets a third variant (OGA `impactsplat04`).

- Picked by listening proxies: per source its 10th-percentile 20 ms floor, its events (onset, length, centroid,
  flatness, tonality), and spectrogram strips of the candidates. Dropped for quality: 345985 (a continuous spray, hiss
  floor -48 dB), 453769 (long sponge squirt, not one pulse), 195952 (0.4 s, too short for a grain), 654044 (a clearly
  human voiced moan), 461217 (floor -33 dB), 565633 (crunching, not a snap), 685654 (not needed), 266890 (bright,
  floor -41 dB), 223965/223966 (223967 is the lowest of the three), 573937 and 670304 (outdoor, low step-to-floor
  ratio), 641046 (a long impact, not a squelch), the OGA files with a tonal slurp (02, 07). 518474 was cut only from
  1.9-4.45 s (a low hum before, a bird-like chirp near 5.5 s). No candidate failed the license check.
- Layered: the tears (a rip, a wet layer, a crack 0.18-0.2 s in), the chokes (a gargle and a weak cough at 0.35-0.4 of
  its peak, then pitched down: 0.85 and 0.9 speed). The sprays (spurt1, spurt3) are low-passed at 2.5 kHz into a lower
  gush, the steps at 3 kHz (their outdoor hiss).
- Levels on make_physics_sounds.py's scale (loudest 50 ms): spurt -13, choke -14, tear -12 (the knee leaves -13.3..-13.9),
  squelch -14, step -16 (step3 -17.3), slap -13 dBFS; the pour grains -18 dBFS RMS. Within 1-4 dB of the placeholders',
  so the kinds' gains are unchanged; the steps are about 4 dB quieter than the placeholders.
- `vr_gore_sound_debug 1` now also prints each file loaded and its length at a map load. Headless (`-Sound`): all 18
  load (none "Couldn't load"), `vr_gore_sound_test` played every kind (stats: all played, none dropped).
- `make_gore_placeholders.py` is kept as a fallback (not shipped; its default output is now `scratch/gore_placeholders`).

**In VR:** listen for the chokes (monster enough? choke1 is a man's gargle at 0.85 speed, choke2 a lower gargle), the
tears' crack (audible over the rip?), the steps (quiet, a little hissy?), and the pour stream's loop (seams every
0.52 s?). `vr_gore_sound_test <kind> 4 0.6` plays each kind round you.

## Spent enemy guns, ledge shoves, shoves that bled (worktree `release`, branch `agent/ledgeshove`, 2026-10-21)

His notes (vrragtriggers_2026-10-21_15-30-02, 15-32-24; and a coordinator item).

- **Spent enemy guns** (`vr_enemy_weapon_depleted_loot`, new, 0; Gameplay > Enemy Weapons, "Spent Guns Stand Out"): a
  single-use enemy gun (`VR_IsEnemyGun`: the grunts' burst rifle, the enforcers' laser rifle, AD's soldiers' guns, AD's
  crossbow) dropped or thrown with its clip empty is marked `.vr_depleted` (`CreateThrownWeapon`). Then no loot pillar
  (bit 31 of the weapon prop's networked id; `vr_lootbeams.cpp`, counted as "spent enemy guns" in
  `vr_lootbeams_report`) and the force grab skips it (`VR_Forcegrab_IsEligible`; so no eligible particles either). A
  hand still takes it. 1: as before. A gun with rounds left keeps both. The ogres' chainsaws (fuel, never refilled) are
  not included: an empty one is still a heavy blade.
- **Ledge shoves** (`vr_knockdown_shove_ledge_over`, new, 0.1; Combat > Knockdowns, "Ledge Carry Past the Edge", and
  ragtool's Shove group with Ledge Topple and Ledge Push): the ledge drive (`box3d` `driveShove`, ledge mode) kept the
  launch's speed (Ledge Push times it, at least 80 u/s) until its middle was past the edge, then let it fly on. Now,
  past the edge, its middle's speed along the shove is eased down (0.06 s) to this times the kept speed, so it tips
  over the lip and drops near the ledge's foot. 1: as before. Ledge Push (0.7) is unchanged, so it still reaches the
  edge as briskly. A new cvar, so no config migration (configVersion stays 176).
  Numbers (vrclimb, `setpos -150 Y 24 0 90 0`, `impulse 244`, `vr_knockdown_test 22`/`21`, the trench's edge at about
  y 190 (+-4), a 192 drop; its pelvis's landing, units past the edge):

  | its middle to the edge | 46 | 22 | 6 | ~0 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | two hands, before (1) | 345 | 358 | 372 | 386 |
  | two hands, 0.3 | 108 | 116 | 110 | 131 |
  | two hands, now (0.1) | 59 | 62 | 64 | 58 |
  | one hand, now (0.1) | 47 | 47 | 48 | 56 |

  Every one fell to the trench's floor (feet 211-213 units down).
- **Shoves that bled**: a shove's damage was already bloodless (`VR_HitBloodless`: no wound, no splash), but the
  knocked-down ragdoll's limbs flung faster than 150 u/s left blood trails and drops (`decals::limbTrail`,
  `vr_ragdoll_blood`) whether it had bled or not. Now a live ragdoll's limbs (knocked down, staggering, getting up, or a
  monster with health left) bleed only once it has bled (`.vr_bloodied`, set by `VR_Wound_Hit` for any hit that is not
  bloodless, a burn, a fall or a liquid; `box3d::limbsBleed`, passed with `ragdoll::publish`). Corpses bleed as before;
  a real hit afterwards (a shot, a blow, a thrown body) makes it bleed from then. Covers one- and two-hand shoves,
  running shoves and the shoulder charge (all knockdowns). `vr_decal_count` now also prints the limb frames that bled
  and those spared. Headless: an unhurt grunt shoved down, 1630 limb frames bled before, 0 after (1754 spared); a
  wounded knight (a shotgun hit first) shoved down: 1151 bled, 0 spared (unchanged).

**In VR:** empty a grunt's rifle, drop it: no pillar, the force grab passes over it, a hand picks it up; a full one
still glows. Shove grunts off the vrclimb trench at different distances: they should tip over and drop near the wall
(Ledge Carry Past the Edge 0.1; raise it if it looks like they hit an invisible wall). Shove an unhurt grunt down: no
blood trail; shoot one, then shove it: it bleeds as before.

**Follow-up (branch `agent/spentsaw`, 2026-10-22): empty chainsaws are spent too.** His call: an ogre's chainsaw out of
fuel (its record's `wi_clip`, the fuel, at 0; nothing refuels it) counts as spent under the same
`vr_enemy_weapon_depleted_loot` (0): no loot pillar, no force grab (so no eligible particles); a hand still takes it, and
it still cuts as a blade. `VR_Weapon_Spent` (vr_wpnforcegrab.qc) decides for both kinds: at the drop
(`CreateThrownWeapon`) and as a running one let go burns its last fuel lying (`VR_Saw_PropSettle`). Headless (e1m1,
`impulse 164`, the grip held, `impulse 220` drops it): emptied in the hand (`impulse 227`, started, the trigger held
until it stalls): no beam ("spent enemy guns 1"), "never force grabbed"; let go running with its last fuel
(`vr_chainsaw_idle_fuel_use 20`): stalls lying, then the same; with the cvar at 1, beamed and "may be force grabbed"; a
fuelled one beamed and "may be force grabbed" as before.

Voice notes 15:15-15:25. New cvars only (no default of an existing one changed, no config migration).

- **Chokes off** (`vr_gore_sound_choke 0` shipped; Gore > Gore Sounds: Chokes): `goresound::send` refuses a choke
  before anything else, so the server never mutes the monster's voice: its pain and death cries play. On, as before.

  `vr_gore_sound`): the Gore page's rows under Gore Sounds.

  step check on the first step into a still-wet pool (the steps after it wet as before). `splash1..3.wav` cut by
  `make_gore_sounds.py` from 531571 (the puddle steps, already credited) with OGA `impactsplat08`/`05` under two of
  them (07 skipped: its tonal slurp), low-passed at 4 kHz, -14 dBFS (splash1 -17: peak-limited). CREDITS.md and
  SOUNDS_OURS.md updated; the 18 other files regenerate byte-identical.
- **Bloody footprints** (`vr_bloodprints.cpp`; `vr_footprints 1`, `vr_footprint_count 8` (1..32), `vr_footprint_fade 1`,
  `vr_footprint_size 1` (0.5..2)): a foot of the posed body (`avatar::skeleton`, which now also gives each foot's toe tip
  and sole height) coming down after it was lifted (> 2.5 cm over the other, back under 0.8 cm: the walk's swing, a
  step turning on the spot) is a step; without the body's legs, every 0.7 m walked, the feet in turn. At a step: the
  floor under the ankle (one trace), then the pools goresound already keeps (`goresound::poolUnder`, now public: 64
  distances) and, not in one, the ragdolls with blood painted on them (`wounds::bloody`) within 22 units: either soaks
  the feet (no print in the blood itself); else a print while any are left, strength 1 down to 1 - fade. The print lies
  on the floor along ankle -> toe, the ankle a quarter of the sole from its heel (6.3 x 2.4 units at size 1, the drawn
  foot's), the left one mirrored. A teleport (setpos, respawn) is not a step (10 frames to settle); water washes.
- **Bloody handprints** (`vr_handprints 1`, `vr_handprint_count 6`, `vr_handprint_size 1`): the gore's blood smeared on
  a hand (`wounds`' `smearHand`, theirs only: a gib taken 4 blots = soaked full, a bloody blow's or the saw's spray a
  little, `vr_gore_hands_test`) fills a 0..1 level. While some is left, one trace a frame per hand from 8 cm behind the
  palm to 6 cm in front of it (the drawn hand's pose); a surface facing the palm is a touch. A new touch, or one slid
  12 cm, at most every 0.3 s, leaves a print (5.6 x 3.3 units at size 1) along the hand on the surface, mirrored so the
  thumb lies on the index finger's side (`HandPose::up`, by geometry, not by hand), using up 1/count of the blood
  (strong over 0.5, then faint). Water washes it.

  strong, worn, faint) and a hand (2 cells), the gore's blood colours, drawn by `printTexel`. The layout is in three
  places (static_assert'ed): `vr_glsl.h` (QVR_DECAL_FUNCTIONS and its retro sizes) and the permanent layer's bake shader
  (`vr_permdecals.cpp`). `MarkOptions` gains `variant` (which cell) and `mirror`. The prints are ordinary decals: the
  same ring (`vr_decal_max`), buckets and permanent layer.
- Debug: Debug > Logs > Bloody Prints (`vr_bloodprints_debug 1`: each print with its ankle and toe or wrist, each

  the body's state, the cost).

Tests (headless): walking e1m1 with bloody feet, 8 prints at the posed feet's touchdowns, alternating sides 5.4 units
apart (the right foot on the right), each 1/3 of ankle->toe ahead of the ankle, yaw along the foot (90 walking +y),
strength 1.00 .. 0.00 by 1/7, cells 0/1/2. Six grunts beheaded, a pool under you, walking out: the feet soaked 3 times by
the corpses' pools, 8 prints, 2 splashes; a bloody hand dragged on the floor: 6 prints then none (blood 0). Cost over

From the author's 2026-10-22 notes (vrragtriggers 01-13 .. 01-22).

particles; Debug > Profiling > Log Next 3 Seconds, also written to `quakevr/profile/framelog_*.txt`): the first head
pop of a session took 16.6 ms on the main thread, 7.9 of it `world+brush`: the world's program with the decals' retro
code (`GL_WorldDecalRetroProgram`), made when the first mark showed (retro is on by default). Now made in the map's
load (`decals::prepare` -> `R_PrewarmDecalPrograms`, the opaque world's variant the settings pick: +7 ms once a
session): the first pop 6.2 ms, a later one 3 ms. The translucent brush models' variants stay lazy (1.6-1.7 s each to
compile here, uncached by the driver: too long for every load; a translucent brush model drawn with marks about still
makes it then). Gore sounds were already loaded in the load; the rest of the first pop (decal buffers 1.6 ms, the
hologram's first message) is small.

from the head): 3700 particles, 2000 within half a metre, 5 views of cover, yet the particles take 0.2 ms of GPU (half
size and the size cap at work; 0.4 ms with half size off). The pop frame adds ~1.4 ms of GPU (wound paint 0.6, gibs'

leads; to capture it in the headset: Log Next 3 Seconds, then punch.

From his notes of 2026-10-22 (vrragtriggers 01-04 to 01-50). Done:

- **Light ammo vs crates.** A prop's own Box3D hit (`.vr_impact`: crates, explosive boxes) counted the whole approach
  speed, whatever struck it: a 0.45 kg magazine (or a 0.04 kg shell) at 14 m/s "hit the crate at 14 m/s", 75 -> 18,
  broken on the second. Now struck by a lighter loose body it counts the approach times twice its mass share (at most 1:
  a crate into a crate, the level, held kinematic things as before; `vr_box3d_step.cpp`). Shells, shell pairs and the
  three magazines also get Throw Damage x 0.25 (`vr_props.inc`; their throw damage on a monster 1.0-1.6). Test:
  `vr_prop_impact_test 2` (Debug > Gore Tests, "Light Ammo Thrown at a Crate"): ammo 75 -> 75, a crate thrown into a
  crate still breaks it.

  called `physicsblast`; patched in by `ad_import.py` (`--check` 0 of 142). Test `vr_prop_impact_test 3`: a crate 48
  units from a 60 blast moved 0 units by AD's, 7.7 by Quake's; now 7.7 both. Other explosion paths audited: Quake VR's,
  MG's and MG3's go through `T_RadiusDamage`; the rest flagged are visual-only death effects (no damage, no push).
- **Magnetic holsters from the hand:** at an empty holster, the bind button binds (or unbinds) the weapon the pressing
  hand holds (`vr_magholster.cpp` wants, `VR_MagHolster_Press`).
- **Two-hand heavy throws:** the mass limit (`throwLimit`, two hands as half the mass) let an 80 kg box leave at 1.4
  m/s and a 40 kg crate at 2.7 whatever the motion. New `vr_throw_2h_heave` (250 J, Physics > Throwing): two hands
  throw at up to sqrt(2 E / mass) when that is more: 80.5 kg 2.5 m/s, 65 kg 2.8, 40 kg 3.5 (measured with

- **Defaults (configVersion 179):** `vr_knockdown_shove_ledge_over` 0.1 -> 0.45; the nailgun magazine's Fit Overlap
  (`vr_prop_overlap_51`) 0.4 -> 0.385; `vr_prop_throw_dmg_49..53` 1 -> 0.25 (new `namedDefaultChanges` rows: prop

## Death menu held, charge contact, leg-drag struggle, heavy AD melee, vial size (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/round1022`, 2026-10-22)

From the author's voice notes of 2026-10-22 (vrragtriggers).

**Death menu.** Cause: his deaths were on Quake VR's own maps (vrragtriggers today, vrfiringrange on 10-20), which
`M_CheckDeathMenu` skipped (`VR_AutosaveAllowed`), and any press within the delay respawned (QC `PlayerDeathThink`).
Now it opens on every single-player map, and the engine holds the respawn: while dead it sets the QC global
`vr_death_menu_hold` (`PR_SetServerGlobalFloat`, pr_edict.c); a press then only sets `vr_death_menu_asked` (the menu
opens at once, release and press again to ask again), never `respawn()`. Respawn (row 1) sets `vr_death_menu_respawn`:
`PlayerDeathThink` runs QC's own `respawn()` (a checkpoint's on vrtutorial, else the restart loading the last save;
a progs without the global: the old "restart"). Back closes it; a press opens it again. `vr_death_menu 0`: Quake's
press-to-respawn. Placement unchanged (in front of the head at `vr_menu_distance`, as the main menu: MENUPANEL "from
head 0 150 0"). `Misc/quakevr/deathmenu_test.sh`: early (a press: "a press asked for it", menu, no SpawnServer),
respawn ("Death menu: Respawn", the restart queued: "a respawn is under way"), vrmap (opens on vrragtriggers), back
(reopens on a press). In a script the queued restart runs after the script's own commands (localcmd), so the reload
itself is not in the log.

**Shoulder charge.** Contact was 8 units plus two frames' run ahead of his box: about 13-17 units between the boxes.
Now `vr_kdtrig_tackle_contact` (2) plus one frame's run: the author's 10 charge takes connect at 3.9 units mean between

## Ammo pouch: each round its own wobble, wobble sliders, bigger grenades (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/pouch2`, 2026-10-22)

Voice notes `vrfiringrange_2026-10-22_12-20-08` to `12-21-57`: the rounds moved as one block; sliders for springiness and
settling; grenades 5-8% and multi-grenades 15-20% bigger. New cvars only, no migration.

- **Each its own** (`vr_ammo_pouch_wobble_each` 1; 0: one spring for all, as before): every slot has its own damped
  spring (frequency 0.8-1.25x, damping 0.75-1.35x, drive 0.8-1.2x, the acceleration turned up to 30 deg about up;
  golden-ratio steps) and a lying one a second, quicker one across it that tilts it (its ends +-0.08). Standing rounds
  (magazines, grenades) lean each their own way; lying ones (the shell pile, the rocket stack) sway with the shared spring
  as a block and slide up to 0.12 off it. Fixed arrays, no allocations.
- **Never through each other or out of the leather** (`solve`, either mode): the rest layout's rules are built once per
  layout change (`restCache`): each near pair's gap and its slopes (magazines), or the capsules' axes where they are now
  (shells, rockets, grenades: pushed apart at their closest points); the inside's 22 edges as lines (convex), each
  round's ends (lying) or its axis/corners at the rim's height (standing: above the rim there is no leather) kept off
  them, the leather giving 0.1 (`wobbleSoft`; its wall is 0.1-0.3 thick); a lying one's ends never drawn nearer each other
  (drawn rigid, they stay inside where they were kept clear). Up to 10 passes, stopping when nothing moved; a 0.02 margin
  (more at Wobble above 1). The block's sway is cut where the walls stop the pile (`blockSway`).
- **Sliders** (Settings > Ammo Pouch, after Ammo Pouch Wobble, which still caps how far): Wobble Each Round,
  Springiness `vr_ammo_pouch_wobble_freq` (2 Hz, 0.5-5, extends 0.2-8), Settle Time `vr_ammo_pouch_wobble_settle` (1.3 s
  to 5%, damping = 3 / (omega t): 0.18 as before; 0.2-4, extends 0.1-10), Intensity `vr_ammo_pouch_wobble_intensity`
  (1, 0-3, extends 0-5: how hard a move drives them).
- **Grenade sizes** (against the held ones, `vr_ammo_pouch_layout`'s `pouchsize` lines): the grenade 0.9 -> 0.96 of its
  held size (+6.7%; 23.0 cm against 23.9), the multi-grenade 0.7 -> 0.805 (+15%; 18.7 cm against 23.2). Five
  multi-grenades need a deeper pouch: frame 4 (grenades) 4.8 x 4.4 -> 5.0 x 5.0 (`make_ammo_pouch.py`, model rebuilt).
- **Cost** (`vr_ammo_pouch_layout`'s `pouchwobble` line, 20 shells shaken hard every frame, fast mode): springs 0.2 us,
  layout 0.5 us, layout + wobble 17 us at Wobble 1 (112 pairs), 28 us at 3; the rules' build 30 us once a layout change.

## Pressing on props: the hand gives (worktree `release`, branch `agent/proppush2`, 2026-10-22)

From his notes of 2026-10-22 (vrragtriggers 01-24 to 01-35), the item agent/proppush left.

- **Cause.** The hands' bodies (the fist's spheres, the reach body of the open hand or the gun, a carried prop) are
  kinematic: pressed lightly down on a crate on the floor they pushed it into the floor regardless, Box3D squeezing it
  between the two (sunk, then shot out sideways or broken). QC's hand nudge of solid props (`vr_carry.qc`) pushed it
  down along the hand's motion too, and lifted it with a hand drawn up off it.
- **Fix (`vr_box3d_press_back` 1, `vr_box3d_press_max` 50 cm; Physics menu, Pressing Props).** Before each step the
  props near the hands note what holds them (`noteBraces`: the level, doors and lifts, fixtures, a stack braced so, three
  deep). A hand's body meeting such a prop against its support pushes nothing (`preSolve` -> `pressHit`; Box3D's
  pre-solve now passes the contact's separation: a local change in `contact.c`, `mesh_contact.c`, `solver.c`, `types.h`)
  and the hand is held back instead (`notePress`: the depth, moved on by the step, taken out of the hand; Gauss-Seidel
  over the contacts). The bodies (`syncHands`, `syncReach`, a carried prop's `follow`) and the drawn hand
  (`VR_SetupViewEntities`, restored for the game like the knocks) are moved back by it; clear of it, eased back at most
  0.6 m/s (a drawn hand jumping is a swing). At the cap, its bodies go on into the prop, still pushing nothing.
  `physicspush` (QC's nudges and blows) never pushes a prop into what holds it (`unbraced`), and QC's solid-prop nudge
  only pushes into the box, not after a hand leaving it. Sideways pushes along the floor are as before (a support
  counts only within ~40 degrees of straight against the push).
- **Test:** `vr_prop_press_test [main|off [cm/s [cm past]]]` (Debug > Gore Tests, "Press Down on a Crate";
  `vr_box3d_presstest.cpp`): the hand lowered onto a crate's top (moved by `vr_mock_hand_to by`, not to a point: the
  view's pushes made the mock chase the drawn hand into the crate), then 40 cm on into it. A large crate, before -> after
  (sink below the floor in units, the crate's fastest): shotgun 4.6 u, 1.7 m/s -> 0, 0 (held back 42 cm); a held plank
  5.2 u, 7.2 m/s -> 0, 0 (held back 42 cm); the empty hand (absolute moves, 13 cm on) 1.5 u -> 0. Test crates lie 15
  units over the floor asleep (lifted out of it as made); the test puts them down first.
- **Not done (budget):** a large crate on its long side climbable from every side; the climbing leg IK on props.
  Open: the empty hand never reaches the crate with the delta moves (the hand case used absolute moves); pressed past
  the cap (50 cm), QC nudges with the mock's clamped hand still kick a crate (rare in play); a held plank pressed hard
  can break a crate by its blows, as before.

**In VR:** press a crate down lightly and then harder with the shotgun, a plank and the bare hand: the hand should stop
on its top (drawn there), the crate stay put; lift off: no hop. Push a crate along the floor and against a wall:
as before along the floor, stopped at the wall.

## Calibration audit: crouched body after calibrating (worktree `dequant`, branch `agent/calibaudit`, 2026-10-22)

Players report a wrong height or a crouching stance after calibrating. Body tracking is not involved for players without
it (no source: `bodytrack::place` returns before touching anything, weights 0); two regressions hit everyone.

**Leg fit on a stuck learnt standing height** (8f101bb5a, "legs fitted to the standing height"). The body's standing
pose and leg length follow the learnt standing height (`LeanSense::standing`, vr_hands.cpp `senseLean`), which sinks only
while the head is within 12 cm under it. It started at the Height setting when the head was low on the first frame (a
start sitting down, the headset on the desk) and rose with a 0.4 s ease on any spike (a jump, tiptoes, the headset lifted
over the head): either left it over 12 cm above the head for the rest of the map, and a Height applied by calibration did
not move it. Mock (Height 1.646, start at 1.0 m, stand at 1.45, calibrate to 1.45, 12 s later): learnt 1.646, legs'
straightness 0.799 (knees bent); a 1 s lift to 1.75: learnt 1.726, straightness 0.773, 20 s later. Before the leg fit
it only fed lean detection. Fixed: from the Height until the head is first over 0.85 of it, from the head then; a new
Height starts it over; it rises quickly only up to 8 cm over itself, slowly (4 s) beyond. Same runs: learnt 1.450,
straightness 1.000; the lift leaves 1.514 and settles to 1.450.

**VR Calibration standing set no height unless the body's result applied** (b46870b93, Stand Tall replaced the height
step). Poses that didn't agree (then Cancel on the page), `vr_setup_skip` or a stop after Stand Tall left the Height as
it was (the default 1.646). Now (the author's call) Stand Tall's eye height is the Height the moment the pose is taken,
standing, 0.8 to 2.4 m (vr_bodycal.cpp, the capture; it also restarts the learnt standing height), as the height step
set it before; an applied result sets it again (the same). The Height before the run's first Stand Tall is kept
(`heightBeforeStand`) for Apply's Undo and history, so Undo still brings back the Height from before the calibration.
Mock: Height 1.646, eyes 1.45, Stand Tall taken, skipped: 1.45 at once; a saved session refitted, Apply (1.5546), Undo:
1.646.

Not changed (plausible, for the author): the tracked legs (`vr_bodytrack_legs` 1 since 56fbea3e1) keep the tracked
leg's bend and put the foot at that share of our leg from our hip, so Meta legs bent at rest bend ours and lift the feet
(synthetic body, its legs 0.908 straight: ankles 13.4 cm up against 7.8, straightness 0.909); his dump's legs are 0.98
straight. Local reference space (no stage) puts the floor the Height under the head at session start, so calibrating
there measures the old Height again (pre-existing). The upper-body joint set (no legs) never turns the torso blend on
(it wants the upper legs).

**In VR:** start the game sitting, stand up, walk around: the body's legs straight, no crouch (Debug > Views > Log Body
Heights: `learnt` near `eye`, `straight` near 1). Lift the headset over your head for a second and put it back: the same
within a few seconds. Run VR Calibration standing and skip after Stand Tall: the Height is your eyes'.

## Prop climbing from any side; climbing footholds on props (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/propclimb`, 2026-10-22)

Voice notes 01-07-09 (a large crate on its long side climbable only from some sides) and 01-24-46 (the climbing leg IK
works on brushes, not on props).

**Cause.** Box3D's hull of the large crate (40 x 40 x 48) has two corners cut at each end (the hull builder's
simplification): lying on its side, the lip over each end ran into a sliver of a steep face (normal z 0.65) instead of
the vertical end. `ledges::propLedges` took the face beyond the lip as falling the whole `minDrop` (32) at its slope,
so the drop "started" 28 units out (over `edgeReach` 16): the two end lips were no ledge, only the long sides were.
(Upright, all four lips held.)

**Fix** (`vr_ledges.cpp`): the drop's start is measured from the prop's own shape (`dropFlare`): how far its points (and
its edges' crossings at the band's foot) reach past the lip between the lip and `minDrop` under it, beside the lip
only. A long slope (a wedge's) still reaches far: no ledge, as before. Lips shorter than 2 units after the bevel lift
(a cut corner's edge) are none.

**Test** `Misc/quakevr/climb/prop_sides_test.sh <agent> [up side sidex up45 side45]`: the large crate climbed from each
side (the player square to it, 20 back; both hands onto the lip and pulled over, prop_climb_test.sh's plays), in five
orientations: upright, on its long side with the long axis along x, along y, upright turned 45 degrees, lying turned
45 degrees (the crate has only two resting shapes, 48 high and 40 high; "on its short side" is the lying one turned 90
degrees, `sidex`). Pass: held and mantled onto, standing on the top.

| orientation | before (sides 0 1 2 3) | after |
|---|---|---|
| upright | ok ok ok ok | ok ok ok ok |
| lying, long axis x | ok FAIL ok FAIL | ok ok ok ok |
| lying, long axis y | ok FAIL ok FAIL | ok ok ok ok |
| upright, 45 deg | ok ok ok ok | ok ok ok ok |
| lying, 45 deg | ok FAIL ok FAIL | ok ok ok ok |

The FAILs were the crate's ends: no hold at all (`vr_climb_probe` listed only the two long lips). `prop_climb_test.sh`
12/12 PASS after.

**Footholds on props** (`vr_avatar.cpp` footTrace, `box3d::propTrace`): the climbing feet's traces were the level's
only (`SV_Move` MOVE_NOMONSTERS skips SOLID_BBOX props, and their boxes don't turn anyway). Each now also casts against
the solid props' Box3D shapes, up to where the level stopped it, and a point in one counts as solid (a tenth-unit
overlap: a ray from inside a hull meets nothing). New setting `vr_body_climb_feet_props` 1 (archived; VR Settings >
Body: Footholds on Props). Headless (`vr_debug_climb_feet 2`, the heavy crate hung on 6 s; two stacked mantled onto):

| case | props 0 | props 1 |
|---|---|---|
| hang (1394 frames) | 46 searches, all none; feet on holds 0 / 0 | 2 face holds; feet on holds 1394 / 1350 (L/R) |
| stack mantle (635 frames) | 18 searches, all none | 6 face, 1 none; feet on holds 333 / 290 |

Feet inside something: 0 frames in all. Cost: 5.0-5.6 traces a search (3 before: the hold found takes the placement
traces), a search at most 0.008-0.014 ms (0.004-0.006 before); the per-frame update median 0.4-0.6 us either way.

**In VR:** spawn a large crate on its side (Debug > Tests > Climbing, `vr_test_spawn 122`) and climb it from all four
sides, also after knocking it about; hang on a large crate (or two stacked) and look down: the feet should press on
its face, not hang.

## Holster Setup: drag and drop (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/holstersetup`, 2026-10-22)

The player-facing way to place the holsters: VR Settings > Body and Equipment (Holster Calibration) > **Holster Setup
(drag and drop)**, the first holster row, marked recommended. `vr_holstersetup.cpp`.

- **Safe:** single player only (refused otherwise, and dead or at an intermission); the game pauses through the runtime
  menu's pause (`VR_RuntimeMenuPause` now also true while it runs: no server frame, no monsters, no physics). Every
  controller button is taken (vr_input.cpp, ahead of everything else), the sticks neither move nor turn.
- **Shown:** each holster's and pouch's zone (the boxes the hands find them by, vr_holsterzones) as a see-through box over
  it, labelled ("Left Chest", "Ammo Pouch 1.50x"); blue idle, yellow hovered (a hand within 1.2 of its size), green held,
  cyan its mirrored pair; the holstered gun, sleeve and pouch models lit up as hovered or held. A panel 55 cm ahead
  (placed on entering) with six buttons and the hints over it.
- **Drag:** a grip with the hand in a box takes it (a tick); it follows only after the hand moves 0.75 units (no
  accidental drags), then its reach point goes where the hand's move takes it, 1:1 in the world: the settings that place
  it are solved for that point (their effect on it probed at the grab, one unit each, then a damped least-squares step
  twice a frame), so the body's fitting, the torso's front and sides and the height scaling are all taken care of. Drag
  6 units down: the hips' reach points 24.78 -> 30.81 below the eyes (`vr_hip_offset_z` 0 -> -3.9). A tick every unit
  moved; near its shipped place it snaps there (a stronger tick). One holster at a time.
- **What it writes:** with Symmetry (`vr_holstersetup_symmetry`, on, archived) a holster's pair's offsets
  (`vr_hip_offset_*`, `vr_upper_holster_offset_*`, `vr_shoulder_holster_offset_*`: the Holster Calibration sliders show
  it), the pair moving mirrored; seated (`vr_bodycal_seated`), the seated layout's (`vr_*_holster_seated_*`). Symmetry
  off: the holster's own new trim `vr_holster_trim_<lshoulder|rshoulder|lhip|rhip|lupper|rupper>_x/y/z` (default 0,
  added to its pair's offsets before they are placed: both standing and seated). The pouches: their own offsets
  (`vr_ammo_pouch_*`, `vr_grenade_pouch_*`, or `_seated_*`). Covered: the six holsters, the ammo pouch (with Immersive
  reloading) and the grenade pouch (with hand grenades); the magazines come from the ammo pouch.
- **Resize:** both grips on the same box: its size times the hands' spread over the spread when the second took hold
  (and it moves with their middle); or one hand holding it and its stick up/down (x e^(0.8 s^-1)). New
  `vr_holster_size_<zone>` (default 1, 0.5-2.5 here): the zone's box and the model (the hip and chest sleeves, the
  pouches; the guns keep their size), mirrored to the pair with Symmetry.
- **Panel:** touch a button with either hand and pull the trigger: Symmetry, Undo (also B/Y), Reset Holster (the last
  held or hovered: with Symmetry the pair to their shipped place, trims 0, sizes 1; without, this one's trim and size
  only, back with its pair), Reset All (the current posture's), Cancel (every setting as on entering), Done (also the
  menu button). Undo steps: each hold that changed something, each reset (64 kept).
- Commands: `vr_holstersetup`, `_done`, `_cancel`, `_undo`, `_reset [all|<zone>]`, `_press <button>`, `_report` (each
  zone's reach point from the eyes in the body's frame, its size); `vr_mock_hand_to <hand> setupbutton <index>`.

Test: `Misc/quakevr/holstersetup_test.sh <agent>` (13 checks, all PASS): enter (paused) and Done; the right hip dragged 6
down moves both hips 6.03 down; a gun put back at the right hip dragged 8 units out holsters at the new place, drops at
the old one, and without the drag drops at the new one; Symmetry off moves the right hip alone (`vr_holster_trim_rhip_z`
3.25); a pinch from 3 to 6 units: sizes 1.00 / 2.00 (Symmetry off), 2.00 / 2.00 on the chest (on); the stick: 2.00 ->
2.50; Cancel puts all back; the panel's Undo and Done by the mock hand and trigger; seated, the seated hips move and the
standing ones don't. `holstersetup_test.sh <agent> shot`: scratch/holstersetup.png (the panel, the hips from the eyes,
the boxes from in front).

**In VR:** from the menu, enter Holster Setup: is the panel easy to read and reach at 55 cm, the boxes clear; grab each
holster (the back ones over the shoulders too) and drag it: does it stay under the hand, does the pair mirror, is the
snap back to the shipped place felt; pinch to resize; Undo, Reset, Cancel, Done; then holster a gun at the new places.
Seated: the seated places change. Not headless-tested: entering from the menu row itself (the same start, the menu
closed and reopened on leaving).

## AD fixes: the Dark Prince, the ogres' chainsaws, flames on the body, the health vial (worktree `release`, branch `agent/adfixes1022`, 2026-10-22; vr_cfg_version 183)

From his voice notes of 2026-10-22 (vrragtriggers 19-47, 19-54; vrstart 19-31).

- **The Dark Prince** (`monster_dprince`, AD's progs/mon_dprince.mdl) took none of the humanoid ragdoll triggers: it was
  in the Bosses group (vr_mgroups.cpp, mislabelled "demon prince": every trigger 0, no push), not among the active
  ragdoll classes (vr_box3d_ragdoll.cpp), with no VR_AD_Mon setup (QC vr_ad_monsters.qc: no knockdown get-up, head
  zone, parries, corpse health) and not in vr_struggle_classes. It already had a rig (AdDprince: the death knight's
  mesh, frames and seeds). In AD it is no boss: AD's FGD calls it a "Mini Boss!" (as the baron, which is in Death
  Knights), but its code is a plain monster's (ad_monster_start, 400 health, BBOX_TALL as the death knight, no boss
  flags, no script or wave; placed in none of AD 1.80's maps). Now a Death Knight (group hknight; its health
  multiplier that group's), active (knees as the knights'), set up as the death knight (VR_Knockdown_SetupReverse 223,
  212, 243, 224; head 7 32 7; melee, armour), and it struggles: `monster_dprince:1.3:1:400` (the death lord's, a little
  stronger). It keeps its own sword (AD's w_dprincesword.mdl, its gib): no sword drop (a follow-up if he wants one).
  Tests: ad_active_test.py 256: shove (staggered, down), get-up (243-224, standing), neck snap (loose, 36-119 deg), as
  the death knight's; struggle_test.py ad_dprince legpull/legdrag: it struggles (Claw leads the leg pull, as the death
  knight, whose verdicts there fail the same, grunt-tuned, way).
- **AD's chainsaw ogres drop their chainsaws**: the nail ogre (`monster_ogre_flak` and AD's `monster_ogre` code:
  progs/mon_ogre.mdl, id's mesh, the chainsaw its own piece, vertices 20..51) and the hunter ogre (`monster_hogre`:
  progs/mon_hogre.mdl, 210..332) drop Quake VR's chainsaw as Quake VR's ogre does (QC VR_AD_DropChainsaw, from
  VR_AD_Dying: VR_DropOgreChainsaw); vr_monstermods.cpp hides it in their death frames (112..135; 154..187), AD's gib
  throws no second one (its first gib, when the chainsaw: none; the grenade launcher kept). The mace and hammer ogres
  already drop theirs; Freddie's chainsaw is his arm (no tool); the fishing ogre is scenery. Test: killed each
  (vr_test_kill 1): "adogre: ... drops its chainsaw", "the chainsaw (32 / 123 vertices) hidden in 24 / 34 death
  frames", the dropped progs/v_chainsaw.mdl lies there.
- **Flames on the body**: VR_Burn_OnBody's points were a fat line's hit (4 units out) or, missed, the point clamped
  into the bounding box (a box's side: well in front of a thin body); the player's flames, put by the Quake model or
  the box, and spread along the body's tangent plane, sat off the body drawn in the headset. Now: every point is put
  onto the model's surface (new builtin modelanchor: the nearest point of any entity's .mdl as drawn, a ragdoll's as
  its parts carry it; no box fallback while there is a model), and each flame keeps an anchor on that triangle
  (modelanchorpoint) so it moves with the animation between fits; a player's flames are put on, and every think fitted
  to, the body's shapes as drawn (VR_Burn_OnYourBody: mapflametouch's nearest shape, its part: a hand or arm's flame
  goes with the hand), the shapes kept built while the player burns (VR_Burn_MapFrame). Debug > Burning Tests: "How It
  Burns" (vr_burn_test 4) also prints each flame's distance off the surface; new "Set Yourself on Fire" (13) and "How
  Far Your Flames Sit Off You" (14). Numbers (a death knight, 4 flames): standing, between fits, at most 4.6 units
  (measured at an arbitrary frame: the think is 20 Hz, the body animates and steps between); its corpse 0.0; you
  (mock headset) 0.0 on the body shapes. Open: a running monster's drawn model lags its server origin (client lerp of
  its 0.1 s steps) while the flames are placed by the server's: if he still sees them ahead of a running monster, the
  flames need the client's lerp (a client-side attachment).
- **The health vial's held offsets** (his Held Object Offsets: his slot 63, progs/health_5.mdl, Grip Mode 2: in the
  palm; nothing else of the slot differs from the defaults) are the defaults: vr_props.inc slot 62 (cvars _63). The
  migration (vr_props.cpp takeShippedSlots, from migrateConfig for configs below 183): the slot takes its defaults when
  free or already the vial's (each key left at its own default); a slot of another model is kept; the vial claimed
  before by another slot, nothing else set, is freed. Checked with a 182 config: vr_prop_id_63 progs/health_5.mdl,
  vr_prop_grip_63 2, the old slot 58 freed; vr_struggle_classes the new default.

Defaults: vr_struggle_classes + `monster_dprince:1.3:1:400` (183 row); vr_prop_id_63 "" -> progs/health_5.mdl,
vr_prop_grip_63 0 -> 2 (takeShippedSlots). configVersion 182 -> 183.

## Shoulder charge 3: body contact, run-up, standing tall (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/charge3`, 2026-10-22)

From the author's voice notes of 2026-10-22 evening (vrragtriggers 19-37 .. 19-44).

**Contact.** Cause: QC tested Quake's 32-wide player box against the monster's QC box, while the engine lets the two
bodies meet much deeper: the player is `vr_hull_ent_width` wide against monsters (16 with the defaults) and both
boxes are inset `vr_body_monster_inset` (4) a side (vr_bodycontact.cpp). Face to face the bodies meet 16 units nearer
than QC's boxes touch, so even at `vr_kdtrig_tackle_contact` 0 it fired a body's width early. Now the engine reports
the real gap (`bodycontact::levelGap`, QC builtin `bodygap(player, monster)`: the pair hull world.c collides with), and
the charge connects when that gap is within `vr_kdtrig_tackle_contact` plus this frame's run, the monster ahead within
60 deg of the run and at his height. Measured on his 10 charge takes (replayed at his leniency 0.2; `vr_kdtrig_debug 1`
prints the contact line, now with the body gap and the gap from his chest and waist line to the model as drawn along
the run, `hitmodel_any`): before, bodies 19.6 units apart (18.5..20.9), his head 29.4 from the dummy's middle, chest to
model 18.3 (about 58 cm), leading shoulder (0.18 m ahead of that line) 12.6; now bodies 2.1 apart (0.2..3.7), head 11.9
from its middle, chest to model 0.4, the shoulder 4.7 into it (touching). Head ahead of the origin at contact: 0..5
units (no roomscale offset to speak of); the monster's box against its model: the inset covers it.

**Run-up.** `vr_kdtrig_tackle_runup` (1.5 s, Shoulder Charges > Run-Up): he must have run at the least speed (Least
Speed, scaled by the leniency as before) for that long; dips under 0.25 s and jumps keep the run, the bounce off a
charge ends it. Not scaled by the leniency (the slider's value is literal). His 10 takes have run-ups of 0.26-0.60 s
(each starts about 130 units from the dummy): all 10 fail it, as a sprint begun near the enemy should. Defaults keep
1.5 s as he asked; the eval's charge set at the defaults reads 0/10 caught for that reason (10/10 with
`vr_kdtrig_tackle_runup 0`). New takes with a long run-up, or `vr_kdtrig_tackle_runup 0` in eval.sh's charge replay,
would make that set meaningful again.

**Standing tall.** `vr_kdtrig_tackle_stand` (0.8, Standing Tall): his head's height over the floor at least that share
of his calibrated standing eye height. The engine writes `.vr_stand` from each move (vr_server.cpp: the head over the
origin less `vr_floor_offset`, over `vr_height_calibration` in units; seated or flatscreen 1). His 10 charges connect
at 0.91-0.95: all pass. New take column `charge_rs` (run-up so far, standing share).

**His defaults** (configVersion 184; 183 is another branch's): `vr_kdtrig_tackle_push` 1.25 -> 1.3, `_knock` 152 ->
148, `_leniency` 0.85 -> 0.2, `_bump` 100 -> 120, `_contact` 2 -> 0, `vr_footprint_count` 8 -> 16. Checked: a config at
182 with the old values moves, a custom leniency (0.7) stays.

**AD plasma blasts.** Cause: AD's radius damage throws props with its own damage (physicsblast), and the plasma bolt's
splash is 20 (a rocket's 120): within 60 units only, a crate 48 units off didn't move. Now `VR_ADGun_BlastPush`
(ad_import.py patch on `ad_T_RadiusDamage`; `--check` 0 of 142) throws with `vr_ad_plasma_push` (70: Rogue's plasma
blast; AD > Plasma Blast Push) for an AD plasma bolt's blast, when more than its own. `vr_prop_impact_test 3` now also
does an AD plasma blast and Quake's of 20: the crate 48 units off moved 0.0 -> 12.8 units (a 60 blast: 7.7).

**Gibs underfoot.** `vr_smallgibs_stomp` (1) and `_stomp_speed` (200 u/s; Small Gibs > Pop Underfoot): landing (a
jump, a drop) at that speed or faster pops the meat and brain chunks under his feet (within 12 units of their middle,
at his soles; not teeth, not one in a hand) as a shot does (`VR_Gib_Burst`). Checked once per landing in
PlayerPostThink. `vr_smallgibs_test 26` (Debug > Gore Tests > Popped Underfoot): 5 lying under him, an 8-unit drop
leaves 5, a 64-unit drop 0.

eval.sh: melee verdicts unchanged (six rows differ by 0.1 in an offset).

**In VR:** charge a grunt after a long run: your shoulder should meet its body, not the air before it. A sprint begun
a couple of steps away, or a crouched charge, does nothing. AD Plasma Gun next to crates and bodies: they fly. Jump
onto small gibs and brain chunks: they pop.

## Item Pickup Mode; running legs; handprints (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/pickupmode`, 2026-10-22; vr_cfg_version 185)

His approved asks of 2026-10-22: his handprint count as the default, the legs stepping as often as the footprints at a

**Handprints** (configVersion 185; 186 is another branch's): `vr_handprint_count` 6 -> 8 (his config). Checked: a
config at 184 with 6 moves to 8, a custom 12 stays.

**Running legs.** The prints follow a person's stride at speed (0.55 m + 0.19 s, 0.6..2.2 m: the prints2 section); the
legs capped their cadence at `vr_body_step_rate` (2.2) steps a second, half as often as the prints at a run. Now the cap
rises at speed to that same cadence (`avatar::personStep`, shared with the prints; wading slows it as before) as far as
`vr_body_step_run` says (new, 1; Advanced VR Options > Body > Running Cadence, 0..1.5; 0: the cap alone, the old walk exactly). The stride is
the same, so the planted foot keeps up better (it slid back at 0.8 m x 2 steps/s against the ground's ~12 m/s; now
x 5.2). Measured with `vr_bloodprints_info` (vrtesthall, 2.5 s straight, world scale 1):

| | prints a second | legs before (`vr_body_step_run 0`) | legs now (1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| walk, 200 u/s | 3.97 | 1.98 | 3.57 |
| run, 320 u/s | 5.15 | 1.98 | 5.16 |

(The walk's legs count 9 touchdowns to the prints' 10 in the window: one step's phase.)

**Item Pickup Mode.** VR Settings > Playing > Item Collection's two rows (Carry Ammo and Health, Auto-Collect) are one
switch, `vr_menu_pickup_mode` (a menu wrapper, not saved, as Turning Mode: shown as the settings are, sets them):

(`vr_carry` 0, Auto-Collect left as it is). Under it **Backpacks Too** (`vr_carry_autocollect` 1/2), dimmed unless the
mode is Auto-Collect (the page rebuilds when the mode changes). Advanced VR Options > Carrying and Throwing > Carrying
keeps its detailed rows. Checked: a config with `vr_carry 0`, autocollect 2 shows Vanilla; Auto-Collect then gives 1/2,
Immersive 1/0, Auto-Collect again 1/2 (backpacks remembered), Vanilla 0/2. `vr_menu_path_check`: vrcalibration 0
missing, vrtesthall 0 missing (no board names the old rows). SETTINGS.md updated.

## Cheap scorch marks, on by default (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/scorch`, 2026-10-23; vr_cfg_version 186)

The flamethrowers' scorch marks (`vr_adgun_fx_scorch`) were off because each new mark made the live decals' grid again
(`buildWorld`: records, buckets, upload), and with the permanent layer twice: as it came, and 0.1 s later as it baked and
left the ring. Now a scorch is baked straight into the permanent layer (`MarkOptions::bakeNow`, vr_decals.cpp `add`):
the same stamp `bakeSettled` would have baked a tenth of a second later (a scorch neither spreads nor darkens, so it
looks the same), never live, so the grid is not touched at all. Live as before where the layer can't take it (a runtime
brush, the frame's bake budget `vr_permdecal_bake_max` spent, a brush entity). With the layer off (`vr_permdecals 0`)
they stay live, three a spot at most (a fourth within 6 units on a surface facing the same way is not added: the stream
held on one spot makes the grid again only as it moves on). `vr_decal_count` says how many were baked at once.

**Default** `vr_adgun_fx_scorch` 0 -> 1; migration row at 186 (a config at 0 moves to 1, a custom value stays). Menu help
(AD Guns > Flamethrowers' Look > Scorch Marks) updated.

**Measured** (`scratch/sc_flame2.sh`, e1m1, AD flamethrower held on the wall and arch by the start, 2400 frames logged in
fast mode, `--exclusive`; "heavy": 64 spreading pools live in the ring first):

| case | scorches | grid builds | CPU mean / p99 / max ms | GPU mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before, off, hold (720 frames) | 0 | | 0.89 / 2.22 / 6.2 | 1.17 |
| before, 1, hold (720 frames) | (few) | | 0.93 / 3.63 / 7.6 | 1.53 |
| before, heavy, off | 0 | | 1.02 / 2.35 / 7.6 | 1.28 |
| before, heavy, 3 | (~50) | 2 a scorch | 0.96 / 2.35 / 29.6 (a particles stall) | 1.22 |
| after, heavy, off | 0 | 5 | 0.97 / 1.88 / 7.5 | 1.19 |
| after, heavy, 1 (default) | 17 baked at once | 7 | 0.98 / 1.94 / 5.9 | 1.20 |
| after, heavy, 3 | 52 baked at once | 6 | 0.93 / 2.40 / 7.9 | 1.21 |
| after, sweep across walls, off | 0 | 0 | 0.88 / 1.96 / 9.0 | 1.14 |
| after, sweep, 1 | 14 baked at once | 0 | 0.89 / 2.11 / 7.3 | 1.16 |
| before, heavy, 3, layer off | 44 live | | 0.84 / 1.79 / 5.0 | 1.22 |
| after, heavy, 3, layer off | 12 live | 14 | 0.85 / 1.50 / 5.7 | 1.21 |

With scorches on, the frame is the same as off (within run-to-run noise, 0.05 ms); no decal scope reaches a frame's top
three; the layer's flush stays under 0.1 ms. The old "1.2 -> 6 ms" did not reproduce here even before the change: the
ring is small with the layer on (marks bake after 0.1 s), so each rebuild was cheap in the mock; it was a 30-frame log
right after the stream started (swap and scene stalls in its top scopes). The rebuilds per scorch are gone anyway: they
cost more with a full ring (128 carved holes live, drying gore) and in the headset.

Look: `scratch/sc_eyeup.png` (scorch 3 held 10 s on the arch over the start: lit, and fullbright). Most of the stream's
scorches land on ceilings and arch undersides (the flames drift up).

Migration (`scratch/mig_test.sh`): a 184 config with `vr_adgun_fx_scorch "0"` -> 1, with "2" -> 2 (both now 186).

**In VR:** hold the flamethrower on a wall, the floor and a ceiling for a while, then sweep it: the scorches build up
where the fire licks, and the frame stays smooth (Debug > Profiling > Log Next 3 Seconds if it doesn't).
## 1.1 sweep leftovers: plank sweep, leggrab, slams, the reload suites (worktree `dequant`, branch `agent/sweepfin`, 2026-10-23)

- **legsweep `plank_lr` "no contact" (real).** Since the prop impact rule (2026-10-20) a held crate plank swung into the
  shins at 6 m/s (1.5x the piece's break speed, `vr_prop_break_piece` 4) breaks at the grunt's box (vr_carry.qc
  `VR_Prop_HeldSmash`), short of its legs and before the engine measures the sweep, so the sweep found nothing in the
  hand. With 3.25 m/s needed to sweep and 4 to break, a plank sweep was all but impossible. Now a prop that breaks in the
  hand (its edict freed or its model gone) is followed on by the hand's own move for 0.1 s (`vr_legsweep.cpp`
  `lostProp`): it breaks and sweeps. One let go of or thrown is not followed. legsweep 16/20 -> 17/20 (the plank swept,
  fell to its right); the other three are the known backward-fall shapes (this run: shotgun_toward, sword_hilt and
  laser_lr, across 21.5 against 19.6 along; nailgun_lr passed).
- **leggrab (first run since the struggle changes): 13/17 -> 17/17, stale expectations.** `pull_solo_weak` (1.4 m/s,
  one hand) now pulls: One-Hand Pull is 1 since his configVersion 175 (was 1.3), so one hand needs 1.2 m/s like two; the
  case now pulls at 1.07 m/s (not pulled, the hold breaks). `pull_left`, `thigh_half`, `pull_both_weak` failed the
  fall's shape at the trace's end: a downed grunt still held by the legs struggles (vr_struggle, his feature) and
  squirms its feet back out of the hands and slews aside (thigh_half's head 2 units aside at 0.2 s, 24 at 1.4 s; feet
  10.8 towards you at most, 2.6 at the end). The fall is now judged as it lands (the trace line nearest 0.3 s: its head
  against the pull, more than aside) and the feet by their most towards you; the end's facing verdict is still printed.
- **ragimpact slam (harness made deterministic; the weak blows are by his numbers).** The case ran on the wall clock:
  2 to 8 strikes of 10, or the hand missing the head, by the machine's load. `ragimpact_test.py` now runs on fixed
  frames (`RI_REALTIME=1` for the old way). On fixed frames: 4 strikes at 2.6-3.2 m/s, 4.1-6.4 damage each, health
  30 -> 5, head worn 22 of 104: not killed, not popped. With `vr_struggle 0`: 10 strikes (1.5-3.4 m/s), killed, worn 45.5.
  The struggling grunt (held by the head: pry, squirm) keeps its head from striking on most slams (the hold's lag stays
  2.6-4.8 units, under the grip guard's 6); not fixed. "Three slams kill and pop" is out of reach of his Impact values: a
  held head strikes at 2-4 m/s (the hand's 5.7 m/s in the mock), and with `vr_ragimpact_damage` 0.08, curve 1.5 about 4,
  head 1.5, 32.7 kg behind it, a 3 m/s strike deals ~5; killing a 30-health grunt in three needs ~10 a strike (4.3 m/s),
  popping its head (0.65 x 160 = 104) in three needs 35 a strike (about 8.5 m/s, past the 40 cap's reach). Options for
  him: count a held part's strike at the holding hand's speed into the surface (the hand drives it), ease the struggle
  while the holding hand swings fast, or raise Impact Damage / lower Head and Limb Health. Left for his call.
- **contact 23 PASS, gunshape 24 PASS, 0 FAIL** (first runs since the regfix/pouch/press changes).
- **reload_test.sh: 109 PASS 2 FAIL -> 111 PASS, 0 FAIL (stale placements).** "A pair held near the open chambers
  doesn't refuse a hit from below": at 0.7 of the way along the gun the pouch's pair now lies 3.1 units from the port,
  inside Port Leniency 3.15, and loaded on arrival (nothing left to refuse); held at 0.8 it is 3.4 off and the hit from
  below shuts it, 0 loaded. "A prop held in the other hand knocks the nailgun's magazine out by its surface": the held
  head's shape stopped 2.10 units from the magazine at the case's 4 units (Hit Reach 2; 1.7 when written); from 3.5 off
  it knocks it out at 1.8 units, the fist from as far off and the head's 6-off near miss still don't.
- **Not done (budget): the knight's and the ogre's welded weapon giving on landing** (`weldLoose`: Box3D's weld at its
  60 Hz constraint, the substep cap 72; the loose piece meets the level only) and **the stagger tests' failures under
  load** (stagger_test.sh's cases are batched on fixed frames already, but `cost` times frames with `--exclusive`). Neither
  reproduced here.
- eval.sh: canary and full set verdicts unchanged (169/177; 3 rows differ by 0.1 damage, run to run).

**In VR:** swing a crate's plank through a grunt's shins: it should break and sweep him down. Slam a held grunt's head

## Fuel tanks lying about; one back tank for every fuelled gun carried (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/tankhose`, 2026-10-23)

His voice note (vrmelee-recording_2026-10-23_01-06-09): the pyro's flamethrower and the fumigator's poison sprayer lying
about always have their tank beside them, joined by a visible hose (the player's hose system) and a Box3D rope; the tank
is a prop a hand can drag but not force grab, and dragging either drags the other. In a hand the tank is on the back
(as before); dropping the gun drops the tank with it; holstered guns get a hose to the back tank; several fuelled guns
carried share one back tank, the last held one's.

- **The tank lying about** (QC `vr_ad_enemyguns.qc`, "Fuel tanks"): `CreateThrownWeapon` (every gun made lying about:
  a player's drop or throw, a monster's death drop, the toolgun's spawner) calls `VR_FuelTank_Attach`: a fuelled gun
  gets a `vr_fueltank` entity, model `progs/vr_fueltank.mdl#6` (red) or `#7` (green), `vr_rigid` (a Box3D prop),
  `.vr_prop_mass` `vr_adgun_tank_mass` (3 kg), carried by a hand (`VR_Carry_Setup`; no `FL_FORCEGRABBABLE`: no force
  grab). Placed off the dropper's back (a player: 10 units behind his origin, his velocity, `.owner` him for a second so
  it leaves his body), behind a monster, or beside the gun (any other maker: the spawner, an older save's gun). Gun and
  tank name each other by `.vr_fuellink` (saved with the game); the tank's `.owner` is its gun after that (Box3D's
  contact filter: they never collide, the rope holds them). The tank thinks every frame and goes when its gun is no
  longer its gun lying about (taken into a hand, removed, capped, freed: `modelindex` 0), or `vr_adgun_tank_world` is 0.
  `VR_FuelTank_Frame` (StartFrame, every 0.5 s) gives a tank to any fuelled gun lying about without one (an older save,
  a tank removed by the toolgun).
- **The model** (`vr_adgunart.cpp` `makeTank`, `adguns::tankFile`): the back tank's own profile (6 cm round, 27 cm tall,
  a neck under it, a valve) turned as an alias model, 12 sides, 336 triangles, a 64 x 16 skin (the colour, a hazard
  band, metal), round its body's middle; the writer of the gun variants (`writeMdl`, split out of `makeVariant`).
- **The rope** (`vr_box3d.cpp` `syncFuelRopes`, each step after the toolgun's joints): each tank and its gun found
  again from their `.vr_fuellink` (a saved game, a new world, a body made again when a hand carries either: its joint
  made again); a Box3D distance joint between their origins, slack up to `vr_adgun_tank_rope` (0.9 m; or as far apart
  as they are when it is made, plus 2 cm), no spring. `box3d::forEachFuelRope` lists them (the hose, the info).
- **The world hose** (`vr_adtank.cpp` `setupWorld`/`stepWorld`): each rope within 15 m of the eyes (the nearest 8) a
  hose from the tank's outlet to the gun's inlet, 22 Verlet points, as long as the rope plus both ends' reach from the
  bodies' middles (never stretched by the rope), falling and lying on the world (`verlet::collide`), the player's cord
  and colours; left as it lies once both ends have stayed still for 90 steps. A listen server's (it reads the server's
  ropes).
- **Carried** (`vr_adtank.cpp`): one tank on the back while any fuelled gun is in a hand or a drawn holster; its colour
  the gun last taken into a hand (both at once: the main hand's), kept while that kind is carried. Each hand's gun has
  its hose through the hip or shoulder clip as before (no more two tanks side by side); each holstered one
  (`view::holsterGun`) a hose straight from the tank (the torso and arms kept out). `vr_adgun_hose_holstered` 1 (0: the
  hands' only). The mirror image draws them all.
- **Settings** (VR Settings > Combat > Enemy Weapons > Arcane Dimensions' Guns): Holstered Guns' Hoses, Tank Lying
  About (`vr_adgun_tank_world` 1), Tank Rope (`vr_adgun_tank_rope` 0.9 m), Tank Weight (`vr_adgun_tank_mass` 3 kg). Debug
  > Tests > Arcane Dimensions Monsters: Poison Sprayer Lying With Its Tank (`vr_ad_test 158`), Kick the Nearest Fuelled
  Gun (159), Fuel Tanks Count (150). `vr_adgun_hose_info` now also prints the back tank, every carried hose, and the
  world: the server's tanks, fuelled guns, pairs, orphan tanks, guns without a tank, ropes (joined), and each rope's
  most, the distance apart and its hose.
- **Tests** (`vr_ad_test 150`..`160`, `vr_ad_enemyguns_test.qc`; one `vr_ad_test` a frame: it is a cvar read once a
  frame), e1m1, headless; scripts `scratch/t1.sh`..`t7.sh`:
  - drop from the hand (151, 153): 1 tank made off the back, 1 pair, 0 orphans, rope joined, 0.40 m apart; the back
    tank gone. Taken again (155): the tank goes the next frame, 0 tanks, the back tank back.
  - two guns in the hands and two holstered (151, 152, 156): one back tank (variant 7, the sprayer, taken last), three
    hoses (the left shoulder holster isn't drawn: no hose); the main hand's dropped: 1 world tank, the back keeps 2.
  - save and load with a tank lying about: 1 tank (not 2), its rope joined again; `changelevel e1m2` holding the
    sprayer: 0 world tanks, the back tank on; dropped there: 1 pair, joined.
  - a dead pyro's drop (`vr_test_spawn 232; impulse 241; vr_test_kill 1`): its tank made behind it, 2 pairs with the
    spawner's sprayer, 0 orphans.
  - kicked at 700 u/s (159): the rope held them within 0.92 m of 0.9 (in flight), 0.80 at rest; removed (157): its
    tank went the next frame. The tank carried in a hand (160) lifted the sprayer: 0.88 m apart, joined.
  - `vr_ad_test 71` (each AD gun dropped): 9 passed, 0 failed, 2 tanks, 2 pairs. `ad_import.py --check`: 0 of 142.
  - cost: a resting world hose isn't stepped (0.002 ms a frame for two); a moving one about 0.01 ms; the rope sync one
    pass over the edicts a step (an int read each).
  - pictures (worktree `scratch/`): `tank_world.png` (the sprayer lying with its tank and hose; a pyro's drop),
    `tank_carried.png` (one back tank, hoses to two hands and the hip holster), `tank_drop.png`, `tank_carry.png`.
- **For him in VR**: drop a flamethrower and watch the tank fall off the back; drag the tank by hand (the gun follows)
  and force grab the gun (the tank trails it); the hose's look lying and swinging; the holstered guns' hoses and the
  one back tank's colour with two guns; Tank Rope's length.
- **Not done / notes**: the world hose doesn't collide with props (the world only), and is a listen server's only (a

## Mini bosses: toughness against ragdoll cheese; Death Fury swords, zombie knight blade, crossbow bolt, toolgun bosses (worktree `release`, branch `agent/minibosses`, 2026-10-23; vr_cfg_version 187)

The author's notes of 2026-10-23 (vrmelee-recording 01-09-55, 01-10-59; vrragtriggers 01-24-49 .. 01-39-21).

- **Toughness, per monster group** (Combat > Monster Groups, a "Toughness" block on each group's page, and a page each
  by action): four new settings, `vr_mgrp_<group>_kdscale` (every chance to knock it down times this: the shove's and
  bash's, the ragdoll triggers', the hits' unbalancing knockdown, the stomp's, the leg sweep's; a sure one, over a ledge
  or unaware or from behind, by this chance too: QC `VR_KD_Scale`, `VR_KD_SureRoll`; the engine's leg sweep rolls it),
  `_downtime` (its own timer, `vr_knockdown_time_min`/`_max`, and `vr_knockdown_keep_max` and each hit's and hand's keep,
  times this: `VR_KD_DownScale`), `_getup` (its get-up's frames' speed times this: QC `VR_Knockdown_Interval`, the
  engine's active get-up `ri.fps` and the blended get-up's interval) and `_snapkills` (1: the neck snap kills; 0: its
  neck holds: the crack, softer, and `vr_foegrab_necksnap_tough` of its full health as damage, 0.25; it fights on in the
  hands, QC `VR_FoeGrab_NeckSnap` returns 2 as the dummy's). Every existing group 1, 1, 1, 1 (unchanged).
- **Two new groups** (the death knights' settings otherwise): **Mini Bosses** (`miniboss`: kdscale 0.5, downtime 0.5,
  getup 1.5, snapkills 0): AD's Dark Prince (`monster_dprince`), the minotaur (`monster_minotaur`, out of Giants: it was
  never knocked down, no ragdoll triggers, no neck snap), the justice knight (`monster_justice`, AD's normal judicator,
  and `monster_baron`, its old name: the author's "Justice Knight"). **Elite Knights** (`eliteknight`: kdscale 0.72,
  getup 1.25, downtime 1, the neck snap still kills): the death fury and the death sergeant (my call: the neck snap kills
  them; they are commoner than the mini bosses).
- **Active ragdolls**: the minotaur and the justice knight (and baron) added to `vr_box3d_ragdoll.cpp` activeClasses
  (their rigs were there: AdMinotaur, AdJustice). ad_active_test.py now includes them (215, 231) and sets
  `vr_mgrp_miniboss_snapkills 1` for its neck check.
- **Measured** (vrfiringrange, AD's data): a two-hand shove's chance, Dark Prince 0.07, death knight 0.13, death fury
  0.09. Forced down with 4 s timers: the death knight's get-up due at 4.00 s, rising over 2.97 s; the Dark Prince's due
  at 2.0 s, rising over 1.98 s. The Dark Prince's neck snapped: "its neck holds", 88 damage of 350.
  ad_active_test.py 215 231 256 216 201: 15/15 PASS.
- **The death fury's swords floated as a ragdoll**: every loose piece of a rig was one loose bone, welded to the part
  nearest the middle of them all (between its two swords: its pelvis). `SeedTable::loosePerPiece` (QVR_AD_RIG_SPLIT,
  the fury's rig): one loose bone per piece; `Rig::looseInHands`: each welded to the forearm nearest it in the rest pose
  (its left sword hangs by its hip there). Now: "welded to its forearm_l", "welded to its forearm_r".
- **The zombie knight's corpse kept its blade** (it drops it as a weapon now): no death frames to hide it in (its falls
  are its knockdown's). `SeedTable::looseKept` (QVR_AD_RIG_KEPT): its blade a loose piece though no frame hides it, held
  (welded to its right forearm) while it lives, gone from its dead ragdoll (killed down, or beheaded or cut: the existing
  rules for loose pieces). rigVersion 5 (the rig cache).
- **The death fury's head gib could not be resized while held**: the author's config had all 64 Held Object slots
  claimed (`vr_prop_id_01` .. `_64`), so `progs/h_dfury.mdl` got none (props::claimSlot: -1). 80 slots now; slot 65
  (index 64) ships `progs/h_dfury.mdl` at Size 0.65, a head's mass (configVersion 187 gives it to older configs).
- **The AD crossbow's bolt held another way** (the off hand, a grip taken where the hand met it): the bolt was laid along
  the shot computed from the hand's controller and the slot's own hold, not the drawn gun. It lies along the shot only
  while that is within 3 degrees of the rail (`railShotCos`), else on the rail (`vr_adcrossbow.cpp` boltPose). Built,
  not tested in a run (the mock has no off-hand grip of a two-hand gun to aim).
- **The rocket soldier's dropped launcher** holds 4 rockets (`vr_adgun_rocket_ammo` 4; 5 before vr_cfg_version 187).
- **Toolgun bosses**: AD's boss judicator (`monster_judicator`) and ice golem (`monster_icegolem`) wait for their map's

  spawner names them first and uses them after (`VR_AD_DispenserBossPrepare`, `_Wake`); the toolgun's live spawn
  (`AD_SpawnLive_Finish` -> `VR_AD_LiveBossStart`) names one and runs its spawn function again, then wakes it. What AD

**Suggested, not applied** (rare, strong humanoids; AD's own health, before Monster Health's cut): the death lord
(`monster_death_lord`, 400, the fury's and the sergeant's: Elite Knights); the stone golem and the drole (500 each, the
minotaur's: Giants, never knocked down now; Mini Bosses if they should go down at all). The justice knight has 600; the

## Toughness for the death lord, golem, drole (worktree `release`, branch `agent/tough2`, 2026-10-23)

The Mini bosses' suggestion, approved by the author ("assuming they can be active ragdolled"). Group membership only:
no setting's default changed, no configVersion bump.

- **Death lord** (`monster_death_lord`, 400): Death Knights -> **Elite Knights**. It already was an active ragdoll.
- **Stone golem** (`monster_golem`, 500) and **drole** (`monster_drole`, 500): Giants -> **Mini Bosses**, and both made
  active ragdolls (`vr_box3d_ragdoll.cpp` activeClasses). Both rigs were already there (AdGolem: a humanoid's pelvis, chest,
  head, arms and legs, 105 units tall; AdDrole: two legs, two raised scythes, two lower claws hanging from its hips) and
  both already had QC knockdowns (their deaths backwards, `vr_ad_monsters.qc`). The drole is a biped, so it is not too
  beast-like to be a Mini Boss. In Giants they were only ever pushed (shove 0.03, no triggers, no lift, no neck snap,
  no sweep); now they get the Mini Bosses' settings.
- **The golem's get-up is blended from the floor** (`ActiveClass::blendsUp`, the golem's alone): when its body rose
  through its death played backwards, the pelvis lagged the get-up by 20-30 units (the minotaur's lags 13), and it lost
  the get-up and slumped on the first try, twice in three runs (`riseLost`: 1 m). A stronger pin did not help
  (`vr_ragdoll_active_getup_pin` 5: lost both tries). Its shove, stagger and fall stay active, and it then gets up
  blended, like a ragdoll that is not active.
- **Giants** has no members now. It is kept so its settings' names stay, and its menu help says "no monster now".
- **ad_active_test.py**: now covers the golem (222, spawned 160 ahead, because at 64 the second golem stood on the first
  one's corpse: "no room to stand"; its get-up checked as blended) and the drole (226). Run on 222 226 259 215:
  12/12 PASS. With the shipped `vr_mgrp_miniboss_snapkills 0`, the golem's and the drole's necks hold (108 damage of
  431 each).

**In VR:** shove, sweep and stomp a stone golem and a drole. They go down half as often as a death knight (the shove's
base 0.12 x 0.5; as Giants it was 0.03, with no sweep or ragdoll triggers). The drole rises with its body; the golem staggers and falls with its body, then blends up. Twist their necks:
they survive. The death lord is a little tougher to knock down and gets up faster; its neck snap still kills.

From the author's voice notes of 2026-10-23 (vrfiringrange 01-16-39 and 01-18-00, vrragtriggers 01-28-41, vrstart
01-23-46, vrtesthall 01-47-31, vrmelee-recording 01-14-52).

  ragdoll head bone's own, with the eyes where they are this frame and the bone's whole turn (pitch, yaw and roll). There
  is no smoothing and no turn limit. Your own head's turns and steps are left out; only the eyes' spacing is kept, turned

## Armed grunts (experimental; feature branch, 2026-10-23, worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/armedgrunt`)

His request: a grunt whose weapon can be any weapon you can use, held as the weapon's prop and fired the way you fire
it (same projectiles, effects, sounds, damage path), so it can be disarmed. Stages 1-4 done and part of 5 (below).

**What it is.** `monster_vr_grunt` (QC `vr_armedgrunt.qc`; fields and hooks in `vr_armedgrunt_defs.qc`): its spawn
function picks the weapon, then becomes a grunt (`classname` `monster_army`, `.vr_ag` 1): ragdolls, knockdowns, hit
reactions, decapitation, limb gore, holding, shoves, hulls and every grunt table in the engine treat it as one. Map key
`weapon` (WID_*; -1 fists; 0/unset: the pool), `weaponflags`. Toolgun: Monsters > Armed Grunts (the pool, fists, axe,
sword, crowbar, chainsaw, shotgun, super shotgun, nailguns, launchers, thunderbolt, the grunt's and the enforcer's
rifles; `vr_toolgun_packs.inc`, appended so the old numbers stay). FGD regenerated.

**The model.** `progs/vrgrunt.mdl` (`Misc/quakevr/make_vrgrunt.py`): Quake VR's soldier.mdl with the gun's 116
triangles dropped and its vertices (463..548) kept, so the numbering, frames, skin and rig are the grunt's
(`modelmeta::Id::VrGrunt`, the grunt's seed table in `vr_ragdoll.cpp`, `vrgrunt.` a monster file; its limbs build).

**The held weapon.** An entity of its own (`vr_ag_weapon`, the weapon's record in `.weaponinst`, SOLID_TRIGGER for the
hands, MOVETYPE_NONE) drawn with the weapon's model, so the engine draws it as a lying weapon is (Weapon Offsets' model
transform at its origin: the hand). Every server frame it goes to the grunt's right hand as the server poses it
(vertices 32, 26, 31), along the line the hidden gun has in that frame (vertices 497/545 to 498/514, its roll from 529
over 496): the animations' hands close round it as they did round the rifle. Melee weapons lie along that line the other
way. Aiming, it points at the target; a shot kicks it back (2.5 units, 9 degrees, 0.15 s); a melee blow swings it
(raised 60 degrees, down through 90 more in 0.4 s). Two engine helpers through existing builtins (the VR builtin range
is full): `modelanchorpoint` with an anchor x of -2-n is vertex n as drawn (`hitmodel::vertexPoint`);
`weapondrawnpose(e, 0, 6)` is the muzzle of the weapon model e is drawn with (its Muzzle anchor and offset).

**Firing: your code.** `VR_AG_Shoot` sets the grunt's hand fields as a player's would be (`handpos`, `handrot` aimed at
the target, `muzzlepos` from the held weapon, `weapon`, `weaponflags`, the record) and calls `W_FireShotgun`,
`W_FireSuperShotgun`, `W_FireSpikes`, `W_FireSuperSpikes`, `W_FireGrenade`/`W_FireMultiGrenade`, `W_FireRocket`/
`W_FireMultiRocket`, `W_FireProximityGrenade`, `HIP_FireLaser`, `W_FireLightning` (plus Quake's beam for it),
`VR_FireBurstRound`/`VR_FireGruntGun`, `VR_FireEnforcerRifle`; melee: `W_FireAxe`, `W_ChainsawMelee`,
`HIP_FireMjolnir`, `W_FistMelee`, a gun's butt `W_GunMelee`. Their haptics, casings and kicks go to clients only and
do nothing for a monster; the player animations (`player_shot1`, ...) are never called. Damage to players times
`vr_agrunt_damage_scale` (0.5) in `T_DamageDeal`; to monsters it is the weapon's own (monsters' stock values, as
`VR_WpnDmg` gives a non-player).

**AI.** `CheckAnyAttack` sends an armed grunt to `VR_AG_CheckAttack`: the grunt's clear-shot test and chances by
range per weapon (the thunderbolt only near, the shotguns near, the nail guns near and middle, the launchers middle),
fire frames shoot1..9 (one shot in shoot5; the burst rifle shoot5..7; nail guns, thunderbolt and laser cannon one a
frame in shoot4..8), aimed a little behind a moving target and up to `vr_agrunt_aim_error` (3) degrees off. Explosive
weapons back away from a target nearer than 160 (rocket launcher 190) units and club one within 60. Melee weapons and
fists run in and swing (the shove frames) within 52 units. Its own run frames (`vr_ag_run1..8`) do the backing off and
the walk to a weapon; the grunt's pains end in the grunt's run, so `VR_AG_CheckAttack` puts it back on its own.

**Ammo.** The weapon's record's clip (your reloading clip sizes; 20 for one with none), `vr_agrunt_reserve` (2) clips
more (the grunt's and enforcer's rifles: their clip only). Empty: a reload (the grunt's unused load frames,
`vr_agrunt_reload_time` 1.5 s); nothing left: it throws the gun away. Dying (gibbed too) it drops the weapon with its
rounds; its backpack holds the reserve (none: the grunt's 5 shells).

**Disarming and re-arming.** A blow of `vr_agrunt_disarm_damage` (10) or more within 10 units of its gun hand (16 on
an arm), a knockdown, or your empty hand closing on the weapon (`vr_agrunt_disarm_yank`: through the weapon's
handtouch it becomes a lying weapon and `wpnthrow_handtouch_ent` puts it in that hand) knocks it out. Disarmed it
fights with its fists and, with `vr_agrunt_rearm`, goes for a usable weapon lying within `vr_agrunt_rearm_range` (384)
in sight, not spent, when you are not nearer to it than it is (one at its feet: always), takes it up (load frames) and
fights with it. Settings: Combat > Armed Grunts (Experimental) (and the pool's weights `vr_agrunt_w_*`).

**Tests** (vrtesthall; Debug > Tests > Armed Grunts): `vr_agrunt_test 1`, every weapon hunting you for 5 s: 17 passed,
0 failed (damage to you at 0.5: fists/melee 37-47, shotgun 38, super shotgun 56, nailgun 79, super nailgun 155,
grenades 72, rockets 155, thunderbolt 227, laser cannon 115, proximity 40, burst rifle 29, laser rifle 21; the
grenadier sometimes kills itself with its own grenade). `vr_agrunt_test 2`: reload (8 shots, 1 reload, clip 8),
disarm by a hand hit (the shotgun lying with 8), re-arm (1 pickup), drop on death (8 in it): 4 passed.
`vr_agrunt_test 3` with `vr_mock_hand main 0.1 0.72 -1.2 65 0 0` and `+grabmain`: the shotgun in your hand, the grunt
empty-handed: PASS. `vr_knockdown_test 0` on a row: the super shotgun drops (2 in its clip), the grunt gets up with
its fists. Save and load: the three grunts' weapons 1.4-2.1 units from their hands after the load and after their AI ran.
e1m1 and normal grunts unchanged (their hooks return at once without `.vr_ag`). Rows of them: `vr_agrunt_test 6-9`.

**Left.** No IK: the arms keep the grunt's rifle animation, which suits two-handed guns in most frames; one-handed and
melee weapons are held in the right hand with the left hand on nothing. True IK would be per-bone turns on the client
as `vr_hitreact.cpp`'s kicks are. No muzzle flash of the held weapon on clients (`weaponfired` draws none for a monster
hand): a dynamic light (EF_MUZZLEFLASH) and your weapons' gunsmoke at its muzzle. Arcane Dimensions' guns and the
Super Axe's special are not in its arsenal (their fire is AD's/MG3's own code). An idle grunt doesn't walk to a
weapon; only in a fight.

**In VR:** spawn Armed Grunts from the toolgun (Monsters > Armed Grunts): check the weapon sits in its hands while it
runs and shoots, a rocket hurts about half, shoot its gun hand with the shotgun up close, grab its weapon out of its
hand, kill one and take its gun (its rounds in it), knock one down. Combat > Armed Grunts for the damage and the pool.

### Armed grunts: polish (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/armedgrunt2`, 2026-10-23)

- **Hands on the grips** (`vr_agrunt_ik` 1; client, `vr_hitreact.cpp` armsNow, layered through kickInstance's bone

  vrgrunt.mdl drawn alive finds the held weapon nearest its right hand (vertices 32/26/31, within 28 units) and bends
  each arm by two-bone IK (upperarm + forearm, the elbow kept on the animation's side): the right hand to the grip (the
  weapon's origin), the left to its first Grip hotspot (Weapon Offsets; a Cup: under the right hand; none: hanging by
  its side, elbow back). Every weapon in the arsenal has a Grip hotspot, so all are held two-handed, melee ones too

  `vr_agrunt_ik_info` prints the solve now.
- **Muzzle flash on the held weapon**: `weaponfired(prop, -1)` after each shot; `vr_weaponfx.cpp` monsterFired sees a
  weapon model (its slot) and draws that slot's own flash (size, time, an AD gun variant's flash model and feel) at its

- **Arcane Dimensions' weapons** (with AD's data): the soldiers' guns (WID 20-28, their own `VR_ADGun_Fire*`), the

- **Launchers fired safely** (`vr_agrunt_blast_safe` 1): the round's burst predicted (`VR_AG_BlastPoint`: a rocket's
