## Shoulder charge: hands above the chest; crates break from fewer blows; Vanilla pickups (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/charge4`, 2026-10-23; vr_cfg_version 189)

From his notes of 2026-10-23 (vrmelee-recording 01-01-34, vrragtriggers 00-54-11, vrtesthall 01-44-55 and 01-45-50).

### Shoulder charge: hands above the chest

- **Cause.** His new charges hold the hands a bit above the chest: 1.5-4.4 units below the eyes, under Hands Low (5,
  times the strictness 1.3 at Leniency 0.2: 6.5). Two more missed on the head's tip (9-10 deg against 9.75) and on
  turning side-on only in the last 0.1 s (the turn was part of the held pose).
- **Fix.** The pose is now the tuck (hands below the head, close, not reaching ahead, head down), held
  `vr_kdtrig_tackle_hold`; side-on (`vr_kdtrig_tackle_turn`) is asked for only as the two meet (`vr_kdt_charge_sideon`;
  not yet: no strike spent, the next frame may be). Defaults (config 189): `vr_kdtrig_tackle_low` 5 -> 0.5,
  `_head` 7.5 -> 5, `_turn` 50 -> 60, `_runup` 1.5 -> 0.5 (his); `VR_KDT_CHARGE_AHEAD` 0.3 -> 0.4. His not-expected
  runs are kept out by the head (0.3-3 deg) and by the turn at contact (55-58 deg).
- **Takes** (the kit's replay, run-up 0): expected 14/22 -> 22/22, false 0/15 -> 0/15, at the defaults and at his
  Leniency 0.4 / Stand 0.75. Missed before: left 01-00-37, -41, -48, -53; right 01-00-14, -17, -24, -27.
  (`scratch/charge_sim.py` replays the recorded measures offline for a threshold sweep.)

### Crates break from fewer blows

- **Cause.** The press fix (agent/proppush2) moved the drawn hand back on a prop and restored the game's hand, but kept
  the offset on the game's muzzle (`VR_SetupViewEntities`). The muzzle is the far end of a melee weapon's line (QC
  `VR_Blow_Points`): held back it lagged the hand (the first blow 5.3 m/s for a 6 m/s hand), then caught up at once as
  the press let go, a blow at 2-3 times the hand's speed (18.2 m/s: a crate broken by one).
- **Fix.** The game's muzzle never carries the press offset (drawn hand only), as before the press fix. The sinking
  fix itself is untouched (the bodies and the drawn hand are still held back).
- **Test:** `vr_prop_strike_test [down|ahead [m/s [strikes]]]` (`vr_box3d_striketest.cpp`): the main hand struck into
  the nearest solid prop at that speed, again and again (it steps up to it, slow glides in between), until it breaks.
  `scratch/strike_run.py` plays the matrix (fist, crowbar, axe, sword; crate ahead and down, barrel ahead). At 6 m/s
  ahead, crowbar on a crate: before the fix blows 5.29 then 18.24 m/s (broken on the second); press off 6.95;
  fixed 6.91. At 5 m/s, fixed: every blow 2.8-5.8 m/s, none over the hand's speed; crate ahead 4 fist blows, 2-3
  weapon blows to break; barrel ahead fist 5 blows 75 -> 53, crowbar 2, sword 3. Not done: the same matrix on the
  build before the press fix (stopped for time).

### Bodies by walls

Not looked into (time): see the report.

### Item Pickup Mode Vanilla

- **Cause.** Pickups are taken by their hand touch; the body's touch reaches it only with `vr_body_interactions` (0),
  so in Vanilla (vr_carry 0) walking over them took nothing. And every carry gate read vr_carry, so a round from the ammo
  pouch (a carried thing) was dropped the frame it was taken ("carry: lost"), crates and gibs couldn't be carried.
- **Fix.** The engine's body touch calls a pickup's (FL_ITEM) hand touch with vr_carry 0 (`vr_physics.cpp`). QC
  `VR_Carry_On(box)`: vr_carry 0 stops only pickups being carried; the pouch's rounds, crates, gibs and wall torches as
  in the other modes.
- **Checked** (`scratch/vanilla_test.py 0`, e1m1): walked onto a shells box: "You got the shells"; the main hand at the
  pouch takes a grenade for the off hand's launcher ("a grenade taken from the pouch", 29 left) and holds it, no
  "carry: lost". Not confirmed: the silver key (test spawn 113) was not taken in that run (the walk may not have reached
  it); the health box was walked over at full health (not taken, as in Quake). eval.sh not run (time).

**In VR:** charge with the hands a bit above the chest (and as before); run past a grunt with the hands up: no charge.
Hit crates and barrels with the fist, crowbar, axe and sword: as many blows as before the press fix. Press a crate down:
still no sinking. Vanilla: walk over ammo, health, armour and a key: taken; take a round from the ammo pouch: it stays
in the hand; carry a crate.

## Dying against a wall: the hand to it, a slide down it (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/walldeath`, 2026-10-23)

Voice note (vrtesthall 01-44-55): grunts shot with a shotgun next to a wall never reach for it or slow their fall; they
flop. What the lean (ROUND22 "Active ragdolls: environment", `vr_ragdoll_active_env_lean`) needs, in plain words: a
body-shot death (not a headshot: half the pellets that hit in the head, nor a beheading) of a monster with an active
death; within its first second, still up (chest an arm's length over the floor, pelvis not far over it); a near-vertical
wall within about 1.5 arm lengths of its chest (or one its fall carries it into); a 10% chance of no hand.

- **Why it didn't show** (`scratch/wall_test.py`: real shotgun and super shotgun kills by vrtesthall's south wall,
  grunts 8 to 64 units off it, the player 50 or 90 units away; awake grunts shot twice, or still ones once):
  - The lean was found in nearly every body-shot kill, but the hand reached the wall at 0.3 to 0.5 s, when the grunt
    was already down (pelvis 30 -> 19 units in 0.5 s); only about half the hands held at all (shotgun: 12 of 22 still,
    7 of 16 awake), and the hold (0.42 body weights) never slowed the fall: nothing looked like a slide.
  - A wall behind him: the hand went straight back to the nearest point behind his shoulder, hidden by his body.
  - The super shotgun's kill push slams him up against the wall (pelvis 50 units up, his chest sometimes inside the
    wall's brush): "not upright" (pelvis too high), and the chest's probe rays start inside the wall and meet nothing:
    no lean in about half of those kills (11 of 24).
- **Fix** (`vr_ragactive.cpp`):
  - **The slide** (new `vr_ragdoll_active_env_slide`, 0.6 body weights; the "Wall Slide" slider under "Lean on
    Walls"): while his chest is against the wall he leans on (within 0.7 arm lengths of it), his pelvis's and chest's
    sinking is held to 0.5 m/s by at most that much of his weight, fading over 1.8 s: he slides down it into a slump.
  - The hand grabs the wall sooner (within 0.35 arm lengths of its goal, or 0.3 off the wall; retargeted to the
    wall from where it is after 0.15 s, was 0.3), the hold slapping it on.
  - His back to the wall: the palm goes out beside him and lower (0.6 arm lengths to his side, 0.25 down), where it
    is seen; sometimes (60%) both hands, when neither is on a wound. No-hand chance 20% -> 10%.
  - Slammed up off the floor he stood on (same floor under him as at the start): still "up" with the pelvis up to 2.6
    arm lengths over it, and the fall's ray leans on a wall he is thrown across into (not one he falls down past: a
    ledge's floor is another floor, so the ledge cases are unchanged). The round probe also casts from the pelvis when
    the chest's ray meets nothing (a chest inside the wall).
  - Blown away from the wall (moving off it faster than 2.5 m/s as the lean starts): no lean ("ragenv: N no lean:
    blown away from the wall"). Never fired in the tallies (the kill pushes him towards it there).
- **Checked** (body-shot kills that braced a hand on the wall and held, of kills; every one of them leaned and slid):
  shotgun, still grunts 38 of 43; shotgun, awake grunts 19 of 22 (plus a headshot and one killed 154 units off the
  wall: nothing, as it should); super shotgun, awake grunts 37 of 42. The rest: the no-hand roll (5) or a hand that
  didn't get there (8). Pelvis heights now e.g. 30 24 22 22 22 15 at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1/1.5 s (slumped against the wall),
  the super shotgun's 49 41 26 28 28 17. Eyeshots: `scratch/eyes_c1.png` (shotgun, the arm out to the wall, debug
  lines), `scratch/eyes_final_ssg.png` (super shotgun). env_test.sh wall/along/ledge/thrown/crate/open: as before (the
  ledge grabs and hangs, the open case nothing). eval.sh: the same 169/177 passes as the baseline (3 takes differ by
  0.1 unit in their offsets, verdicts unchanged).

**In VR:** shoot grunts (shotgun and super shotgun, body shots) standing a step or two in front of a wall: most should
throw a hand out to the wall beside them and slide down it into a slump, the super shotgun's slamming them into it
first. Shoot one standing away from walls, and one with a headshot: no change. Wall Slide 0 gives back the drop.

## Monster weapon drops: the infected's weapons as they turn, Freddie gibbed (worktree `release`, branch `agent/drops1023`, 2026-10-23)

From the read-only audit of monster weapons (approved by Vittorio).

- **Dawn of the Machine's infected** (`monster_army_infected`, `_knight_`, `_enforcer_`, `_hell_knight_infected`): their
  first death is `MG3_Infected_Turn` (combat.qc Killed hands them over before any death function), so `army_die`,
  `knight_die`, `enf_die` and `hknight_die` never ran and nothing fell. Now `MG3_Infected_DropWeapon`
  (vr_mg3_infected.qc), first thing in the turn while he is still the old monster: the grunt's gun and the enforcer's
  rifle through `VR_DropEnemyGun` (full), the knight's sword and the death knight's (`QVR_WPNFLAG_USE_SECONDARY_AMMO`)
  through `VR_DropKnightSword`, the same calls and the same statue exception (`spawnflags & 2`) as the stock deaths.
  A wedged one (no room for the new body: killed again at once) has dropped it already. The zombie or fiend he becomes
  is set to `progs/zombie.mdl` / `progs/demon.mdl`, which hold no weapon; their own deaths drop nothing.
- **AD's Freddie**: his super nailgun dropped only with his gun arm cut off (`VR_ADGun_LimbCut`). Now also when he is
  gibbed (`VR_ADGun_FreddieGibbed`, from `VR_AD_Gibbed`, AD's `monster_ThrowGib` hook: gibbed in his death or his body
  gibbed later): thrown from where his left forearm was, up and out to his left, a full clip. Once per Freddie: the new
  field `.vr_adgun_freddie_off` is set by whichever comes first (a cut arm, a blast's popped arm or the gibbing).
  `vr_adgun_drops 0` still drops nothing. No AD source change (ad_import.py `--check`: 0 of 142 differ).
- **AD's deflector** (`monster_deflector`): not in `VR_ADGun_ForClass`, by scope rather than a decision against it. The
  guns were made for AD's soldier family (above, "Armed AD soldiers, defender/eliminator, centurion, pyro and
  fumigator"; `vr_adguns.hpp` `variantCount` 8: rocket, grenade, plasma, defender, eliminator, centurion, pyro,
  fumigator). The deflector got Quake VR's treatment later in the rig batch (head zone, knockdown, its rig with a `gun`
  bone on the right hand), and `vr_monstermods.cpp` hides only its muzzle effect and field rings in its deaths: "It
  keeps its gun". It also has no one gun to map: `ad_mon_deflector.qc` gives it two attacks per skin (yellow, the
  default: a wall of flame up close, `ad_deflect_fireflame`, and a volley of 1-3 drunk rockets, `ad_deflect_fire_rocket`;
  blue, `spawnflags` PLASMA: three plasma bolts, `ad_deflect_fireplasma`, and the rockets), its shield (reflects nails,
  lightning, plasma and the axe) is the monster's, not the gun's, and AD gibs it as an inert `progs/w_enforcergun.mdl`
  (skin 3 on the blue one). Not implemented.

Tests: `vr_mg3_mtest 2` (developer 1) now also checks each infected dropped one weapon as he turned (its kind and flags,
its model, grabbable, a full clip, near him; he is the zombie or fiend model) and that killing the zombies and fiends
again adds none. `vr_ad_test 95` gibs Freddie's body after the arm cut: no second gun. New `vr_ad_test 102`: a Freddie
near you gibbed whole drops one super nailgun, full, taken into the main hand. Debug > AD Monsters > Soldiers' Guns >
"Freddie Gibbed Whole" runs it.

Results: `vr_mg3_mtest 2` on e1m1: 19 passed, 0 failed (the grunt's `v_gruntgun.mdl` clip 30, the knight's
`v_ksword.mdl`, the enforcer's `v_enfrifle.mdl` clip 20, the death knight's `v_hksword.mdl` flags 1, each 14-15 units
from him; 6 -> 6 weapons lying after the second kills). ad_dm1 (`-game ad`): `vr_ad_test 102` PASS (gibbed, health
-100: one SNG, 36 in it, 138 units out); `vr_ad_test 95` PASS (cut: one SNG; the body then gibbed: 0 more).

What it would take to give the deflector a gun: a design choice first (which attack the dropped gun fires: the rockets,
the flame wall as the pyro's flamethrower, or the blue skin's plasma as the plasma rifle; one gun or one per skin); then
a WID (29 on), a ninth burst-rifle variant in `vr_adgunart.cpp` (add-ons, skin, `fireFeels`, `variantCount`), its
weapon-offset slot defaults, a `VR_ADGun_Fire` branch, its `VR_ADGun_ForClass` entry, its gun hidden in its deaths in
`vr_monstermods.cpp` (vertices of its rig's `gun` bone, now kept, and the rig re-measured without them), AD's
`w_enforcergun.mdl` gib cleared on a drop (as the crossbow's), a toolgun row (`ad_monsters_gen.py` GUNS) and a test.

**In VR:** Dawn of the Machine (or the Debug menu's infected spawns): kill an infected grunt, knight, enforcer and death
knight: each should burst with his gun or sword falling beside him, grabbable, the zombie or fiend that gets up holding
nothing. AD: blow a Freddie apart with rockets: a super nailgun should fly out of the gibs (one, even if his arm was

## Blood in water (worktree `release`, branch `agent/bloodwater`, 2026-10-23)

Built from the BACKLOG design (agent/firewater; his notes vrtesthall_2026-10-23_01-42-34, _01-43-54), both halves. No
protocol change, new cvars only (`vr_water_blood` 1, `vr_water_blood_time` 30; Gore > Blood in Water).

**(a) Bloody water surface** (`vr_water.cpp`, "Blood in the liquids"; `vr_glsl.h` `LiquidBlood`). Up to 16 clouds, each
{centre, surface height, size, peak, born, fade-from}, in the frame data beside the ripples (`BloodInfo`, `BloodAt[16]`
xy centre, z surface, w radius now; `BloodAmp[4]` strength now; `gpuframedata_t` `bloodinfo`, `bloodat`, `bloodamp`).
Radius `size * (8 + 52 * sqrt(age / 20 s))` (8 -> 60 units over 20 s; `size` sqrt(amount), 0.6..1.4), strength
`peak * (1 - t / vr_water_blood_time)^1.3` (a half-second rise in), times `vr_water_blood`. A new cloud within a living
one's radius (x0.8 + 12 units, same height within 8) tops it up (`peak = min(now + 0.6 * amount, 1.5)`, its fade
restarted) instead of taking a slot; full, the weakest now goes. The shader (both liquid programs, after the
refraction: the colour over what is behind it): one loop over the clouds on level-ish faces (|facing.z| > 0.5, both
sides: the surface seen from under water too) that skips any further than 1.14 radii or 40 units off its height; the
edge broken by two octaves of `LiquidNoise` drifting slowly (slime's slower); `mix(c, vec3(0.32, 0.02, 0.015) * light,
min(0.75 k, 0.88))` (slime a brown `vec3(0.2, 0.09, 0.02)`; none on lava or teleports), its alpha raised as much
(without refraction), faded out from 1200 to 2000 units.

Sources (`water::addBlood(at, amount, above)`: in a liquid, up to its surface in 16-unit steps, 192 at most, then six
halvings; out of one, a liquid at most `above` units under it, six halvings; lava, a teleport's leaf, too deep: none):
- `particles::spawn` Preset::Blood (amount count / 20, 0.15..1) and BloodTrail (0.1 a count, 0.3 at most), with or
  without `vr_particles`;
- the gore's EventBurst (0.7 x size) and EventCorpse (0.8, 40 units above);
- the gore's drops: your own bleeding (`playerBleed` -> `fall`) let in the water you wade in (0.12 x drop), a ceiling's
  drip falling into a pool (the drop now ends at the surface, no mark under the water);
- the blood streams (`vr_bloodstream.cpp`): once a second at the surface over a wound under water, or where a stream
  pours in (0.3 x strength x power);
- a body or a thing standing in water that blood was painted on in the last 15 s (`Mask::bled`, set in
  `detail::paint` for blood splats): QC's four-a-second `QVR_WOUND_WATER` events (monsters, you) and `washGear` (a
  bloody prop or weapon afloat or dropped in) add a cloud at the waterline once a second (`Mask::bloodCloud`), 0.3
  fading to 0 over those 15 s.

**(b) Blood slowed in water** (his first step: no per-particle collision). One `water::bloodInLiquid` (one leaf walk)
a burst: `blood()` (its drops and the tiny droplets, a quarter as many, and its mist puff), `bloodTrail` (its smear; no
falling drops), the gore's mist (`mist(..., wet)`: twice as long, drag 3, sinking 4 u/s, 0.3 of the speed), the
streams' spurts (`bloodDroplet(..., wet)`). `soak()`: velocity x 0.25, drag 5 (stopped in ~0.3 s), gravity 0.03
(sinking ~5 u/s), 2-4 s, alpha x 0.7 fading out, 1.6x the size growing to about 3x: a slowly blooming cloud. A stream
whose wound is under water (tested with its landing arc, 12 a second) pours no chain: 14 soaked puffs a second off the
wound; one pouring into a liquid ends its points at the surface (the arc's crossing time, from the surface found below
the landing) and blooms puffs there. The gore's hit and burst rays under water reach 0.3 as far, no back-splatter and no
rays to the ceiling; their marks 0.6 the size, showing 1 s + flight / 40 later, no drips or runs from them.

Debug menu (Gore tools): Blood in Water (`vr_water_blood_test [distance] [amount]`: a cloud on the liquid below a
point ahead), Blood Spray Ahead (`vr_water_blood_spray [distance] [count]`: a hit's blood, Preset::Blood), Blood in
Water: Clouds (`vr_water_blood_info`).

**Cost.** GPU: vrfiringrange's pool from above with 16 clouds in view, eyes 2048 x 2048, `vr_profile_report 6` x3
(on, off, on): eyes' GPU 1.659, 1.678, 1.659 ms: no difference beyond noise. CPU: a fight's worth (10 Preset::Blood
sprays a second for 6 s, half under water, half over it, 30 clouds made or merged): `particles` 0.130 ms, `particle sim`
0.033 ms a frame; the `water blood` scope never shows in the report (under 0.001 ms); at most 18 leaf walks an
`addBlood`, one a `bloodInLiquid`.

**Checked** (mock headset): `scratch/bw_pool.png` (the pool from above, blood off / on, five clouds 13 s old),
`scratch/bw_spray.png` (a spray under water at 0.35 s and 2 s, a spray in the air), `scratch/bw_grunt_underwater.png`
(a grunt in the pool with three streams: puffs at its chest, its cloud on the surface seen from below; streams info: 3
pouring, 0 chain pieces drawn).

**In VR:** fight in the firing range's pool (or vrtesthall's): shoot and gib monsters standing in the water: dark red
clouds should spread on the surface where they bleed and fade over half a minute; wade while hurt (under 75 health):
your own cloud follows you. Dive and shoot one under water: the spray should stop short and hang as a sinking cloud,
with no splats flying across the pool. Say whether the red is too strong or too faint (Gore > Blood in Water).

Not done (BACKLOG): the per-particle surface crossing (a spray from above the surface carried into it, a ragdoll half
in), clouds drifting with the swells or currents, underwater blood decals on the pool's floor (only the rays' marks
are smaller and later).

## 1.1 decisions: particle cap, shadow atlas on demand, struggle in the groups (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/dec11`, 2026-10-23)

His 1.1 decisions (BACKLOG.md, "The 1.1.0 plan").

**Particle size cap 0.15.** `vr_particle_max_screen` (Graphics > Effects: Largest Particle) has shipped at 0.15 since it
was added (5f65185a1, "Particles near the eyes, a size cap..."); no build had 0.3, so no config holds an older default:
nothing changed, no migration.

**Shadow atlas on demand** (`vr_shadow_atlas_grow` 1, archived; Graphics > Shadows: Grow Shadow Atlas). The atlas was
always 8192 x 8192 D32F (256 MB) and the static atlas (the map lights' cached world depth) 6144 x 4096 (96 MB): 352 MB.
- Making a texture that size mid-play is a hitch: the driver allocates at the framebuffer's completeness check, 2.5-5 ms,
  with the storage and attachment 0.4-3.3 ms more: 7.2-7.7 ms CPU for a growth to 8192 x 6144 (12.5 ms with the GPU
  synced and the new atlas cleared). Over the brief's 2 ms, so the atlas does not grow mid-play.
- At a map's load the atlas is sized for its lights: its map light slots (with growing on, `vr_shadow_maplights` but no
  more than the map has lights), the dynamic lights' budget at a typical 256-texel face (a muzzle flash, a rocket, an
  explosion near you: `selectDlights`' size), the flashlight's tile; rounded up to 32 MB bands (1024 rows at 8192),
  still 8192 wide, so the faces pack exactly where they did. The shader samples by `textureSize`, so a non-square atlas
  needed no shader change.
- Each frame the faces' full-size rows are measured (`packRows`); when they need more than the atlas has, the frame packs
  them smaller (as an over-full 8192 atlas always did: halved, the map lights' moving casters skipped) and the atlas grows
  to the most this map has needed at the next moment a hitch goes unfelt: the menu or console up, paused, the
  intermission, dead. A new map sizes it again. `vr_shadow_stats 1` prints the atlas sizes, MB, the rows the faces want
  (and the peak), the frames squeezed, the growths and the last one's cost; with it on, a growth is timed GPU-synced.
- Measured (headless, defaults): e1m1, e2m6, e3m3, e4m7 all 8192 x 5120 + 6144 x 4096 = **256 MB** (was 352); their
  frames wanted 2048-4352 rows standing about (three or four map lights near you: the player is always a caster). Five
  1024-face lights (`vr_light_test 2000`) wanted 8704 rows: squeezed (168 frames) until the menu opened, then grew to
  8192 x 8192 in 16.4 ms (GPU-synced, under the menu). A "start at 64 MB" was not possible without losing shadows: the
  map lights' moving casters alone take 4096 rows (128 MB) wherever three or four lights reach you.
- `vr_shadow_atlas_grow 0`: square at once, as before (352 MB).

**Struggle in the monster groups** (config 190). `vr_struggle_classes` retired; each group has Struggle (on/off: on for
Grunts, Enforcers, Knights, Death Knights, Mini Bosses, Elite Knights, Zombies, Mummies; a new `struggle` column in
`vr_mgroups.inc`), Struggle Strength, Speed, Arm Drive (times each class's own, 1) and Weaker When Hurt (1):
`vr_mgrp_<g>_struggle`, `_struggle_strength`, `_struggle_speed`, `_struggle_arms`, `_struggle_hurt`.
- Each class's own strength, speed, full health and arm drive are the old list's, a table in `vr_mgroups.cpp`
  (`struggleProfiles`, 23 classes); `mgroups::struggleOfClass` resolves a class's (clamped as the list was: strength 0-3,
  speed 0.2-3, arms 1-2.5). A member of a struggling group without a profile does not struggle, as before: Honey's
  soldier, the infected, AD's point knight, ranged knight, death knight ghost, Quoth's death knight, the minotaur, golem,
  drole, justice knight, centurion, the Shub zombie (the per-class exceptions a group can't express).
- Menu: each group's page has a Struggle header (the five rows and Struggle Profiles: its classes' strength / speed /
  full health / arm drive in the help); a page per setting (Monster Groups - Struggle ...); Holding Enemies > Struggle:
  Each Monster Group. `vr_mgroup_list` adds `; struggles s sp h a` to each struggling class's line.
- Migration (190): the retired line's value is kept as the config runs (`VR_RetiredCvar`); a list that is not one of its

## Graphics presets: one table, My Settings, VR Settings > Graphics Presets (worktree `release`, branch `agent/gfxpresets`, 2026-10-23)

Approved by the author. Before, `vr_graphics_preset` (0 off .. 4 ultra) wrote some 60 cvars one way through three
functions (`lighting::applyPreset`, `water::applyPreset`, `haze::applyPreset`); nothing kept the player's own values,
and nothing said whether the settings still matched a preset. Its High was not the defaults (6 shadowed dynamic lights
of 512, 9 taps, 2048 units against the shipped 8 of 1024, 16 taps, 3072): the shipped game was the old Ultra.

**One table** (`vr_gfxpresets.cpp`, `presetRows`, 73 rows): each row a cvar and its value at Off, Low, Medium, High
and Ultra, `D` for the cvar's default (its `default_string`, so `vr_defaults.cfg` too). High is all `D`: the game as
shipped, so nobody's game changes unless they pick a preset. The same table applies a preset, finds the one the
settings match (every row equal, as numbers when both are; Custom otherwise), and is what My Settings keeps. Graphics
only: no comfort, gameplay, body, calibration or audio cvar is in it (checked: a config written before and after a
preset differs only in table rows).

**My Settings:** the first preset applied in a game folder first writes every row's current value to
`<gamedir>/graphics_my_settings.cfg` (`name "value"` lines, through a temporary file; git-ignored in `quakevr/`).
Switching presets never writes it again. *My Settings* sets the kept values back exactly (only names in the table are
read back); *Save as My Settings* (pressed twice within 3 s when some are kept) replaces them. A row added later is
simply not in an older file: My Settings leaves it as it is and ignores it when matching.

**Menu:** VR Settings (Sight) > **Graphics Presets** (`pageGraphicsPresets`, LevelStandard): "Now: <state>" (a preset's
name, "My Settings", "High (My Settings)" when both, or "Custom"), a note line for 5 s after a press (the first preset
says your settings were kept), Off (Quake) / Low / Medium / High (as shipped) / Ultra, then My Settings and Save as My
Settings, and a link to the Graphics page (shown from Advanced detail). Advanced VR Options > Graphics lost its Preset
cycle: it shows the state line and links to the page.

**Console:** `vr_graphics_preset 0..4` applies a preset, `5` My Settings, then sets itself back to -1 (a button, not a
state; the voice notes print the state name instead of its value). `vr_graphics_preset_save`;
`vr_graphics_preset_status` prints the state and, when Custom, every row that differs from the nearest preset.

**What the presets now hold** (new rows marked +): Off: Quake's look as before, plus no muzzle-flash shadows+, plasma
arcs+, carved holes+, permanent marks+, scorch marks+, particle size cap 0.1+. Low: as before (2 shadowed dynamic lights
of 256, no map light shadows, no bumps/parallax/AO/refraction/teleporter views/haze, fewer projectile, flame and torch
lights) plus no muzzle-flash shadows+, no carved holes+, particle cap 0.1+. Medium: as before (4 dynamic lights of 512,
2 map lights, 1536 units, 4 taps) plus parallax without its depth write+ (`vr_parallax_depth_write 0`), no muzzle-flash
shadows+, particle cap 0.12+. High: the defaults. Ultra: 12 shadowed dynamic lights, 6 map lights, 4096 units, 12 torch
lights, `vr_bloom_fast 0` (the four-level glow), `vr_particle_halfres 0`, `vr_parallax_steps 24`.

**Cost** (`bench.sh --settings`, a cfg `vr_graphics_preset N`, 2 reps of 600 frames, 90 Hz paced, 2048-pixel eyes,
exclusive; ms a frame, eyes' GPU avg / p95, CPU busy avg; labels `gp_v1_*`, Medium `gp_v2_2`):

| Preset | AD fight (`play_ad_tfuma_fight`) | Gore fight (`play_gore_fight`) | Water (`water_range_surface`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off | 1.30 / 1.98, CPU 3.03 | 1.66 / 2.53, CPU 2.20 | 0.71 / 1.04 |
| Low | 1.39 / 1.93, CPU 3.57 | 2.07 / 3.03, CPU 1.97 | 1.01 / 1.39 |
| Medium | 2.03 / 2.47, CPU 3.31 | 2.49 / 3.19, CPU 1.93 | 1.12 / 1.41 |
| High | 4.27 / 4.86, CPU 3.30 | 3.75 / 5.01, CPU 2.39 | 1.25 / 1.72 |
| Ultra | 4.45 / 5.05, CPU 3.51 | 3.85 / 5.21, CPU 2.04 | 1.21 / 1.51 |

The first Medium (the old one: parallax on with its depth) measured 4.75 ms on the AD fight, no cheaper than High.
Single changes over High (AD fight / gore fight GPU ms; High 4.27 / 3.75): parallax off 1.95 / 2.42, normal maps off
1.87 / 2.35, **`vr_parallax_depth_write 0` 2.10 / 2.49**, `vr_parallax_steps 8` 4.25 / 3.65, `vr_parallax_distance
512` 4.11 / 3.62, `vr_parallax_refine 0` 4.09 / 3.67, carved holes off 4.16 / 3.38, AO off 4.00 / 3.34, tone mapping
and bloom off 4.02 / 3.44, `vid_fsaa 2` 3.68 / 3.14, `vr_taa 1` 3.80 / 3.67. Parallax's cost is nearly all its depth
write (the world's pixels lose early depth testing), not its steps: Medium keeps parallax and drops the depth write.
Worth the author's look: the shipped default pays about 2 ms of a 4.3 ms frame on this card for the relief's depth
(things meeting the carved relief rather than the flat surface); no default changed here. Shadows cost little in these
scenes (0.04-0.06 ms). CPU time barely moves with the preset (the game, not the drawing).

Left out on purpose: anti-aliasing (`vid_fsaa`, its own row on VR Settings > Display and Graphics; 2x saves ~0.6 ms)
and TAA (opt-in, a look of its own), the weapons' and gloves' relief (`vr_weapon_relief`, `vr_glove_relief`: made as
models load, no frame cost), decals themselves (`vr_decals`: gore), render scale and foveation (the headset's).

Tests (headless, e1m1): personal values set (`vr_shadow_dlights 5; vr_bloom 0.123; vr_water_foam 0`), then each preset
applied: the status names each (Custom before, nearest High, 3 differ); one change after High: Custom, 1 differs;
`vr_graphics_preset 5`: My Settings with the three personal values; configs written before and after the round trip
are identical (0 differences), and before/Low differ in 28 rows, all in the table. A second start (the config back to
its baseline): the state High, the file kept; My Settings sets 5 / 0.123 / 0 back; two presses of Save as My Settings
(menu, `vr_menu_press`) then a preset and My Settings: bloom 0.2 kept. `vr_menu_path_check` vrcalibration 6 found,
vrtesthall 14 found, 0 missing. Screenshot of the page after `vr_menu_press Graphics Presets > Medium`: "Now: Medium",
"Medium set.".

The author approved it (BACKLOG.md, "Droppable, usable mace: AD's Death Sergeant"): AD's death sergeant drops its flail
and the player swings it, its spiked head a body of its own on a chain.

  saves, level changes and the toolgun as the other AD melee weapons). `VR_ADMelee_Drop` drops it for
  `ad_CT_MONDSERG` (AD's gib1, `w_blueflail.mdl`, no longer thrown). `vr_monstermods.cpp` hides its 395 vertices
  (870..1264) in the deaths (223..254); the rig (`vr_ad_rigs.inc` adDsergeantSeeds) loses its dangling "flail" bone,
  so the flail is a loose piece as the hunter ogres' weapons are (shin parents renumbered).

  handle alone (AD's vertices 0..63, 207..212), laid as the knight's sword (the hand 40% up from the pommel);
  `#flailhead` its spiked ball and ring (64..206, 213..218), its middle at the origin, +x to the ring, at the held
  weapons' drawn size. AD's chain is not used: the engine draws its own. Weapon Offsets slot 47 (index 46: the mace's
  settings, its own tip `3.4688 1.2836 9.1007`, mass 1.2 kg); `weapons::numSlots` 47; toolgun Weapons choice 346
  (`ad_monsters_gen.py`'s GUNS row; its QC rows added by hand: the generator would undo 309-311).
- **Held** (not holsterable: the head swings only in a hand; the hammer's and mace's rule): the handle strikes nothing
  (`VR_Melee_Thing` none). The head (`vr_box3d_flail.cpp`): for each hand holding `#melee`, a shapeless kinematic anchor
  at the hand's muzzle (QC .muzzlepos: the handle's end as drawn), led each frame like the reach bodies, and a dynamic
  sphere (4.4 u, `vr_flail_mass` kg, a bullet: continuous) held to it by Box3D's distance joint as a rope
  (`vr_flail_chain` m plus the ring's reach). Categories: catProp plus its own catFlail; it meets the level, doors,
  monsters, props and corpses, never the player, his hands or what they carry. Its user number is negative (no
  entity: every contact consumer checks for > 0). Carried on a jump the hand never makes (over 1.5 m, or faster than
  25 m/s real: a stale muzzle as it is taken, a teleport, a load), placed short of the level; no faster than 40 m/s;
  its middle never crosses the level's surface (put back if it did: none in the tests). Made again when the chain
  length or mass changes; gone when the hand lets go.

  0.2 s, none in its first 0.3 s, go to QC `VR_Flail_Hit(player, hand, target, at, dir, speed, mass)` (`speed` real:
  bullet time's scale divided out). Damage `vr_flail_damage` 3 x mass x (speed - `vr_flail_min_speed` 3 m/s), at most
  `vr_flail_max_damage` 150, `vr_flail_2h` 1.3x with the other hand on its handle; dealt as the hand's blunt sword blow
  (W_SwordMelee with the blow's contact and speed set to the head's: blood, blunt sounds and haptics, wall marks, the
  impact rule for props, knockdowns), the blow's own fields put back after.
- **Drawn** (`vr_flail.cpp`): the head model where the last step left it (a listen server's), turned with its ring to
  the chain's last link; the chain from the drawn muzzle to the ring as the flashlight's rigid chain of links
  (`coil::Cord`, blue steel), in each eye's opaque scene.
- **Settings:** AD Weapons page, "Death Sergeant's Flail": Chain Length, Head Mass, Damage, Least Speed, Most Damage,

### The flail after swords4 (merged; worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/flail`, 2026-10-23)

- **Renumbered** after swords4 took kinds 7-10, slots 47-50 and `vr_ad_test` 131-139: the flail is kind 11 (weapon
  flags 2816; the kind's bits 8-11 hold it), Weapon Offsets slot 51 (index 50, `numSlots` 51), `vr_ad_test` 145
  (killed, dropped, taken), 146 (in the main hand), 147 (the main hand's hold as drawn: the tip from the hand). Its
  toolgun entry is the table's last (`vr_toolgun_packs.inc`: no entry's number moves; it was among AD's guns, which
  moved every entry after it), its QC dispenser choice still 346 (`ad_monsters_gen.py`'s row taken out: its rerun would
  move the entries).
- **The handle in the hand:** the mace's offsets put it 25 units from the hand (the slot's Scale scales the model about
  its box's corner, swords4's "Held up the blade (fixed)"). Offsets now the mace's + 0.66 x (the mace's corner - the
  flail's), then 3.2 units along the handle to land its grip where the mace's is: X 1.79, Y 3.886, Z 4.70. Its tip
  2.3 units from the hand (the mace's grip 3 below the hand point, as his tuning has it); eyeshot
  `scratch/flail_held3.png`: the handle in the hand, the chain to the head on the floor.
- **Slow motion:** the hands are slowed with the world (`timescale::filterHands`: they follow their controllers at the
  game's pace), so the head lives in its hand's time: `handTime()` = scale / `timescale::handScale()` (1 in bullet
  time, the scale in Sandevistan), its gravity 1/handTime^2, its rope's stiffness and its speeds by it; a blow's speed
  is the hand's time's, as melee's. Before, the speeds were taken to real time (x0.3) and the head made 11 times as
  heavy: full swings hit at 0.4-3.8 m/s. Real-time runs (`-RealTime`, `vr_timescale 0.3`): hits 4.4-12.5 m/s (57, 46,
  44 damage), against 8.8-21.5 at full speed; the slowed hand itself reaches 13.7 m/s at the handle's end against 22
  (its own speed limit, vr_timescale_hand_speed). (Fast-mode runs time the mock swing by the wall clock: they don't
  compare slow motion.) A hand's place arriving in bursts is no jump under 0.5 m.
- **The chain's length:** its rope 120 Hz (Box3D's joints' 60), and after each step the head held to its length,
  pulled position-based (the pull given as speed too); the stretch 7.4 -> 0.00 units; the speed limit (40 m/s) after.
- **Rattle:** AD's `gibs/gibchain.wav` (precached with the flail's model) from the player as the head goes faster than
  6 m/s (at most every 0.3 s) and with each blow; `vr_flail_rattle` 0.7 its volume (AD Weapons page: Chain Rattle).
- Tests: `vr_ad_test 145` all PASS (kind 11); full-speed swings (real time) 8.8-21.5 m/s, 35-111 damage; floor slams:
  14 hits, never through, never put back; `eval.sh` 169/177 as the baseline (verdicts unchanged).
## Show Melee Blades; the sweep test's D and F (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/meleeview`, 2026-10-23)

- **Show Melee Blades** (`vr_debug_melee_blades`, default 0; Debug > Views): for each hand's melee sweep (swords, axes,
  AD's weapons, fists, guns used as clubs, a wall torch), drawn live over everything: the blow line from the hand to the
  tip (`VR_Melee_Line`'s, bold; the near end behind the hand thin), the lines the sweep tested this frame and the last
  0.3 s (`VR_Melee_Ribs`: each striking point's way from the pose before, with `vr_melee_swept` the whole blade's) and
  the blade's surface between successive poses, fading out; a hammer's or mace's head as its box (`admeleehead`, as the
  ribs use it). White idle; yellow while the motion is a blow (`VR_Melee_ShowFast`: `VR_Melee_Decide` would land one
  with the outermost striking point now, its speed for its kind, the arm driving it, no wiggle, not pulled back; the
  fields Decide sets are put back); red for 0.4 s after a blow landed (the sweep of that frame red too), a white cross
  with a red dot at the contact (`mh_c_pos`) and the damage above it (`T_Damage_VRMelee`'s, after positional), for 1.5 s.
- How: QC `VR_Melee_Show` (vr_melee.qc, from `VR_Melee_Sweep` after the ribs, not for the sweep test's probes) sends
  them through the new builtin `meleeshow(hand, what, a, b, v)`, only while the cvar is on (off: one `cvar_hget` a
  sweep, nothing sent, the draw returns at once). `Quake/vr/vr_meleeshow.cpp` keeps 24 sweeps (48 lines each) and 8
  hits per hand (file-scope) by the server's time and draws them with the view (`vr_view.cpp`, beside Show Melee Arcs).
  A mock swing (`vr_mock_swing`) is mostly white with the knight's sword: its grip moves under the 4 m/s a slash needs
  (`melee debug: ... grip 0.9 far 44.0 ... need 4.0`), so it never lands; the author's takes do.
- **D and F (fixed; the test):** `VR_MSWT_Probe` never set `mh_pgrip`. Since b039bd88f (frame-rate independence)
  `VR_Melee_ArcRib` bends a point's line round the grip's way from `mh_pgrip` to `mh_grip` when the chord cuts the arc;
  with `mh_pgrip` '0 0 0' every point's "arc" was taken round the map's origin, so the probe's lines ran far off the
  blade (F: a box 3 units past the tip struck "44.7 along the blade"; D: a floor contact 829 units along it on ad_dm1,
  -16..-25 on vrfiringrange). Not a blind spot in play: `VR_Melee_Track` sets `mh_pgrip` every frame. The probe now sets
  it to the pose before's grip (its moves are straight, so no arc: the chords as when the test was written). After: PASS
  on ad_dm1 and vrfiringrange for the Dark Prince's, the knight's, the justice knight's and the judicator's swords, the
  hammer and the mace (`vr_ad_test 137/117/138/139/128/129`); D lands 22.2 along the knight's sword (its striking
  part's middle 22.0; old 829.4), as in the swept blades' notes.
- eval.sh: canary and full 169/177, every verdict as the baseline; 3 takes differ by 0.1 unit in a contact offset. The
  base commit (8652036b9, without these changes) gives 169/177 with 6 such 0.1-unit differences (a different set): run
  to run noise, not this change.
- Eyeshots: `scratch/mshow_hit.png` (the axe take `slash_backswing_up_left_..._12-30-44` played back: the hit, red line,
  cross and "23.1", then the swept surface fading); `scratch/mshow_swing_hammer.png` (the AD hammer swung by the mock:
  its head box yellow mid-swing, white after, the sweep fading).

**In VR:** Debug > Views > Show Melee Blades. Swing a sword, an axe, the AD hammer, fists and a gun at a grunt or the
dummy: the line follows the weapon from the hand to its tip (the head's box round the hammer's head); slow moves stay
white, real blows turn yellow before they land and red where they land, the dot at the point struck and the damage over
it. Swings that "should have hit": see whether the swept lines went through the target (a miss there is a detection
bug) or past it (the weapon's drawn length or the reach).

BACKLOG's "Open issues to clear" before 1.1, each checked on next (code and a headless run where one reproduces it).

  `chainsaw`, shared with the hunter ogre) still tested every blow with the swing's wide arc and kept turning after you
  (`ai_charge`'s held turn, the hunter ogre's `ai_face`). `ad_import.py` `SMASH_AHEAD`: on smash6-11 of the ogre and the
  hunter ogre, with the arc on, `ai_charge` steps straight ahead (`VR_MeleeArc_ChargeAhead`), `ai_face` doesn't turn,
  and the chainsaw's blow is tested with the normal arc (`vr_melee_ahead`, fight.qc, set around the call; the swing stays
  wide). Arc off: AD's own code. `--check` 0 of 142. Test (`scratch/ogre_smash.sh`: AD start, ogre, seeds 1-8, facing
  and a 100-degree step aside, `vr_enemy_melee_arc_debug 1`): 132 smash blows at arc 69, every one 45 degrees or more
  off (24, at 93-99 degrees after the step) misses; the swing's 169 at arc 89 land to 87 degrees as before. The hunter
  ogre's smash has the same patch (compiled, not run); its thrust is left wide.

  made again stiff. `ragdollNeckSnapped` now writes `.vr_necksnapped` (QVR_FIELD; QC combat.qc), and a ragdoll made for

  never started again. `OnLoadGame` schedules `VR_Crackles_AfterLoad` (vr_burning.qc, 0.1 s later: a sound started in

## Dragging by the legs: the leg pull's hold firms up once it lies (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/legdrag3`, 2026-10-23)

"1.1 open issues"'s still-open item: after a leg pull takes a humanoid down, holding its shins and walking back left it
where it lay (the hold stretching until it let go).

**Causes** (two):
- **The test was against a wall.** vrfiringrange's start is a dais (x 284-332, its top at z 32) 15 units over the
  stone floor before it; a grunt spawned 36 units ahead stands at its foot, and pulled down its legs lie against the
  riser (face 1487 of the BSP, x 284, z 17-32). Walking back pulled it into the riser: box3d contacts on the pelvis and
  both thighs at x 284 with their normals along the pull, the parts' speed 0 under a hold of 2 x 2055 N. That is why
  `struggle_test.py legpull` showed the same at every Pull Hold Strength (and a head drag, knocked down elsewhere,
  moved).
- **On a flat floor the hold was too weak.** The leg pull hands its enemy over at Pull Hold Strength (0.1 of its weight
  a hand: held harder, it pivoted on its pinned shins and fell the wrong way) and left it there. Lying, its weight on
  the floor holds it more than two hands at 0.1 (or 0.3) pull: it lay still until the hold let go (grunt, flat floor:
  0.1 and 0.3 a hand left it; 0.5 dragged it 90 of 102 units at a lag of 4). And the spring's rate (Held On Spring,
  4 Hz) is the held part's own: a death knight held by its feet (light parts) was pulled far under the most force
  before the 72-unit let-go (two hands at 0.75 of its 3343 N: still; at 12 Hz: dragged).

**Fix** (`vr_foegrab.cpp` `legDragStep`, from `carryStep`): from 0.5 s after the leg pull's hand-over (its fall over)
the holds firm up over 0.5 s: their most force to **Pull Drag Strength** (`vr_foegrab_legpull_drag_strength`, new,
1.5 of its weight in all, shared by the hands still holding it: one hand alone drags it too; Combat > Holding Enemies >
Leg Grabs, after Pull Hold Strength) and their spring to 20 Hz (`legDragHertz`). The fall is untouched (soft as
before: the leggrab suite's directions all as before). The let-go is unchanged (72 units for half a second). A grip
taken again later is the usual hold's, not touched (`box3d::ragdollHoldForce` changes soft holds only). New cvar, no
default changed: no config version.

**Test** (`struggle_test.py`): the drags (legpull, legdrag, headdrag and the new legpull1, legyank) walk off the dais
first (`+forward` 25 frames: x 147, the stone floor; `setpos` doesn't move the VR player) and check the drag (its
pelvis at least 0.6 of the walk, no hold let go: `vr_debug_ragdoll`'s "left behind"); legpull1 is the one-hand pull,
legyank the let-go (lying, run back at 400 u/s and the hands thrown 2.5 m back); legdrag takes its left shin by name
(`vr_mock_hand_to <hand> ragdoll shin_l`: a part number took the grunt's "loose" piece, its gun, by its thigh), and its
arms' lead is judged as legpull's (Thrash, the torso's squirm, left out). Pelvis moved of the walk (units, flat floor):

| class | legpull before (0.1 a hand) | legpull after | legpull1 before | legpull1 after | legyank (let go) | legdrag (shin) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| grunt | 1 of 102, let go | 96 | 1, let go | 90 | yes | 103-108 of 113 |
| enforcer | 5, let go | 103 | 7, let go | 100 | yes | 108 of 114 |
| knight | 1, let go | 88 | 2, let go | 81 | yes | 99 of 113 |
| death knight | 1, let go | 90 | 0, let go | 69 | yes | no hold (mock misses) |
| zombie | 1, let go | 84 | 2, let go | 72 | yes | 106 of 113 |
| mummy | 7, let go | 79 | (no one-hand pull) | (no one-hand pull) | yes | no hold (mock misses) |
| AD knight (start map) | 2, let go | 92 | 1, let go | 87 | no: its run is 104 units (a wall) | 106 of 114 |

Either half of legyank alone drags it, held: a run back at 400 u/s (an enforcer came 186 of 231 units) or the hands

isn't pulled down by the mock's one hand; the death knight's and mummy's lying legs are missed by the mock's legdrag hand.

## Parallax depth write's cost (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/pdepth`, 2026-10-23)

Why: "Graphics presets" measured `vr_parallax_depth_write` at about 2 ms of a 4.3 ms eye frame (AD fight).

**Cause** (`vr_world_fragments` at ad_tfuma's spawn, mock VR, 2048-pixel eyes, 4x MSAA, per eye pass): the world's
fragment shader runs on 5.30 M fragments with the depth write and 1.68 M without; 10.67 M against 4.33 M with
foveation off (4.19 M pixels). This NVIDIA driver drops early depth testing for any program that writes
`gl_FragDepth`. The conservative-depth layouts don't change that (see "Conservative depth for the parallax depth write").
So the depth pre-pass saved the shading nothing: every hidden fragment ran the full shader (parallax, bumps, PBR, the
lights' shadows). AD's deep scenes give 2.5-3.2x overdraw, where start and hip1m1 gave 1.15-2x. That is why the AD
fight paid 2 ms and the older measurements 0.1-0.6. The pre-pass also ran its own small shader on all 5.30 M. It isn't
the parallax walk (`vr_parallax_steps 8` saved nothing), and it isn't the shadow maps (their programs don't write
depth; 0.057 ms either way). The cost is all in `world+brush` (3.04 against 1.06 ms).

**Kept: the split** (`R_DrawSolidSplit`, r_world.c). The opaque world's pre-pass and shading are now drawn three ways:
- the textures with relief (`extmat[3] > 0`) nearer than the split distance, with the depth-writing programs;
- the same textures further away, with the plain programs;
- the textures without relief, with the plain programs.

The split is in view depth, `gl_Position.w` (invariant, and linear, so exact on any polygon). It is cut by
`GL_CLIP_DISTANCE2` in the world vertex shader: the PDO programs keep `w < D + 1`, the plain ones `w > D - 1`. The 2-unit
overlap means there's no seam, and both write the same depth there. The plain programs keep early depth testing against
the pre-pass. `D` is `Parallax3.y`: `vr_parallax_depth_distance` (archived, default 0 = `vr_parallax_distance`, at
most that). Beyond the parallax's distance `ParallaxReach` is 0, so the depth-writing shader wrote the surface's own
depth there anyway. At the default the picture is the same: paused eyeshots with the split on and off differ by 88k/66k
pixels (L/R), and two shots with it off differ by 84k/67k (the scene's own flicker); peak 92/102 both ways.
`scratch/pdw_look_nosplit_split_debug.png` shows them (no split | split | `vr_parallax_debug`). The retro decals'
plain twin (`world_decal_retro`) is now made at map load beside the PDO one (`R_PrewarmDecalPrograms`), only while the
depth write is on. `vr_parallax_depth_split` (CVAR_NONE, 1; Debug > Views > Parallax Depth Split) is the A/B.
`vr_world_fragments` prints `split N at D`.

| AD fight (`play_ad_tfuma_fight`, 2 x 600 frames, exclusive, High) | shaded / pass | eyes GPU ms | world+brush |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth write on, no split (as before) | 5.30 M | 4.10 | 2.94 |
| split at the parallax distance (1024, the default; same picture) | 3.35 M | 3.30 | 2.13 |
| split at 512 (`vr_parallax_depth_distance 512`; flat depth past 512) | 2.52 M | 2.87 | 1.73 |
| split at 256 | 1.85 M | not timed | |
| depth write off | 1.68 M | 2.01 | 1.02 |
| Ultra preset (depth write on, split) | | 3.57 | 2.29 |

**Defaults (his decision):** the split saves 0.8 ms, but the depth write still costs 1.3 ms, more than the 0.4 ms
target. So `vr_parallax_depth_write` is now 0 by default (High) and 1 in Ultra (`presetRows`; Medium's own 0 is gone, it
is the default now). Config 192 moves configs still at the old default 1 to 0; custom values stay (checked:
`vr_cfg_version` 141 → 192, the value 1 → 0; Ultra sets 1 and High sets it back to 0). SETTINGS.md's preset table is
updated: High 2.0 ms, Ultra 3.6 ms.

**Not tried / next:** early rejection inside the depth-writing shader. After the pre-pass, a compute pass would build a
4x4-tile "farthest depth" copy of the eye's depth (all MSAA samples). The PDO shading would discard at once any fragment
whose nearest possible hit (the relief's top) is behind its tile's farthest. That's exact, and it would cut most of the
remaining 1.67 M hidden fragments (an estimated 0.6-0.8 ms). Its cost: the tile pass (about 0.05-0.1 ms an eye), each
eye/multiview/mirror FBO's depth as a texture, and the coarse-shading tiles. That could bring the depth write under
0.4 ms. Also open: drawing the far relief with flat depth (`vr_parallax_depth_distance 512`, 0.86 ms over off) changes
how things meet the relief past 512 units.

In VR: Graphics > Surfaces > Parallax Depth Write is off now. Turn it on (or pick Ultra) and look at monsters' feet and
props on raised floors near and far: it should look as before, for about 1.3 ms in big AD maps (0.8 ms less than before).
## One wall blow a swing (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/wallhit2`, 2026-10-23)

1.1 open issue (meleewall's numbers): crowbar and shotgun swings into a wall sometimes struck it twice, a doubled thunk,
sparks and mark.

The harness, committed this time: `Misc/quakevr/melee_wall_takes.sh <agent> [sets] [name]` (and `.py`). Every melee
take of his (`motions/`, eval.sh's TAKES; not poses, misses, grabs or charges) with its weapon, the axe takes also with
the crowbar and the shotgun (gun bash), replayed in one `vr_motion_eval` in vrmelee-recording with the take's dummy put
at the north wall: the wall at the dummy's front, 8, 16 and 24 units nearer (the player stepped back off the wall where
his box would be in it) and 10 past it. It counts each replay's wall blows (`melee event: ..., a wall`, developer 1).
New for it (`vr_motion_play.cpp`, test options of `vr_motion_play` and `vr_motion_eval`, MOTIONS.md "Evaluation"):
`at <x y z yaw>` (the take's dummy at a point), `weapon <id>` (the main hand's weapon), and per-take options on a
`list` line after a bar. The axe slash takes are also swung twice (the blow's 0.7 s played again straight after it:
two real blows) to check that a second real blow still lands.

Why a swing struck twice (each pair of wall blows logged with the weapon's distance off the wall between them):

- **The weapon still on the wall** (the crowbar): an overhead or diagonal swing laid the bar along the wall; its chisel
  end struck, the hand slowed against the wall (VR_Melee_Rearm re-arms a slowed hand), and 0.4-0.6 s later, past the
  0.35 s re-hit wait, the hook struck the same wall, the bar never more than 4 units off it.
- **The swing's recovery poking the wall again** (the sword's tip, the shotgun's muzzle): a strong blow (6-30 m/s), then
  0.6-1.1 s later, the weapon drawn 13-24 units back, a slow jab or stab (2.6-4.6 m/s) of the same motion's return.
- Left as they are: **a wind-up bump**, only with the wall 8-24 units nearer than the dummy was (the gun's barrel already
  at the wall as the take starts): a slow muzzle jab (2.6-3.5 m/s, a gun bash counts from 2 m/s) as the gun comes up,
  then the real blow. The first can't be told from a light jab when it lands; none at the dummy's front.
- Not the cause: separate hand and blade contacts (one decision a frame, VR_Melee_Sweep), the sweep on two frames in a
  row (the 0.35 s wait): every second blow came 0.36-1.1 s after the first.

The fix (`QC/vr_melee.qc`, VR_Melee_WallFresh, VR_Melee_WallLeft): a hand's wall blow remembers that wall's plane. The
same wall (normals within VR_MELEE_WALL_SAME, the contact within 4 units of the plane) is struck again only once the
weapon has been **0.2 m off it** since (VR_MELEE_WALL_OFF: near end, grip and far end), and within **1.2 s** of the blow
only by one at least **0.6 times as fast** (VR_MELEE_WALL_FOLLOW, VR_MELEE_WALL_WEAKER). Another wall (a corner) at
once; `vr_melee_wall_hold 0` as before. No cvar or default changed. Developer 2 prints each refused one.

Numbers (mock, 625 replays: replays struck / with two or more wall blows):

| weapon (takes x 5 spots) | struck before / after | two+ before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| axe (20) | 71 / 71 | 0 | 0 |
| crowbar (the axe's 20) | 76 / 76 | 9 | 1 |
| shotgun (the axe's 20) | 74 / 74-75 | 19 | 11 |
| sword (29) | 125 / 125 | 7 | 2 |
| fists (36 punches, slaps) | 88 / 88 | 0 | 0 |
| two real blows 0.7 s apart (13 axe slashes; axe, crowbar, shotgun) | - | - | 13/13, 12/12, 13/13 struck twice |

At the dummy's front: crowbar 0, shotgun 3 -> 0, sword 0. What is left is at 8-24 units nearer: the shotgun's wind-up
bumps (10), one shotgun jab at 10.6 m/s then a swing at 8.0 with the gun drawn 15 units back between (two blows by the
rules), one crowbar (chisel 4.9 then 5.9 m/s, the bar drawn 10 units off between), one sword recovery stab (refused
at 3.1 m/s, struck a frame later at 3.9) and one sword's wind-up stab. The same list in one run can differ by a replay
from another (state carried from take to take: shotgun 74 / 75 struck). eval.sh: verdicts as the baseline (169/177;
five damage readings 0.1 off, PASS -> PASS).

## Parallax depth write: the tiles' early-out (tried 2026-10-23, not shipped)

Kept for reference on the local branch `agent/pdepthhiz` (b0ac8d3f4), not merged (the author, 2026-10-23: "Don't ship the
pre-pass"). After the opaque world's depth pre-pass a compute pass reduced the eye's depth to each 4x4 tile's farthest
depth (every MSAA sample), and the depth-writing parallax programs discarded, per 2x2 quad, any fragment whose nearest
reachable relief depth was behind its tile (`vr_parallax_depth_cull`). The picture was unchanged (eyeshot diffs within
the scene's own flicker), but it didn't pay on the author's NVIDIA driver, AD fight bench (exclusive, 2 x 600 frames,
depth write on with the split, eyes' GPU ms): off 2.01; on 3.40; on with tiles built but unused 3.76; on with the
early-out 3.35. The tile pass costs ~0.36 ms (likely the driver decompressing the 4x MSAA depth to read it as a
texture), the early-out saves ~0.41: net ~0.05, noise; even free tiles would leave the depth write ~0.9 ms over off
(the pre-pass's own depth-writing shader and the late depth test remain), and CPU busy rose ~0.25 ms (per-pass GL
queries). So `vr_parallax_depth_write` stays off in High and on in Ultra with the near split (section "Parallax depth
write's cost").

### Armed grunts: presentation (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/agpresent`, 2026-10-23)

From his notes of 2026-10-23 (vrtesthall 15-35-21 .. 15-38-47): punches instead of the shove, melee weapons held blade
up and swung, the crowbar sounding like a crowbar, a running chainsaw, the hands jittering on the weapons.

- **The jitter's cause** (measured: `vr_agrunt_ik_debug -1` prints `agj` lines, `scratch/agjit.py` the frame-to-frame
  second difference of the IK targets in the grunt's space; shotgun grunt hunting you, `vr_agrunt_test 106`): the IK
  turned the weapon's place into the grunt's space with `e->origin`, where its *next step ends*, not where the body is
  drawn (the step lerp, up to 15 units behind): a sawtooth of up to 15 units each step. Right grip rms 2.02 (max 15),
  left 2.03 (max 15). Drawn frame (`render::drawnPlace`): 0.11 / 0.19 (max 2); left was the server's prop lagging the
  drawn poses by a tick or two (a kink at each frame change). Now the weapon is drawn on the client from the drawn body
  (below) and the animation's hand eased over 40 ms (a shot's frames are drawn unlerped: the hand jumped 7.4 units):
  right rms 0.16, p95 0.044 (was 0.32); left rms 0.23, p95 0.13 (was 0.60); the max left (3-4) is the recoil kick.

  hand plus `v` (its body's space), the weapon's turn in its body's space or its drawn rifle line's (`wo`), the left

shotgun grunt running and shooting: both hands still on the gun, the kick.

### Armed grunts: gameplay (worktree `release`, branch `agent/agplay`, 2026-10-23)

The author's notes (vrtesthall_2026-10-23_15-38-47 .. 15-44-27): disarming was too easy (walk up, grab the shotgun);
an armed grunt's ragdoll and corpse took no gunfire or melee; a shove always dropped the weapon; grunts ran forever at
a weapon floating in water. New file `QC/vr_armedgrunt_play.qc` (its header has the rules), tests in
`QC/vr_armedgrunt_play_test.qc` (`vr_agrunt_test 20..27`).

**Ragdoll and corpse (the cause).** The armed grunt had its own `th_die` (`VR_AG_Die`, a copy of `army_die`), and the
corpse code keys the grunt on `th_die == army_die` (combat.qc `VR_Corpse_Parts`: corpse health, head, gibs; also
vr_smallgibs.qc): its corpse was never armed as a gibbable body (no `takedamage`, shots went through to the floor).
Fix: its `th_die` is the grunt's `army_die`; `army_die` asks `VR_AG_Dying()` (its weapon falls instead of the grunt's
rifle). The engine side already shared the grunt's rig (`vr_ragdoll.cpp` seeds `Id::VrGrunt` as `Id::Soldier`).
`VR_AG_Die` stays as a stub calling `army_die` (old saves). Test 20: a grunt and an armed grunt side by side, knocked
down alive then killed: both take the same pellets alive (8, 8) and as corpses (8, 8 of 160), both gib.

**Disarming rules** (Combat > Armed Grunts, Disarming):
- Grabbing its weapon starts a tug-of-war (`vr_agrunt_tug` 1). It holds on, faces you, your hand is jerked towards it
  with haptics (`handimpact`, rising buzz as you gain). You win by keeping your hand pulled back
  `vr_agrunt_tug_pull` (10 units) or more from where you grabbed, away from it, for `vr_agrunt_tug_time` (1.2 s) in all
  (easing off loses progress at half the rate). Hurt, the time is times its share of health (at least 0.35); while it
  flinches from a hit, half. About every `vr_agrunt_tug_fight` (1 s) it fights back: a gun fires at you (40%), shoves
  you off (30%) or headbutts you (30%, 6 damage times `vr_agrunt_damage_scale`, a view punch, a push); fists and melee
  weapons only headbutt (they never shove). A shove or a headbutt breaks your grip; letting go, or your hand ending 64
  units from the weapon, loses too; 0.8 s before you can grab again. Won: the weapon is in your hand.
- A grab takes it at once when it is staggering or knocked down, stunned by a parry (`vr_parry_stagger_until`), down to
  `vr_agrunt_tug_hurt` (0.35) of its health, or taken unawares (not fighting you, you behind it).
- A blow on its gun hand or arm of `vr_agrunt_disarm_damage` (10) knocks it loose, half that while it is shaky (above).
- Your weapon's parry of its melee blow (its punch, swing or thrust: `VR_AG_Striking`, now a melee monster's blow for
  `VR_Parry_MeleeMonster`) knocks the weapon away with the chance `vr_agrunt_parry_disarm` (0.35; a well-timed parry
  1.5x). Its shoves' parries don't.

**Shoves and falls** (`vr_agrunt_fall_drop` 1): a stagger never drops the weapon. Knocked down onto the floor, it lets
go 0.4 s into the fall, beside it (20-50 u/s); getting up it goes for its own weapon first (within 160 units, whoever is
nearer), if you haven't taken it. Off: a knockdown keeps the weapon.

**Weapon reach** (`VR_AG_Reachable`): it only goes for a weapon not in a liquid, resting on a floor (within 40 units
under it), the way there probed every 12 units: a floor all along, no step up or down over 18 units, no liquid, no wall
at 24 units up. Going for one, it gives it up when it gets no nearer for 2.5 s, after `vr_agrunt_seek_timeout` (6 s),
or when the weapon is out of reach on a recheck (every 0.5 s), and leaves it alone for `vr_agrunt_seek_shun` (20 s).
Also: an unarmed grunt goes for a weapon before the stealth AI's walk or look-about (ai.qc: the `VR_AG_Idle` check moved
ahead of `VR_Stealth_Walk`/`VR_Stealth_Stand`; an alerted unarmed grunt walking to its post never re-armed).

**Notes.** The grabbing bit reads clear in other entities' thinks (fast mode at least): the tug's "let go" uses the
release time (`mainhand_lastreleasetime`, kept in the player's think). A tug won hands over the weapon with
`forcegrabCatching` (`wpnthrow_handtouch_ent` wants a grab begun in the last 0.125 s). The held weapon is drawn
client-side from the body (agent/agpresent): the tug doesn't move it towards your hand (the feel is haptics and the
hand's jerks).

**Tests** (vrtesthall, `vr_mock_hand main 0.1 0.72 -1.2 65 0 0`; 21-23 with `+grabmain` held): 20 ragdoll/corpse PASS 3;
21 tug: begun, held still 2 s it holds on, pulled 16 units it is yours after 1.21 s (need 1.20) PASS 3; 22 an axe grunt
fighting back every 0.3 s headbutts you off, keeps the axe PASS 2; 23 calm '' / stunned / hurt / staggering / knocked
down, a hurt grunt's gun grabbed at once PASS 3; 24 a blow of 6 on the hand: calm keeps it, hurt drops it; its swing
parried: disarmed PASS 2; 25 staggered keeps it, floored drops it 14-22 units away, gets up and takes it back PASS 3;
26 a shotgun floating in the pool and one in the air ignored (4 s, it never steps into the pool), one on the floor taken
PASS 2; 27 no nearer for 3 s: given up, shunned, not found again PASS 1. `vr_agrunt_test 3` now sets `vr_agrunt_tug 0`
(the grab at once) and puts it back.

**Blows and throws on the weapon itself** (`VR_AG_WeaponStruck`, every frame in the prop's think): your hand, or what
it holds (its line from the hand to its muzzle), meeting the held weapon's line (8 units behind its grip to its muzzle,
5 units round) at `vr_agrunt_disarm_swing` (4.5 m/s: a hit lands from `vr_melee_speed` 3.2, so a deliberate hard swing,
not a tap) knocks it out along the blow; a thrown weapon, prop or gib whose last frame's path meets it with a momentum
of `vr_agrunt_disarm_throw` (20 kg m/s: a 2 kg weapon at 10 m/s; a gib or a shell tossed is far under; a full hit
stagger is `vr_hit_stagger_throw_ref` 60) knocks it out along the throw. Tests 29 (2 m/s kept, 6 m/s out) and 30 (a
nailgun at 3 m/s kept, at 14 m/s out).

**Every disarm's sound** (`VR_AG_DisarmFeedback`: hand and weapon hits, throws, parries, tugs and grabs, falls): the
weapon's clatter by kind (a gun `vr/phys/metal_h1-4`, a blade `metal_m1-4`, Mjolnir `wood_h1-4`: the physics props'
own) and the grunt's pain sound, at most every 0.6 s.

**Held weapons are no loot** (the author's note): the loot beams skip an entity with the held flag (`vr_lootbeams.cpp`,
effects 128: QC `VR_AG_EF_HELD`), and `VR_Forcegrab_IsEligible` names `vr_ag_weapon` (it was already not eligible: no
`FL_FORCEGRABBABLE`, not `weapon_touch`; the pointing sparkles only follow eligible targets). Test 28 with
`vr_lootbeams_report`: holding, the weapon not eligible and only the map's own weapon beamed (before: the held shotgun
too); dropped, the lying shotgun eligible and beamed.

**In VR:** grab a calm shotgun grunt's gun from the front and pull back hard (about 25 cm) for a second or so: the
hand should buzz and jerk, it should headbutt, shove or fire at you now and then; grab one that's staggered by a shove,
hurt or parried: yours at once; shove one: it keeps the gun unless it falls, then the gun lies beside it and it picks
it up as it rises; drop a weapon into the pool at vrtesthall's side: grunts should leave it alone; swing the crowbar
hard into a grunt's gun, throw a weapon at it: knocked out, with a clang and a grunt; no loot beam on a held gun.
Sliders: Combat > Armed Grunts (Disarming: Blow on Its Weapon, Throw at Its Weapon, Tug-of-War and its four sliders,
Parry Disarm Chance, Drops It When Floored; Gives Up on a Weapon After, Leaves It Alone For).

His notes (e5start 17-51, 17-52, start 17-53): his water foam values as the defaults; the band "breathing" in and out
unevenly round the shore; foam particles where the foam meets the rock so the edge isn't one straight line; lava,

  amount): water `vr_water_foam_*`, lava `vr_lava_foam_*`, slime `vr_slime_foam_*`, each `_on`, `_opacity`,
  `_frequency`, `_strength`, `_breathe`, `_breathe_speed`, `_breathe_irregularity`, `_red`/`_green`/`_blue` (0..2: over 1
  glows), `_particles`, `_particle_life`, `_particle_opacity`, `_particle_size`. Teleports have no foam. Water: his

## The flail lying about keeps its ball and chain (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/flailprop`, 2026-10-23)

His ask: a dropped, thrown or monster-dropped flail keeps its head and chain, like the fuel tanks lying about. Built on
the plan in "The flail: heavier, smaller".

- **The head lying about** (QC `vr_ad_melee.qc`, "The flail lying about"): `CreateThrownWeapon` (a hand's drop or throw,
  a death sergeant's drop, the toolgun's dispenser) calls `VR_FlailHead_Attach`: a `vr_flailhead` prop
  (`progs/w_blueflail.mdl#flailhead`, `vr_rigid`, `.vr_prop_mass` `vr_flail_mass`). A hand can carry it
  (`VR_Carry_Setup`), but it cannot be force grabbed on its own (no `FL_FORCEGRABBABLE`): force grab the handle and
  the head trails it. Handle and head name each other by the fuel tanks' `.vr_fuellink`. The head goes when its
  handle is no longer its flail lying about (`VR_FlailHead_Think`, as the tanks). `VR_FlailHead_Frame` (StartFrame,
  every 0.5 s) gives a head to any flail lying about without one (an older save, a head the toolgun removed).
  `vr_flail_world` (new, 1; AD Weapons > Death Sergeant's Flail: Head Lying About) 0: the handle alone. Needs AD's
  data (`vr_ad_mounted`).
- **Hand to world, world to hand:** after each step the engine leaves each hand's head place and speed on the player
  (`.vr_flail_head`/`headvel`, `.vr_flail_offhead`/`offheadvel`; `vr_box3d_flail.cpp noteHeldHeads`). Let go of, the
  head lying about is made there at that speed (the head nearer the handle, with two flails), sparing the player's
  body for 1 s as the tanks do. Taking the handle (`wpnthrow_handtouch_impl` calls `VR_FlailHead_Taken`): QC writes the
  lying head's place, speed and the time (`.vr_flail_taken`/`offtaken`) and removes it. The hand's head is made there
  (`make`, within 0.5 s; brought within its chain of the handle's end if it lay farther), at that speed. A death
  sergeant's, the toolgun's or an old save's: beside the handle, 0.9 of the chain off its right, falling with it.
- **The rope** (`vr_box3d.cpp syncPropRopes`, was `syncFuelRopes`, generalised): a kind per rope (`World::RopeKind`
  Tank, Flail). A flail's rope runs from the handle's tip (`admelee::tipOf`: the made model's MuzzleAnchor, through
  `held::drawnPoint`, new: the drawn transform of one model point, the bodies' frame) to the head's ring
  (`admelee::flailRingReach` 3.5 units along +x, shared now by the held head and its drawing). It is
  `vr_flail_chain` long, the held rope less the ring's reach. `box3d::forEachFlailRope` (new) lists them with their
  ends' distance now.
- **The chain drawn** (`vr_adtank.cpp`'s world lines, generalised): `stepWorld`'s Verlet line (falls, lies on the
  world, rests once still) is now `stepLine`. The tanks' hoses and the flails' chains (`stepFlail`: the ring to the
  tip, `flail::lyingEnds`) share the 8 nearest world lines, and the chains use `flail::chainStyle` (the hands'
  links, rusted and faceted: `drawHose` passes the cord's rust and flatness).
- **Info:** `vr_flail_info` also prints the flails lying about: handles, heads, pairs, orphan heads, handles without a
  head, and each rope's tip-to-ring distance against its length (`PAST` if over). `vr_adgun_hose_info` prints each
  drawn chain.
- **Debug menu** (AD Monsters page): Flail Lying With Its Head (`vr_ad_test 169`), Drop the Main Hand's Flail (166),
  Take the Nearest Flail (167), Kick the Nearest Flail (168), Carry the Nearest Flail's Head (170), Flails Lying

no jump. Pick it up by the handle with the head lying a little away: the head should stay where it lay and swing up
on the chain. Carry the head and drag the flail by it, force grab the handle. Kill a death sergeant. Check the chain's
look lying, and the head's size beside the handle (the head is the held one's size; the handle lying about is the
weapon slot's).

**Notes:** the chain lying about collides with the world only, not with props (as the hoses). The head lying about
is a prop: thrown, it hurts as props do, not as the held head's blows (`VR_Flail_Hit`). A remote client sees the head
and its rope, but no chain (a listen server's, as the hoses).
## Crates: one hit (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/cratehit`, 2026-10-23)

His note (vrstart 2026-10-23 15-29-14): one very strong punch or melee-weapon hit still breaks a crate; the press fix
(agent/proppush2) suspected.

**The test was misleading.** `vr_prop_strike_test` stepped the mock hand once per server frame; the client's frames are
not the server's (fast mode: fewer, real time: more), so the hand reached the game in jumps and the poses' clock (real
time) did not match: blows read from 0.5 to 4.6 times the strike's speed (an axe at 5 m/s: 5.3, 18.1, 23 m/s). The
earlier "18.24 m/s before the fix" was very likely this too. Now the strike is one move the mock glides through on its
own frames (`vr_mock_hand_glide`, real time): **run it with `-RealTime`** (a fist reads 5.00, 7.00, 9.00, 12.00 m/s).
Developer 3 traces the hand each frame (tracked, drawn, the game's, held off the level); `vr_debug_weight 1` now says
why a held weapon was put back in the hand.

**Old build vs next** (crate 107, the strike down onto its top, default hand pose, -RealTime; strikes to break, the
blows' read speeds in m/s; old = 4a7269606, the merge before proppush2, with the test added):

| weapon (heft) | 5 m/s old / next | 7 | 9 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fist (1.00) | no blow / no blow | no blow / no blow | 2 (9.00) / 1 (8.99) | 1 / 1 (12.0) |
| crowbar (1.41) | 2 (6.30, 6.48) / 1 (6.47) | 1 (8.63) / 1 (8.84) | 1 / 1 (8.65) | no blow / no blow |
| axe (1.41) | 2 (5.76, 5.74) / 2 (5.75, 5.76) | 1 (9.27) / 1 (9.23) | 1 (11.9) / 1 (11.6) | 1 / 1 (10.4) |
| sword (1.48) | 1 (6.30) / 1 (6.47) | 1 (8.65) / 1 (8.83) | 1 / 1 (8.4) | 1 / 1 (7.2) |

Next is the old build within noise (crowbar 5 m/s: 6.30 is 0.99 of the break, 6.47 just over). The press fix and the
muzzle fix leave nothing behind. (A fist straight ahead, in the earlier matrix: 5 m/s 8.3 a blow, 7 m/s two, 9 and
12 one, as designed. Down at 5-7 m/s a hammer fist is under the punch's need; the crowbar's chop at 12 ends past the
top before its arc reads: test geometry, the same in both.)

**By design.** Intensity = blow speed x heft / 9 m/s; from 1 the crate breaks, from 0.5 it loses (2i - 1) of 75. So a
punch breaks a small crate at 9 m/s (two at 7, nine at 5), and the crowbar and axe (heft 1.41) at 6.4 m/s, the
sword (1.48) at 6.1 m/s, of the hand's speed. Held weapons also read 1.2-1.3 times the hand's speed in this test: the
weight's spring lags a hand that starts at full speed at once, then catches up faster than it (real swings speed up
gradually, less of it). A strong swing (8-12 m/s at the hand) breaks a crate with any weapon, a strong punch (9+) too.

**What did inflate blows (fixed).** With the weapon tipped down (the strike ahead, `vr_mock_hand main 0.15 1.25 -0.35
-45 0 0`) its head slid along the floor: the level's hold (vr_handpose) moved the hand's target 26 cm at once as it took
hold and let go; the weight took the target's jump for a hand's jump and put the lagging weapon back in the hand at once
(20-25 cm in a frame), unmarked: the melee's own jump test starts at 30 cm, so it read a blow at 17-25 m/s. Only the
half-turn flip set `VR_HANDJUMP_*` before; now every put-back does (`vr_weight.cpp`). The same strikes:

| strike ahead, head on the floor | crowbar 5 / 7 / 9 m/s | axe 5 / 7 / 9 / 12 |
|---|---|---|
| next | 6.30, 17.67 / 24.96 / 19.93 | 5.81, 5.74 / 9.28 / 23.76 / 4.49, 10.35 |
| fixed | 6.27, 6.28 / 8.85 / 8.35 | 6.03, 9.50 / 9.24 / 11.88 / 10.36 |

In play: a heavy weapon swung along or off the floor or a wall into a crate or a monster. eval.sh: verdicts as the baseline (169/177, none changed; 8 takes differ in an event or the hand error, the canary escalated to the full set).

**If he wants crates tougher** (not changed): Crates > Breaking > Break Speed (`vr_prop_break_speed`, 9 m/s for a
small crate's 75 health; wood x1). At 12: a punch breaks it from 12 m/s (two from about 9), a crowbar or axe from
8.5 m/s; at 14: 14 and 9.9. Large crates and barrels scale by the square root of their health already.

- [ ] Punch a small crate hard (as hard as you can): one; a medium punch: two or three. Same for the crowbar and axe:
  a full swing breaks it, a moderate one takes two.
- [ ] Swing the axe or crowbar along the floor into a crate (the head scraping first): no one-hit break from a slow
  scrape.
