### Struggling enemies look at you

Author's note (2026-10-23): a living humanoid in active ragdoll form, dragged or held by its legs, torso or shoulders
(or lifted), should turn its head to look at him where it can: straight at him with its belly towards him or held up
before him, to the side when it faces away, trying to see him. It reads as alive, less uncanny.

`vr_ragstruggle.cpp`, `lookAtHolder`, after `bodyTargets` each struggle frame: its head's target (its turn in its
parent's rest space) slerped towards a look at the holder's head over the struggle's own head moves. The aim: his head
from its neck in its parent's (the chest's) frame, as a turn about the spine (yaw) and a nod (pitch), each clamped to
0.9 of its neck's twist and cone (the drive clamps again at 0.95). With him behind it the yaw goes as far as the neck
turns, to the side he is on; that side is kept while he is straight behind (within about 12 degrees), so the head
doesn't flip. The aim eases (0.12 s) and makes small quick re-aims (saccades: up to 4.6 degrees of turn and 2.9 of nod,
every 0.3-1.2 s, seeded per enemy). The look's weight eases (0.25 s) to `vr_struggle_look` times (1 - held by its
head) times its effort's ramp (none at no effort: a flinch dips it); none beheaded or with the neck snapped (`headPart`,
`jointOk`: a cut or loose joint). The head channel's strength is at least `vr_struggle_look_strength` times the
weight (then times effort, `vr_struggle_strength` and the grip guard, like every struggling muscle). Dying ends the
struggle and its strengths let go, as before.

New cvars (Enemies > Struggle > Behaviours, and the ragdoll tool's Struggle group): `vr_struggle_look` 0.9 (0..1; 0
never), `vr_struggle_look_strength` 0.6 (0..0.9).

`vr_struggle_status`'s hold line ends with "its head looks N deg from you, turning M deg/s" (its head's rest +x from
the way to your head; its spin against its parent's). `struggle_test.py`: new case `shoulderdrag` (the right upper arm,
walked back; judged on the drag only), `STRUGGLE_LOOK=1` adds `<case>_nolook` runs (`vr_struggle_look 0`) and a LOOK
line per case, `STRUGGLE_STATUS_EVERY` (s, default 0.3) for more samples.

Grunt, the later two thirds' mean (status every 0.1 s; three runs identical), look on (no look):

| case | head from you | head spin |
|---|---|---|
| lift (shoulders, held up) | 9 deg (9) | 25 deg/s (26) |
| leglift (hung by the legs) | 56 (80) | 0 (20) |
| legdrag (one shin, lying) | 48 (100) | 29 (30) |
| legpull (both shins, pulled down, dragged) | 67 (110) | 45 (34) |
| armdrag (forearm) | 27 (73) | 87 (168) |
| shoulderdrag (upper arm) | 20 (22) | 25 (17) |
| headdrag (head held: no look) | 28 (28) | 65 (65) |

Held up by the shoulders it already looked at you (Swat's aim); held by the head nothing changes. The spin's rise in
legpull and shoulderdrag is the saccades (each a quick dart). The struggle cases with `_off` all pass (leads, lag
against off, poses; the drags 71-94 percent), `dead` passes, `eval.sh` as the baseline. Eyeshots (looking down 50
degrees, 3 s in; `scratch/hl_<case>_<1|0>.png`, 1 the look on): legpull's grunt, belly up, faces you; without, its head
lolls aside.

**In VR:** drag a grunt by its legs (belly up and belly down), hold one up by the legs, by the shoulders, drag one by
an arm: its head should find you and follow you as you move, with small darts, never snapping from side to side when
you are straight behind it. Hold its head: no look. Kill it while held: its head goes limp. Tune Look at You / Look
Strength (Enemies > Struggle) if it stares too hard or too weakly.
## Blade shape editor (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/bladeedit`, 2026-10-23)

Approved by the author: an in-VR editor for what a weapon's blows strike with, curved blades first.

**Per-slot data** (vr_weapons.inc, "The blade's shape"; `Quake/vr/vr_blade.hpp`). New Weapon Offsets keys, cvars
`vr_wofs_bl_*_NN`; every default keeps the shape the code gave before (no migration, no wofs version bump):
- `bl_near` (BladeNear, -1): the near end (pommel, butt, handle's end) behind the hand, a share of the hand-to-tip line;
  -1 the kind's own (QC `VR_Melee_NearBack`: a sword 0.3, an axe 0.25, the chainsaw 0.1, the crowbar 0.78, a gun 0.3).
- `bl_width` (BladeWidth, 1): times the swept points' radius (`VR_MELEE_RADIUS` 3 x `vr_melee_range_multiplier`).
- `bl_spine` (BladeSpine, 0) and `bl_s1_off`/`_side` .. `bl_s5_off`/`_side`: 0 the model's own curve (the curved AD
  swords' made spine, `admelee::bend`; else straight), 1 a Catmull-Rom spline through the hand, five points at 1/6 ..
  5/6 of the line and the tip, each off the line along its normal in the blade's plane and along the model's +y (shares
  of its length, as `admeleebend`). Any weapon held by its handle can have one (not only swords); `vr_melee_curved_blades
  0` still straightens all.
- `bl_head` (BladeHead, 0) and `bl_head_lo_x/y/z`, `bl_head_hi_x/y/z`: 0 the model's own head (the AD hammer's and
  mace's), 1 this box (shares of the line, as `admeleehead`): any weapon can get a head that strikes as a volume.
- The tip stays the Muzzle anchor plus Muzzle X/Y/Z (the editor's tip handle edits the offset).

**QC** (`vr_melee.qc`): `VR_Melee_ShapeOf` (in `VR_Melee_Line`) reads the hand's weapon's slot and shape; the near end
(`VR_Melee_NearBackOf`, held or carried off its handle), the curve (`VR_Melee_BendLine`: `vr_mline_bend` -1 - slot, read
by `VR_Melee_At`), the head (`VR_Melee_HeadOf`, the track's `mh_hd_lo/hi`) and the width (`mh_bwidth`, the radius in
`VR_Melee_Sweep`) follow. Every consumer of the layout goes through these (the swept ribs, the decapitation share, the
hit sounds and parts, the wall checks, parry's and the wall buttons' near-to-far line, the Shadow Axe's floor chops,
the hot blade, the motion recorder's points). Parry keeps the chord (near end to tip), as before for the fury's curve.
The VR builtin numbers are all taken (900 + 179 < 1080): no new builtins. `weapondrawnpose(p, hand, 7)_x` is the slot
(from the hand's weaponmodel/weaponmodel2, server side), and `admeleebend`/`admeleehead` with a kind below 0 read slot
-1 - kind's own curve, head and '<near> <width> <flags>' (vr_builtins.cpp).

**Editor** (`Quake/vr/vr_bladeedit.cpp`; Weapon Offsets > Posing Mode > Edit Blade Shape; Debug > Views > Edit Blade
Shape (Main Hand), Print Blade Shape). Holster Setup's pattern, but the game goes on (the hands strike as they would;
the buttons are the editor's, the sticks don't move the player) and Show Melee Blades is forced on (put back on
leaving), so QC's own blow line and sweeps show the edited shape live. Over it, the blade as its settings lay it
(computed client-side from the hand and muzzle the server gets: the same point as QC's `VR_Melee_At(0.5)` to 0.01
unit), its width as a tube, and handles the other hand's grip drags (the grabbed point keeps its offset to the hand):
red tip (Muzzle X/Y/Z, solved through the drawn weapon's muzzle per unit of offset), orange near end, blue width,
green curve points (the first drag seeds all five from the curve shown: the model's or straight), pink head corners
(when it has a head). Haptics on reaching a handle, on grabbing, every unit dragged, on letting go. Panel: Undo, Reset
Blade (the blade keys and the tip offset to the shipped defaults), Straighten (a straight curve of its own), Head Box
On/Off (a box of its own, seeded from the model's head or a small box at the tip), Cancel (everything as on entering),
Done (prints `vr_blade_dump`). B/Y undoes, the menu button is Done; it leaves (keeping) if the weapon leaves the hand,
the map changes or a menu opens. Commands: `vr_bladeedit [main|off]`, `vr_bladeedit_done|_cancel|_undo|_reset`,
`vr_bladeedit_press <0..5>`, `vr_bladeedit_report` (each handle along the line, P, Y; the curve's 0.5 point),
`vr_blade_dump [slot 1..]` (the slot's tip offset and blade keys as `QVR_WEAPON_DEFAULT` lines, `//*` changed). Mock:
`vr_mock_hand_to <hand> bladehandle <i> [<along> <normal> <flat>]`, `bladebutton <i>`.

**Tests** (scripts in `scratch/`: `bl_dump.sh`, `bl_shape.sh`, `bl_edit.sh`; `-Games "-game hipnotic -game rogue
-game ad -game quakevr"`, ad_dm1):
- Defaults unchanged: `vr_melee_sweep_test 2` (new `QC/vr_blade_test.qc`: the main hand's near end, far end, every
  layout point in the hand's frame, the head box and radius) for 16 melee weapons (axe, Mjolnir, knight sword, chainsaw,
  crowbar, MG3 hammer, shotgun, the fury's, death knight's, death guard's swords, mace, hammer, the four monster swords):
  origin/next's QC (built with the dump added) and this branch's give the same 147 lines; the largest number difference
  0.0004 units, the run-to-run noise of the mock hand (two runs of this branch: 0.0003). `eval.sh`: 169/177 pass (the 8
  known failures), no verdict changed; 4 takes' damage moved by 0.1, among them a straight punch (the fist's path does
  not touch the new code: the baseline's drift).
- Edited shapes strike as drawn: `vr_melee_sweep_test 3` (new): a box just outside the curve's bow is struck by the
  curve and missed by the straight line, one just inside the other way; a box 1.5 radii past the tip missed at width 1,

**Notes.** The sweep strikes with the layout's points (9 on a sword) and the straight lines between neighbours: a very

### Crates: two strong hits (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/cratetough`, 2026-10-23; vr_cfg_version 195)

His request: no single realistic strong blow (a punch up to ~12 m/s, a full weapon swing up to ~10-11 m/s of the hand
with its heft) breaks a crate; two strong blows do, medium ones take 3-4.

- **Why the break speed alone could not.** With the old wear rule (worn from half the break speed, (2i - 1) of its
  health) the band between "two hits" (0.75) and "nothing" (0.5) is narrow: at 16 m/s a 12 m/s punch takes two, but a
  9 m/s punch eight and a 7 m/s one nothing; and a strong axe blow (11.5 m/s read x 1.41 = 16.3) still breaks it in one.
- **Change.** `vr_prop_break_speed` 9 -> **18** (config 195: configs at 9 move, custom values stay) and a new
  `vr_prop_blow_wear` **0.25** (Crates > Breaking > Blows Wear From): a hand's hit (a blow, or a prop held and smashed)
  wears a prop from 0.25 of its break speed, (i - 0.25) / 0.75 of its health. 0.25 x 18 = 4.5 m/s, the same lightest
  blow that marks a crate as before. Thrown and dropped props (their own `vr_crate_impact`, `vr_explobox_impact`,
  `vr_crate_piece_impact`) and a crate's pieces keep the old rule from half. QC `VR_Prop_WearFrom` /
  `VR_Prop_HandWearFrom` (`vr_carry.qc`).
- **Measured** (`vr_prop_strike_test`, -RealTime, vrtesthall with `vr_crates 0`, a fresh small crate 50 units ahead per
  case, the strike down onto its top unless "ahead"; strikes to break, 8 at most; old = this build at 9 / 0.5):

| weapon (heft) | 5 m/s old / new | 7 | 9 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fist down (1.00) | no blow / no blow | no blow / no blow | 1 / 3 (9.0) | 1 / 2 (12.0) |
| fist ahead (1.00) | 8+ (75 -> 5) / 8+ (75 -> 51) | 2 / 6 | 1 / 3 | 1 / 2 |
| crowbar (1.41) | 1 / 3 (6.45) | 1 / 2 (8.7) | 1 / 2 (8.65) | no blow / 8+ (one 7.6) |
| axe (1.41) | 2 / 4 (5.7) | 1 / 2 (9.1) | 1 / 2 (11.5) | 1 / 2 (10.4) |
| sword (1.48) | 1 / 3 (6.3) | 1 / 2 (8.65) | 1 / 2 (8.7) | 8+ / no blow |
| hammer (1.58) | 1 / 3 (6.7) | 1 / 2 (8.2) | 1 / 3 (5.9) | no blow / no blow |

  (the blows' read speeds in brackets; held weapons read about 1.2-1.3x the hand in this test, so "9 m/s" is already
  a harder blow than a real 9 m/s swing; "no blow" at 12 and down at 5-7 for the fist is the test's geometry, as in
  "Crates: one hit".) No single blow breaks a crate now; the hardest (axe at 11.5 x 1.41 = 0.91 of 18) takes two.
- **Side effects** (`vr_prop_impact_test 1` and the strike test on explosive boxes, old / new):
  - Explosive boxes follow the crates (16.7 m/s to blow up from a blow, was 8.4): a 12 m/s punch two, a 9 m/s punch
    three, the axe two (was one each). Thrown into a wall: the same (12.6 m/s unhurt, 15.4 blows up).
  - Held and smashed into a wall (not overhead): a crate breaks from 18 m/s; 13.5 m/s leaves 25 of 75 (old: 6.75 m/s
    left 37); a hard 12 m/s smash takes two. The overhead slam (`vr_carry_slam`) still breaks it at once and the thrown
    crate's hit on another crate is the throw's damage: neither reads the break speed (unchanged).
  - Thrown or dropped crates and pieces: unchanged (9.6 m/s unhurt, 13.6 damaged to 22, 17.6 broken).
  - AD's and the expansions' breakables scale with it too: glass (a vase, a window) 2.25 -> 4.5 m/s (still a light
    punch), wood as the crates, stone (a rubble wall, 10 health) 6.75 -> 13.5, metal (200 health) 22 -> 44 (a full axe
    swing wears it from 11 m/s: about eight to break, was three). Shots and blasts are unchanged.
- **Migration** (`vr_migrate_config`): 194 at 9 -> 18; 194 at 12 stays 12; 195 at 9 stays 9.

- [ ] Punch a crate as hard as you can: it takes two; a medium punch three or four; a light tap only pushes it.
- [ ] A full axe or crowbar swing: two; a moderate swing: three or four. The same on an explosive box (it blows up on
  the second strong hit).
- [ ] Smash a held crate into a wall hard twice: broken; the overhead slam still breaks it at once.

## Checklist: Pass, Fail and Test (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/checktest`, 2026-10-23)

To make headset testing faster, every checklist item now has three buttons on a row under its text: **Pass**, **Fail**,
**Test**. Left and right (or pointing the laser at one) pick a button; the pick stays from item to item, so a run of
passes is one press each. A click on the item's text does nothing (no accidental passes).

- **Pass** retires the item as a tick did (green `[x]`, dimmed; left out with Hide Ticked). **Fail** marks it red
  `[!]` and keeps it listed until a new line replaces it (its key is its text). Pressing the same again puts it back
  to untested; Undo Last Tick restores the previous mark (its help says which). The summary line counts the failed.
  Stored in `quakevr/checklist_ticks.txt` as before: passed items' text a line, failed ones after `[fail] `; an older
  file's lines are passes. `vr_checklist tick <n>` still toggles a pass; new `pass|fail|test <n>`.
- **Test** (dimmed when the item has no scene) runs the item's scenario: the line's trailing `{test:<id>}` (hidden,
  not part of its key) names `quakevr/scenarios/<id>.txt` (Quake/vr/vr_scenario.cpp; the format and how to write one:
  TESTING.md, "Checklist scenarios: how to write one"). One press loads the map fresh, sets the scenario's settings
  first, then once the map is in places you (spot and facing), puts its weapons in your hands (the toolgun's
  Weapons entries, taken as a grab takes them), places its toolgun spawns around you on the floor (monsters, armed
  grunts and enforcers with any weapon, crates, barrels, explosive boxes, corpses, flames, items), sets god/notarget/
  health, runs its commands, closes the menu and floats the hint (the line's text) ahead and a little low for
  `vr_scenario_hint_time` (new, 12 s; `vr_scenario hint` shows it again).
- The Checklist page's top: the test running, **Reset Test** (the same scene again from scratch; `vr_scenario reset`
  can be bound) and **End Test**. Settings a scene changes are put back by End Test, the next test, another map or a
  load; while the config is written they are written as they were before the test (their strings swapped for the
  file's write, no callbacks), so quitting mid-test never keeps them.
- Checks for workers and the coordinator: `vr_scenario validate` (every file: map present, spawn and weapon names in
  the toolgun's list, settings and commands exist; every checklist tag has its file), `vr_scenario runall quit [ids]`
  (each scene run headless in turn: SCNRUN OK/FAIL with the first problem), `vr_scenario where` (a `start` line, free
  distances, the nearest liquid's surface and extent). `cl_insert.py`'s lines stay plain text; a tag is just appended.

Scenes written for the [next branch] items (47 files, 59 of 65 lines tagged). No scene: parallax depth write and
graphics presets (look at his own maps through menu presets), Holster Calibration / menus / seated play (menus and
calibration), running legs (any floor). Shared scenes: `flail` (dropped flail, flail feel, Death Sergeant's flail),
`struggle_grunts` (head-look, struggle per group), `shoulder_charge` (all three charge items, an 800-unit lane),
`crates_melee` (both crate items), `mini_bosses` (tougher AD monsters, mini bosses, Death Fury), `ad_crossbow`,
`plasma_bolts`, `foam_pool`, `scorch_wall` (two each). Most are in vrtesthall (its pool for foam, blood in water, pyro
steam, flame into water, armed grunts falling near water; its south wall for wall blows, scorches and wall deaths).

**In VR:** Checklist page: pick Pass / Fail / Test with the stick and with the laser; the colours (green passed, red
failed) and the bracketed pick; Test on a few items (armed grunts row, crates, the pool with grunts, mini bosses):
right map, you face the scene, weapons in the right hands, the hint readable and not in the way; Reset Test; End Test
(Show Melee Blades goes off again after `melee_blades`).

## Voice notes carry more context and an instant replay (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/notectx`, 2026-10-23)

So that a worker can tell what he meant and reproduce it, each voice note now keeps (docs: [VOICENOTES.md](VOICENOTES.md)):

- **The checklist item** last under the Checklist page's cursor (or picked), its section and state, how long before the
  note (`checklist::hovered`, called by the menu for the cursor's row: two lines in `vr_menu.cpp`, an accessor at the end
  of `vr_checklist.cpp`, for the merge with `agent/checktest`), and the scenario the checklist's Test last ran:
  `notectx::testRun(scenario)` is the hook; **checktest's Test button should call it** (not wired here: that button is
  on the other branch).
- **The hands:** weapon id and name, model, offsets slot, flags, clip/size, ammo, spent; a carried prop; an enemy held
  (`foegrab::noteHand`: by which part, the holds, the stretch, the two-hand moves); a ragdoll's limb (`box3d::noteRagdollHold`:
  the rig's part, its struggle's weights, effort, fatigue); the force grab's target.
- **The monsters within 5 m:** class, distance, health, think function (its animation state), frame, enemy, an armed
  grunt's weapon, knocked down, dying/corpse, held, headless, its ragdoll's struggle.
- **The settings changed this session** (archived cvars; `cvar.c` calls `VR_NoteCvarChanging` before a change): first
  value -> now, count, when; not a take's playback's own swaps.
- **An instant replay:** with `vr_notes 1`, the motion recorder's row of every host frame (no QC sample) kept in a ring of
  `vr_note_replay_seconds` (30, new cvar; `vr_note_replay 1`, new), the nearby entities every 0.1 s in another; at the note
  both rings go to the pool as they are and are written as `<note>_replay.csv` (a take, label `replay`) and
  `<note>_entities.csv`; the console's last lines (`console.c` -> `VR_NoteConsolePrint`) as `<note>_log.txt`; the frame
  times as `<note>_frames.csv` (hitches marked; the .txt has the summary). A new map starts the rings again.
- The .txt is written on the pool too now; a dropped (too short) note removes its sidecars.
- `transcribe_notes.py` groups each note's context in NOTES.md (Where, Checklist, Hands, Nearby, Settings changed, Files,
  Other: nothing dropped); `--md-only` rebuilds NOTES.md without Whisper.
- Debug > (the commands list) **Save Note Context** (`vr_note_context`: everything but the sound, now) and **Note Replay
  Cost** (`vr_note_replay_stats`).
- `vr_motion.cpp`: the take header's settings lines are built from a copy (`SettingsSnap`), without temporary strings
  (the same text); for a replay on the pool. That took the note start from 4-5 ms to about 1 ms.

**Tests (headless, vrfiringrange).** A shotgun in the main hand (`vr_weapon_grip_mode 1; impulse 9; impulse 154`), a grunt
50 units ahead (`vr_test_spawn 0; impulse 241`), the off hand gripping it (`vr_mock_hand_to off nearest monster_army 6;
+graboff`), a checklist item picked (`vr_menu_press Checklist > ...`, then `vr_checklist undo`), `vr_note_replay_seconds 29`,
then `vr_note_context`: the .txt has `checklist: [next branch: test these first] Blade shape editor ... (open)`, `main hand:
weapon 4 shotgun, model progs/v_shot.mdl, offsets slot 1, flags 0, clip 8/8, ammo 1`, `off enemy: monster_army #266 by its
torso or shoulders, hand's hold 0.85 ...`, `nearby: monster_army #266 at 1.6 m, health 30, think army_stand7, ... held 0.85`,
`setting: vr_note_replay_seconds 30 -> 29`, `setting: vr_weapon_grip_mode 0 -> 1`, the replay 1393 frames 8.4 s (since the map
loaded), the console 149 prints, the frames' summary. Cost (`NOTESTATS`): 3 us a host frame, 1.2 us a server frame; rows
about 2.2 KB (a 30 s ring at 90 Hz about 6 MB; on disk about 2 KB a row, 5.6 MB a note); the note start 1.05 ms.
Replay: `map vrfiringrange; vr_motion_play <note>_replay.csv map vrfiringrange save` played its 1393 frames; against the
take (`scratch/compare_takes.py`, row by row) the head's and both controllers' tracking fed in are identical (max 0.0000 m),
no frame's buttons differ, the hands as the game placed them (player frame) mean 0.25 / 0.03 units off, max 3.1 (main) and
40.9 (off: its grip on the grunt, which the replay doesn't bring back: playback stands only the take's target monster; the
others are in `_entities.csv`). The report's "hands vs the take, relative to the dummy" is large (rms 115 units) for this
take: its nearest monster changes from the training dummy to the spawned grunt halfway, which that measure doesn't follow.
`eval.sh`: runs as before.

**In VR:** record a few notes as usual (with a weapon, holding an enemy, after picking a checklist item, after changing a
setting); check nothing hitches as a note starts; then `python Misc/quakevr/transcribe_notes.py` and look at NOTES.md.

## The fist's blow line; the blade editor's handles at the hand (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/fistblade`, 2026-10-23)

Vittorio: let Edit Blade Shape edit the unarmed case, to move the fist's blow line to match the fists; and (in VR) the tip
handle drags easily but the near end (at or behind the holding hand) does not.

**The fist's line, data-driven** (new cvars, no migration; `vr_cvars.inc`): `vr_melee_fist_from_x/y/z` (0 0 0) and
`vr_melee_fist_to_x/y/z` (4 0 0): the line's two ends in the hand's frame (units along its forward, right, up from the
tracked hand), what strikes between them (the layout's fist, point 0, and knuckles, point 1); `vr_melee_fist_width` (1,
times the swept radius); `vr_melee_fist_mirror` (1: the off hand's right offsets negated, so one set fits both hands). The
near end stays a quarter of the line behind the first end (before: 1 unit behind the hand, a quarter of 4). Shared by the
gloved, bare and ghost hands (QC's fist thing, whatever the model). QC `VR_Melee_Line`'s fist branch builds it (the
defaults' arithmetic is the old code's, bit for bit: `h + fwd * 0`, `h + fwd * 4`, `h + fwd * -1`; the right/up terms only
when one is set) and `VR_Melee_ShapeOf` gives the fist its width; every consumer reads the track (`mh_near/grip/far`,
`mh_bwidth`): punches' hits and sounds, wall punches, shoves' blows, the decapitation and limb checks, the motion recorder.

**The editor with an empty hand** (`vr_bladeedit.cpp`; Weapon Offsets on the empty hand > Posing Mode > Edit Blade Shape,
or `vr_bladeedit main|off`, or Debug > Edit Blade Shape (Main Hand)): a fist session (any hand with QC's WID_FIST, a prop
in it too): handles red Knuckles End, orange Fist End (both lifted out of the fist, tied to their points), blue Width
(beside the line on the inner side). Show Melee Blades forced on as for weapons. Panel: Undo, Reset Line, Mirror On/Off
(the third button), Cancel, Done (no Head Box). It ends (keeping) if a weapon comes into the hand. Done prints
`vr_blade_dump fist` (new; Debug > Print Fist Line): the eight `QVR_CVAR(...)` lines with the values, `//*` changed.

**The handles at the hand (the near end in VR).** The grip itself was not the cause: while the editor runs every button
goes to it before the two-hand grips, holsters and grabs (vr_input.cpp; `client::grabbing` never sees it). The near end
lies on the line behind the holding hand (a gun's or sword's 0.3 of the line: 4 to 10 units, 10-40 cm, into the wrist
and the forearm), and the hand-side curve point next to the hand: the other controller cannot get its grip point within
5 cm of a point inside the holding hand or arm. Now: a handle at or behind the holding hand (the near end always, any
other within 12 cm of the hand; the fist's two ends) is drawn and taken 7 cm out of it (weapons: above the line, square
to it; the fist: along the hand's up), a thin tie down to the point it moves (the drag moves that point by the hand's
motion, so the lift changes nothing in the values). Reach 5 -> 6 cm, the nearest handle taken; the one under the hand
stays its own out to 1.5 reaches unless another is nearer than 0.6 of its distance. The hovered handle glows yellow with
its label, the other hand's dot turns yellow with a thin line to it. `vr_bladeedit_report` prints each handle's lift.

**Tests** (scripts `scratch/fb_edit.sh`, `fb_edit2.sh`; e1m1, mock):
- Defaults: `vr_melee_sweep_test 2` on the empty hand: near -1 0 0, far 4 0 0, points 0 and 4 ahead (the mock hand's
  makevectors noise 1e-5), radius 3; `vr_blade_dump fist`: all eight at their defaults. `eval.sh` twice: 169/177 (the 8
  known failures), no verdict changed; punch damage moved by 0.1 on one take per run (a different take each run, as the
  slashes: the takes' noise).
- `vr_melee_sweep_test 4` (new, QC `VR_Melee_FistLineTest`): a box at the line's knuckles end swept across by the line
  and by the default one: defaults struck by both PASS; `to_x 10`: 6 units off the default line, struck only by the edited
  PASS; `to 4 7 0, from 0 0 2`: 7 off, only the edited PASS; after the editor's drags (3 7 0, width 1.41) PASS.
- Handles with the mock other hand at each grab point, grip, moved, let go: shotgun near end (lifted 2.2 units) hovered,
  taken, 2 back: 0.30 -> 0.44; hand-side curve point (2.3 units ahead, lifted) taken (its curve seeded); tip 14.0 -> 12.0;
  width 1.0 -> 1.2. Fist: Fist End 0 -> -2 / 3 ahead, Knuckles End 4 -> 7 / 2, Width 1.41 / 1.2; the off hand's fist
  edited by the main hand 2 units inward: `to_y -2` (mirrored: inward on both hands); Done printed 3 changed lines;
  Cancel put everything back (0 changed).
- Checklist test scenario: none (agent/checktest is not on next).

**In VR:** with the hand empty, Weapon Offsets > Edit Blade Shape: drag the orange and red dots (above the fist) so the
white line lies along your knuckles, the blue one out to the fist's width; punch a target with Show Melee Blades on; Done
and send the printed lines if they should ship. With a sword and a gun: the orange near end is now a dot above the
forearm tied to the line: check it (and the curve point next to the hand) is easy to take, and the hover highlight.

## The blade's start; the axe's head box (worktree `fastship`, branch `agent/bladeend`, 2026-10-23; vr_cfg_version 197)

Vittorio (note vrstart_2026-10-23_22-34-28, the axe in the main hand): on the axe he can move the tip and the near end
but not "where the line that belongs to the blade ends"; he wants the blade to match the axe; maybe a volume over the
whole axe head instead.

**Which point.** The axe's blow line runs from the hand to its tip, the Muzzle anchor (24.18, -0.10, 27.30): the top
corner of the front bit's edge (vr_axestick.cpp's edge (20.13, 15.81) .. (24.18, 27.30)). Only its striking part
strikes: QC `VR_Melee_Layout`'s first striking point to the tip (the axe's "head" points at 0.75 and 1: a sword's from
0.27, the chainsaw's 0.55, the crowbar's 0.2, a gun's 0.5). That start was a fixed share of whatever line the tip and
near end made: no handle, and not even drawn (the editor drew the whole line alike, its width tube from an arbitrary
0.2). On the default axe it falls 1.2 units off the edge's lower corner; once the tip moves it drifts with it.

**Blade Start** (new keys, `vr_wofs_bl_from_NN` -1 (the kind's), `bl_from_off_NN`, `bl_from_side_NN` 0; no migration):
where the striking part starts, a share of the line, and its point off the line (shares, as the curve's points). The line
runs straight from the hand to it and on to the tip (`blade::fromAt`, added to the curve in `admeleebend`'s slot kinds:
QC `VR_Melee_BendLine` bends with flag 4 too; `vr_melee_curved_blades 0` straightens it with the rest); the layout's
striking points are laid from it to the tip, the handle's points before it squeezed into hand .. start (QC
`VR_Melee_LayoutFrom`, by the track's new `mh_bfrom`; names and parts unchanged). QC sends the first striking point with
Show Melee Blades (`meleeshow` 1's second vector, `meleeshow::lastStrikeFrom`), so the editor shows the kind's start.
Editor: a purple "Blade Start" handle (index 10: `bladehandle 10`) at that point, shown 3.5 cm out of the blade's flat on
the eyes' side (it lies in the axe head) with a tie; dragging it sets all three keys; the line before it is drawn thin
and grey, the striking part bold with the width tube; Straighten puts it back on the line; the panel's text names it;
`vr_bladeedit_report` prints `from`, the head and the model's head box.

**Head Box On seeds round the drawn head** (`modelHead`): the drawn model's first-pose vertices past 0.3 of the line (or
0.25 before the blade start), the box's near end at the lowest vertex 0.15 shares off the line; a slot's stored corners
come first. **The axe's head box is opt-in** (the author): slot 0 keeps `bl_head 0` but ships the corners 0.5 -1.1077
-0.0919 .. 1.2303 0.1013 0.0701 (both bits, as the seed gives it), so Head Box On starts from them; on, its volume
strikes as the head (`VR_Melee_Ribs`), as the mace's. The crowbar: no box (a bar; its striking points cover it).

**Tests** (`scratch/be_test.txt`, `be_test3.txt`, `be_probe4.txt`; vrtesthall, scenario `blade_editor_axe`; the mock
needs `vr_weapon_grip_mode 1` and the grip held, else the given axe goes to the hip holster):
- Defaults: the axe's `vr_melee_sweep_test 2` on origin/next and here: near, far and every point the same to 1e-4 (only
  the head line is new). `eval.sh`: 169/177, no verdict changed; the axe's takes as the baseline. With the head box on by
  default (an earlier try) 16 moved: the axe's slashes 19.8 -> 49.5, 21.3 -> 35.4, 36.7 -> 49.5, a backswing 39.6 ->
  14.6 with its decapitation yes -> no (the box met the dummy earlier); hence opt-in. Left: 0.1 noise on punches and a
  stab, and a sword slash (12-34-13, "the tip") 18.2 -> 21.6, the same in both runs (not the axe; the baseline's drift).
- Config 197 (`vr_migrate_config` at 196): metal 1.5 / stone 1.5 -> 1 / 0.75; metal 2.2 stays 2.2; at 197, 1.5 stays.
  `vr_scenario validate`: SCNOK blade_editor_axe; SCNSUM 48 files, 0 with errors, 0 missing tags. Head Box On on the axe
  seeds 0.5 -1.1077 -0.0919 .. 1.2303 0.1013 0.0701.
- Handles with the mock other hand at each grab point (hovered, grip, moved, let go), the axe: tip 2 along -> line 8.55

- `vr_melee_sweep_test 3` with that start: a box just outside the bend struck by the edited line, missed by the default

## Fuel tanks: the burst's field, no blood, the pickup's flight, armed monsters' back tanks (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/tanks2`, 2026-10-23)

His notes (vrfiringrange_2026-10-23_21-23-16, 21-24-32, 21-25-15, 21-25-53). New cvars only (no vr_cfg_version change).

- **The hiss that never stopped**: the burst played `pyro_flameon.wav` / `fum_poisonon.wav` (AD's loops: a stream's
  "on", stopped by its "off" on the same channel) on CHAN_AUTO of the tank, which then went: nothing could stop them.

  are never set on fire.

  the ground under it, for `vr_adgun_tank_field_time` (6 s) x (0.4 + 0.6 x the fuel's share), reach
  `vr_adgun_tank_field_radius` (96) x the same. Every 0.5 s what is in its circle (its box within 48 units of the
  ground for fire, 72 for the cloud), in sight of its middle: the flamethrower's sets it on fire (VR_Burn_Ignite, the
  burst's burning time: monsters, players, corpses, crates) and deals the living `vr_burn_damage` a second x
  `vr_adgun_tank_field_damage` (1) on top; the sprayer's poisons it (the burst's 8/s x the damage scale, for its time).
  Another tank in the flames bursts (a chain). Look: AD flame tongues licking up off the floor through the circle, or
  green poison and puffs (not through walls, not past ledges); sound: `ambience/fire1.wav` or AD's
  `traps/steam_loop.wav`. Both fade over its second half (the loop's volume in four steps). The one who burst it is

  frame (where, which way up); a fuelled gun newly in a hand (not from a holster nor the other hand) takes the nearest
  tank of its kind within 1.6 m drawn within the last 0.3 s, which flies to the back over `vr_adgun_tank_pickup_time`

  slime `_blue` 0.14 -> 0.16, `_breathe` 0.25 -> 0.7, `_breathe_speed` 0.6 -> 3.4, `_frequency` 1.5 -> 1.6, `_green`

  `vr_water_foam_particle_shore`, `vr_lava_foam_particle_shore`, `vr_slime_foam_particle_shore` (0; -4..16 units).

  frame data's `Foam[i].w`, unused before): in `LiquidFoam` the shore distance is pulled back by up to that many units
  by a slow two-octave world noise drifting along the shore (more where the swells push in), the foam follows the new
  line and the liquid's output alpha is times `LiquidEdge` (see-through past it, a soft 1-unit edge, wider far off),

  `LiquidDisplace` also raises the swells' mesh's rim vertices by up to 0.6x the edge (fading out 12 units in; only up,
  no gap opens): the waterline climbs the wall in curves. The mesh's 16-unit cells make those curves gentle polylines.

## Armed monsters: the physical tug, frozen after a disarm, weapons on the hands, parries, pickups (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/agfix3`, 2026-10-23)

Vittorio's notes (vrfiringrange 2026-10-23 21:07:48, 21:09:18, 21:09:44, 21:10:08, 21:14:15).

**1. The physical tug** (`vr_agrunt_tug_ragdoll 1`, Armed Grunts page "Tug: Physical"). A full grab of a calm armed
monster's weapon (not shaky, not from behind: those still give it at once) makes it an active ragdoll standing its
ground: a stagger begun sure-footed, steady, not carried (`ragdollstagger(g, away from you, 0, 1, 0, cap + 2, TRUE)`),
up again only when the tug ends (vr_knockdown.qc keeps a tug's stagger past `VR_KD_STAGGER_MOST`). Your hand holds the
limb nearest the weapon's grip (its forearm) where your hand is: the weapon's lever (engine `tugRagdoll`,
vr_box3d_ragparts.cpp: a ragdoll grab's motor joint without the palm fit, `RagdollGrab.tug`: the QC's hand holds nothing,
so the held-field check never lets it go; at most 3x the break force, 6000 N). The weapon is drawn riding that limb
(`VR_AG_RagProp`), so hand, weapon and its hand form one chain: the hold's constraint force
(`b3Joint_GetConstraintForce`) is the force between its hand and the weapon. Its arms (`ragactive::Stagger.tug`): the
holding arm pulls its hand in low before its chest, the other hand reaches for the same hand; no wheeling; its pelvis's
pin times 1 + its pull. Its grip breaks at `vr_agrunt_tug_break_force` (900 N: a sharp yank) or at
`vr_agrunt_tug_break_impulse` (350 N s of force x time counted above a tenth of the break force, eased off at half the
need a second: a steady far pull), both times its health share (at least 0.35), half in pain; badly hurt or gone down:
at once. Broken: the weapon is put in your hand (`VR_AG_Yank` now moves it to the hand first: a tug left it a little
behind), it stumbles `VR_AG_TUG_STAGGER` (0.35 s) as a ragdoll and is handed back to its AI unarmed. Let go first (or
`vr_agrunt_tug_hold_max`, 6 s: it wrenches free): up again in 0.2 s, it keeps it. Haptics every 0.1 s, stronger with the
pull's share of the break (and jerks). Sliders: Tug: Physical, Break Force, Break Impulse, Its Pull
(`vr_agrunt_tug_strength` 1.5), Longest. No per-kind table rows (the enforcer's body resists as its ragdoll does). The
builtin: `ragdolltug` (QC wrapper over `ragdollgrab`'s optional `tug` argument: the builtins' table is full).
Measured (test 31, a grunt): held still 13-40 N; drawn back 0.1 m/s to 0.4 m: 30-50 N for the first 20 cm (its body
leans and follows), about 280 N at 35-40 cm; a yank at 0.6 m/s tears it out at 950 N after 0.29 s (17 cm).

**2. Frozen after a disarm.** Cause: a tug's `vr_ag_tug_pl` left set when its weapon left by another way (a blow on its
hand or on the weapon, a throw, a parry, its death) while the old tug was on: `VR_AG_Run` sent it to `vr_ag_tughold` every
frame, which, with no weapon, set `think` to its run without a `nextthink`: standing, doing nothing. Fix: `VR_AG_DropHeld`
ends a tug first (lost), the prop's removal ends it, `vr_ag_tughold`/`VR_AG_TugResume` end a tug with no weapon and go on
running. Test 33: every path (the physical tug, a hand blow, a weapon blow, a throw, a parry, a fall, and the old tug
then a hand blow) then fights or goes for a weapon within 2 s: 7 PASS (0.10 .. 1.18 s).

**3. Weapons on the hands.** A guard's or a hit reaction's turns (client kicks on the arms after the arms' IK) moved the
hands off the weapon drawn at the IK target. `relinkArms` now poses the kicks as drawn (`boneKicks` on the lerped keys)
and carries each weapon by its forearm's kick (both hands). A ragdoll (a stagger, a tug, a fall, a struggle): the server
no longer leaves the weapon where it was: `VR_AG_PlaceProp` rides it on the limb nearest its grip as it was posed when
the ragdoll began (`ragdollpoint` there and back; the prop's posed forward and up kept: `.vr_ag_pfw`, `.vr_ag_pup`), and the
client leaves a ragdoll's weapon to the server. Death: it drops (unchanged). Eyeshots: `vr_agrunt_test 14` with
`scratch5 1` (each guards its head from you), test 31 with `scratch1 1` (unbreakable) for the standing tug.

**4. Parries.** Cause: their blows are your weapons' own code (`VR_AGP_Strike`), which deals damage through
`T_Damage_VRMelee` and `T_DamageImpl`, never `T_Damage`'s `VR_Parry`. Fix: `T_Damage_VRMelee` runs `VR_Parry` for an
armed monster's blow on a player (windows, cooldown, stamina, its stagger, sounds, haptics, the disarm chance), and the
parry's hand test runs with `self` the player (`VR_Parry_HandFor`: during its blow `self` is the monster with its own
hand fields). Test 35: each melee weapon and fists against the crowbar held across (TESTING.md's parry pose).

**5. Pickups reach down** (note 21:14:15). Its take frames from the row (`vr_am_f_take`): the grunt's now painc4..7 (a
crouch: its top 28, 24, 17, 15 units; load1..4 stood upright), the enforcer's paind5..8 (a knee) as before. The weapon is
its own from the first take frame but drawn where it lay (`VR_AG_TakeBegin`: `.vr_ag_took_*`), its hand's IK reaching down
to it; its hand closes at the third frame (`vr_ag_took_grab`, by time: `VR_AG_TakeGrab` counts it, the sound), then it is
carried up to its hold over `VR_AG_LIFT_TIME` (0.3 s, eased; both hands for a second weapon). Cut short before its hand
closes (a pain, a shove, anything but its take frames or its run): dropped where it lay. Test 34: it lay still until the
hand closed (moved 0.0 units), carried up over 0.49 s, 1 pickup PASS; hit as it reaches: untaken, lying PASS.

**Tests** (vrtesthall, `vr_mock_hand main 0.1 0.72 -1.2 65 0 0`, `+grabmain`): 31 the tug pulled (yank, and a slow pull
with `scratch2 0.25; scratch3 0.12`): begun standing, holds still, torn out, up in 0.4 s, then fights: PASS; 32 let go:
keeps it, up, fights PASS; 33 paths 7 PASS; 34 pickup 2 PASS; 35 parries (with `vr_weapon_grip_mode 1; impulse 167;
vr_mock_hand main 0.15 1.35 -0.35 0 90 0`). 21/22 (the old tug) set `vr_agrunt_tug_ragdoll 0` themselves. The mock:
`vr_mock_hand_pull` (m, the main hand drawn back). Scenarios: `agrunt_tug`, `agrunt_parry`, `agrunt_pickup`,
`agrunt_guard`.

## Save My Settings as Defaults; the dropped toolgun's own loot beam (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/savedefaults`, 2026-10-23)

**Proposing defaults.** A developer-only way for the author to hand his tweaks to the coordinator without anything in
the game changing (vr_propose_defaults.hpp/.cpp). `vr_propose_defaults`, *Debug > Save My Settings as Defaults* and a
new corner button *Save Default* (vr_menuui.cpp `ToolSaveDefaults`, between Toolgun and Checklist; shown only at Menu
Detail: Developer, as those two) write every cvar whose value differs from its shipped default (`default_string`, which
`vr_default` in `vr_defaults.cfg` replaces; numbers compared as numbers; read-only cvars skipped) to
`quakevr/proposed_defaults/<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS>.cfg` (`_2`... for two in a second; git-ignored). The button's first
press arms it ("Press again" on the button for 3 s, a console line), the second writes; the button then says
"Saved N" (or "Not saved") for 5 s and the console prints `Saved N settings for review: <path>`.

The file: a header, then sections `// == <area> ==` sorted by area: the menu pages first (the path of the setting's
nearest row, from Search's index: `menu::forEachSettingPath`, every page under VR Settings and Advanced VR Options
whatever Menu Detail shows), then `Weapon slot NN (<model>)` for `vr_wofs_*_NN`, `Held object slot NN (<model>)` for
`vr_prop_*_NN`, then `Not in the menus: <prefix>_*` (the name up to its second underscore for `vr_`, its first
otherwise). One line a setting: `name "value" // default "old", <menu row path | its weapon's tuning pages | not in
the menus>, archived|not archived[, personal?|debug?]`. Everything is written; the tags are name heuristics for
filtering: `debug?` (debug, test, show, dump, profile, trace, mock, dryrun, developer, verbose, `_log`), else
`personal?` (calib, bodycal, handcal, comfort, height, handed, seated, floor_offset, gunangle/gunyaw, offhandpitch/yaw,
dominant, body_tweak/arm/elbow/shoulder/forearm/wrist/eye/torso, xr_runtime, `_version`, tips_seen, tutorial,
note_device, vr_motion_, vr_menu_, vignette, snapturn). Decision: "hand" alone is not a personal tag (it would catch
every hand gameplay setting); handedness and the hand-angle calibration are.

Tested headless: with `vr_menu_level 1` the button is not there (`vr_mock_laser savedefaults` + two trigger clicks: no
press, no file); at 2 the first click printed the "press again" line, the second `Saved 40 settings for review`. The
file had `vr_lootbeam_opacity "0.4" // default "0.15", Advanced VR Options > Graphics > Loot Beams > Opacity, archived`,
`vr_wofs_2h_dispmd_05` under `Weapon slot 05 (progs/v_nail2.mdl)`, `vr_prop_mass_01` under `Held object slot 01
(maps/b_explob.bsp)`, `vr_gunangle ... personal?`, `vr_lootbeam_debug ... not archived, debug?`.

**The toolgun's loot beam** (his note vrfiringrange_2026-10-23_21-18-02: dropped toolguns are hard to find among many
weapons). A weapon prop drawn as `progs/v_toolgun.mdl` gets `vr_lootbeam_hue_toolgun` (305, magenta) and a beam

## Armed monsters: weapons on their hands every frame, the chainsaw parried (worktree `goreflesh`, branch `agent/agdual2`, 2026-10-24)

Note vrtesthall 2026-10-23 22:46:49 (two axes: the left weapon left behind by its hand in some animations; melee swings
where the hand and the weapon part). Brief items 2, 3 and 5 done; 1 (dual guns) and 4 (body in the strikes) not started
(budget).

**Why the weapons left the hands.** The weapon is drawn at the server's target and the arm's IK was meant to bring the
hand there, but the hand drawn was not the hand the IK moved:
- The rig's fit put the grunt's **left hand on its upper arm** (vertBone: the 13 vertices about the left forearm's end are
  bone 3, upperarm_l): bending the elbow moved the forearm to the weapon and left the hand with the upper arm.
- The **right hand's** vertices (its row's 32 26 31, the old rifle grip, and those about its forearm's end) fit their bone
  so badly that the shader gives them 0-0.39 of its turns (the swing share, mean 0.13): the hand stayed mostly where the
  animation had it.
- Model Animation (r_lerpmodels 3: spline, swings, rebuild) draws the hand off the frames' lerp the IK aimed.
- In some poses (the grunt's painc and painb crouches, the take frames) the rig's forearm is 10-35 units off its hand.
- Swings and bent bodies put targets past the arm's reach.

**Fixes** (vr_hitreact.cpp, vr_animsmooth.cpp; all for the armed rigs' models only):
- `vr_agrunt_ik_hands` (4 units): an armed model's vertices within that of a forearm's end (its first frame) are drawn
  wholly on that forearm (rest data: bone, full share, not rebuilt). Read when the model's rest data is made (a map load).
- `vr_agrunt_ik_drawn` (1): kickInstance works out each hand as the shader will draw it (`hitreact::HandFit`: drawn D + W
  K(P), the spline's poses and rows, each vertex's share) and the IK aims K(P) at (target - D) / W: the drawn hand lands on
  the target exactly.
- `vr_agrunt_ik_reach` (0.96): targets (and the weapons drawn there) within that share of the arm's length from its
  shoulder as posed.
- `vr_agrunt_ik_misfit` (3 units): where the rig's forearm misplaces the hand by more than that (per pose, found once a
  model), the target eases to the animation's hand (wholly at twice it): the weapon rides the hand as drawn.

**Measured** (`vr_agrunt_test 41`, `vr_agrunt_test_kind` the kind; new: `vr_agrunt_ik_tag`, `vr_agrunt_ik_err`): an axe in
each hand, AI held, side on: A every frame of the model held 0.15 s, B every swing kind by the right, the left and both
hands (eighths), C one axe in both hands, every swing. The engine counts each drawn frame's hands (the vertices about the
forearms' ends, as the shader draws them, turns included) against their weapons' drawn origins. r_lerpmodels 3, units:

| | before right / left (max) | after right / left (max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grunt, frames | 18.2 / 40.2 (pains 41-43, reload 31-34) | 1.2 / 0.8 |
| grunt, dual swings | 17.8 / 18.1 | 0.00 / 0.00 |
| grunt, two-handed swings (right) | 17.9 | 0.00 |
| enforcer, frames | 9.5 / 36.0 | 2.8 / 0.0 |
| enforcer, dual swings | 11.2 / 21.2 | 0.00 / 0.00 |
| enforcer, two-handed swings | 11.1 | 0.00 |

Before = `vr_agrunt_ik_drawn 0; vr_agrunt_ik_reach 0; vr_agrunt_ik_hands 0; vr_agrunt_ik_misfit 0` (set before the map).
Death frames are left out (no IK: the weapons drop). `scratch1 N` holds tag N (an eyeshot): `scratch/hands_before.png`,
`scratch/hands_after.png` (frame 62 and swing tag 267; the grunt is close and low in the shot: the numbers are the check).

**Parries (item 5).** On next test 35 already parried every blow but the chainsaw's (agfix3's last commit, the grunt spawned
ahead of the head, was the fix for the "parry: none" lines): the chain's ticks went through `VR_Chainsaw_Cut`'s own
`T_DamageImpl`. Now an armed monster's tick on a player runs `VR_Parry` first. Test 35, grunt and enforcer: axe, sword,

eval.sh: 0 verdict changes (3 takes' damage within 3.4, the ragdoll's pose noise).

Scenario `agrunt_weapon_hands` (vrtesthall, god, notarget: armed grunts with an axe, a sword, fists and an armed enforcer's
axe, 260 units off): validate OK, runall OK.

**Left:** item 1 (dual-wielded two-handed guns, the spread and kick penalties and their slider, the "big" weapon flag,

## The melee eval's crash in `vertsOf`: a monster placed before the update, drawn as its ragdoll after (worktree `gorefx`, branch `agent/vertsof`, 2026-10-24)

**Cause.** `posed` (Quake/vr/vr_modelcollide.cpp) cached an entity's placement per entity number for the whole host
frame. Since `agent/meleeworld` (f3b9bcce7, `vr_melee_world_pass`) `strikeTarget` places monsters from the hands'
update, before the frame's server update; the view's `test` then reused that placement after the update. On
vrmelee-recording the dummy soldier dies in that update and its slot now draws `progs/soldier.mdl#rag` (a skinned
alias model: `quakeAlias` gives no header), while the cached placement still said "soldier.mdl, alias", so `vertsOf`
read the vertices through a null header (seen with a temporary print: ent 8, soldier.mdl to soldier.mdl#rag, 3 times
in the full set). Another alias model in the slot (a gib head) would have read past its vertices instead.

**Fix.** A placement is reused only while the entity, its model, its `msgtime` and `cl.time` are the ones it was made
from; otherwise it is made again (the ragdoll then takes the ragdoll path, as before f3b9bcce7). `vertsOf` uses the
alias header the placement was made from instead of looking it up again from the entity's model now;
`drawnTriangles` skips a triangle whose corner is past the vertices (as `gather` already did).

**Tests.** `eval.sh` before: canary 26/34 and full 127/133, 2 copies crashed in each (11 and 44 takes unjudged).
After: canary 37/45, full 169/177, no copy crashed; no verdict changes against the baseline (only PASS -> PASS drifts
of 0.1 in a hit's numbers, which differ run to run; slash_horizontal_ltr's as before).

### Armed grunts: shooting the weapon out (worktree `tghost`, branch `agent/shootdisarm`, 2026-10-24)

A new way to disarm an armed monster: shoot its weapon, or the hand holding it, precisely. QC
`vr_armedgrunt_shot.qc` (hooks in `vr_armedgrunt_shot_defs.qc`; ARMED_MONSTERS.md, "Shooting the weapon out").

- **What is hit.** A player's pellet (its traced path up to where it stopped), lightning bolt, or nail, rocket or grenade
  (its flight each frame, a frame back and a frame ahead; the grunt's own model in the way first: not counted) meeting a
  held weapon (its line from 8 units behind the grip to the muzzle, 3 units round) or the hand holding it (the grip to
  11 units towards its shoulder, 3.5 round). The first met along the path counts. `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_size` scales
  both volumes; a path within `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_near` units beyond them counts at half; `_parts` 0 the weapon only,
  1 the hand only, 2 either. Each held weapon (dual wielding: each hand's) counts on its own.
- **What counts.** The shot's damage (a pellet 4, a nail 9, a super nail 18, a bolt 30, a rocket's direct hit ~110; not
  the positional factor) times its kind's weight (`_w_pellet` 1, `_w_nail` 1, `_w_lightning` 0.3, `_w_blast` 1,
  `_w_splash` 0: explosions never count unless raised) and the part's (`_weapon_w` 1, `_hand_w` 1).
- **The roll.** Hits add up over `_window` (0.5 s) from the first. Reaching `_damage` (16) it rolls once (the next frame,
  so a blast's pellets all count first) at `_chance` (0.25) plus `_chance_scale` (0.8) for each threshold past it (at most
  0.95), and starts over; a failed roll: nothing adds up for `_cooldown` (0.3 s). Won: the weapon flies off along the
  shots (VR_AG_Disarm: its clatter and grunt), sparks and a ricochet. Every weapon hit sparks a little.
- **The shots themselves.** A hand hit hurts the grunt as ever (it is its body). A pellet on the weapon goes on into the
  body behind, or with `_absorb` 1 (off by default: today's damage unchanged) stops there: no damage (the test: 29 health
  lost a 2 m blast passing through, 0 absorbed). While `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm` is on, a player's shot no longer disarms by
  the old blow rule (`vr_agrunt_disarm_damage` near the gun hand, which disarmed a shotgun blast or a super nail near the
  hand every time); melee blows, throws, parries and rockets' direct hits keep theirs.
- **Settings:** VR Settings > Armed Grunts > "Disarming: Shooting It Out" (all of the above). **Debug:** Debug > Show
  Shot Disarms (`vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_debug` 1: `shotdisarm:` each player's shot on an armed grunt, its part weapon,
  hand or body, the damage adding up, each roll's chance and result; 2: also each weapon's line and hand as sparks).
  Debug > Tests: "Armed Grunts: Shooting Weapons Out".
- **Defaults, why.** 16 is between a single nail (9: never alone) and two (18); a shotgun's six pellets all on the gun are
  24 (1.5 thresholds: 0.65), the super shotgun's ~13 on it 0.95: rewarding at close range, a gamble from afar, never a
  single chip shot. Lightning at 0.3: a roll every 0.4 s held on the gun (~35% each), not a sure thing at 0.2 s.

Measured (`vr_agrunt_test 50`, vrtesthall, fresh shotgun grunts, the player's own pellets/nails/bolts aimed at the
gun's middle; 100 trials a case, 40 for the modes): shotgun on the gun 2 m 0.60, 5 m 0.52, 15 m 0.18 (3.3 pellets on
it); super shotgun 2 m 0.96; 3 nails in 0.4 s at 5 m 0.36; one nail at 10 m 0, one pellet at 10 m 0; lightning 0.2 s
at 5 m 0.33; shotgun on the forearm 2 m 0.60 (6 hand hits); hand only: on the muzzle end 0, on the forearm 0.62;
weapon only, on the forearm 0; size 0.5 at 15 m 0 (1.2 hits), size 2 at 15 m 0.68 (6 hits); absorb 0.60 (6 pellets
stopped, 0 damage); dual (a sword and a crowbar), the left crowbar shot: 0.65, the right one never lost. 10/10 PASS.
eval.sh unchanged (26/34 canary, 127/133 full, pass for pass). Scene `agrunt_shootout` (grunts at 2, 5, 10, 15 m,
a shotgun and a nailgun given, the debug prints on).

Open: AD's projectile pellets (`vr_ad_projectiles`) and AD's own bolts/lightning don't count yet (their own touch
functions); the hand's forearm direction is guessed (grip towards the shoulder), not read from the drawn arm.

**In VR:** run the `agrunt_shootout` scene. Shoot the nearest grunt's gun point-blank with the shotgun a few times:
it should fly out of its hand about two times in three, along your shot, with sparks and a ricochet; from the far
ones it should hold on mostly. A quick nail burst on a gun: sometimes. Shoot its gun hand and forearm: the same,
and it bleeds. With Show Shot Disarms on, the printed part (weapon/hand/body) should match where you aimed; in Print
and Volumes, the sparks should sit on the gun and the forearm: if the forearm line points the wrong way, say so.

baseline back afterwards) and run `vr_propose_defaults` (or take his own Save Defaults file), then `python

each slot's QVR_WEAPON_DEFAULT lines and the OldValue rows of the next wofs step. A slot's tip goes only for a melee
weapon (Quake VR's own, or an ID ending `#melee`); a gun's tip change is printed to stderr as not shipped. `--skip NN`
leaves a slot out (a stale value, as the axe's here). Then bump the config version and `settingsVersion`, add the step,
build, and run the checks below.
